#42. JPMorgan Expands JPM Coin to Ethereum Mainnet

Home » Blitz news » JPMorgan Expands JPM Coin to Ethereum Mainnet

JPMorgan brings USD deposit tokens to Ethereum, widening 24/7 on-chain institutional settlement.

JPMorgan has brought its US dollar-denominated deposit token, JPM Coin (JPMD), to the Ethereum mainnet, the bank announced on October 19. The expansion widens the blockchain payment infrastructure available to institutional clients and opens them another public network for on-chain dollar transfers.

JPMorgan already operates JPM Coin, a tokenized deposit product built on its Kinexys blockchain infrastructure.

The latest move allows JPM Coin to support peer-to-peer transfers across the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) ecosystem, including Ethereum and Base. The token was initially launched on Base in November 2025.

According to an official announcement, the USD-denominated deposit token (JPMD) expands the bank’s payment infrastructure for institutional clients, letting eligible accounts transfer money directly on a public blockchain.

Unlike conventional cryptocurrencies or privately issued stablecoins, JPM Coin is tied to funds held within JPMorgan’s banking infrastructure. It is designed for onchain payments and settlement within the bank’s existing deposit framework, and it is intended for institutional use rather than public retail trading.

The launch builds on JPMorgan’s wider push to bring traditional financial instruments onto public blockchains. The bank launched its first tokenized money market fund on Ethereum in December 2025, followed by a second in May 2026, according to The Block.

Kinexys, the bank’s blockchain and digital payments business, has processed more than $4 trillion in cumulative transactions, with average daily volume reaching $7 billion, the bank said.

A major US bank extending a deposit token to Ethereum mainnet signals growing institutional reliance on public blockchains for 24/7 settlement. It adds substantial liquidity and activity to the tokenized-asset infrastructure already taking shape across Ethereum and Layer-2 networks.

#44. Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson is building a new programming language for the network

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson is writing a new programming language for his blockchain. He says it will be the first to combine what a user wants a transaction to do with cryptographic proof that the rules were followed.

“I’m actually personally developing a programming language for Cardano,” Hoskinson wrote on X on Sunday, adding that he’s working on it with Lucas Rosa, a software engineer at Input Output Global who co-created Aiken, one of Cardano’s main smart contract languages.

That’s not something most founders do once their network is this big. Hoskinson runs a company full of engineers and is still choosing to write the tool future Cardano apps could be built on himself.

The language would support three tools: transaction intents, proof-carrying data and Groth16 proofs.

An intent lets a user say what they want done and leave the steps to the app. A trader could ask to swap one token for another only if the final price meets set conditions, without spelling out how to get there.

Proof-carrying data attaches cryptographic evidence to a piece of information, showing it follows certain rules. Another app can check that evidence without redoing every calculation behind it.

Groth16 is a widely used proof system that produces tiny proofs computers can check quickly. Those proofs can show a condition was met without revealing the private data used to meet it.

Together, they could let developers build apps that coordinate trades, check complicated conditions, and pass verified information between services, with Cardano checking a small proof at the end.

Cardano developers already write smart contracts in Plutus, which is built on the programming language Haskell, and in Aiken. Midnight, the privacy-focused blockchain built by Hoskinson’s company Input Output Global, has its own language, Compact, for apps that handle confidential data.

Meanwhile, Hoskinson hasn’t shared the new language’s name, any public code, or a date when developers can start using it.

Mesh will connect crypto and stablecoin wallets to Visa’s global payment network, allowing users to spend digital assets without a separate card.

Visa and crypto payments network Mesh have partnered to allow consumers to spend cryptocurrency and stablecoin balances directly from digital wallets at merchants across Visa’s global payment network.

In a statement shared with The Block, the company said the Nevada Financial Institutions Division had authorized it to provide custody services. Its clients include fiduciaries, public companies, trusts, and high-net-worth individuals requiring qualified bitcoin custody.

AnchorWatch Trust Company offers two custody options. Under its flagship model, ATC holds the keys required for qualified custody, while clients, trustees, or executives can hold additional keys. The other model distributes key control among ATC, BitGo in the U.S., and CoinCorner in the Isle of Man, according to the statement.

The company said it charges fixed-dollar fees based on vault size rather than a percentage of assets under custody. Once a client's monthly fee reaches $10,000, additional bitcoin purchases or an increase in the value of existing holdings will not raise the custody charge, it added.

AnchorWatch also offers optional insurance backed by A+ rated Lloyd's of London syndicates. The company said it has authority to write policies with limits of up to $370 million per ATC client, subject to underwriting approval, with policies issued in the customer's or entity's name.

The insurance can cover losses arising from several risks, including violent coercion and kidnapping. It can also cover fraudulent conduct by AnchorWatch resulting in a bitcoin loss, subject to underwriting approval, policy limits, and other terms, the company said.

Today, the Solana network recorded a historic high: the number of addresses holding tokenized stocks soared to 1.4 million, according to Blockworks data. 1.4 million addresses now hold stocks on Solana https://t.co/0WF8QZfsjz

Back in June, the number of stockholders on Solana barely exceeded 500,000, but a powerful influx of users in recent weeks has made the blockchain the absolute leader in the RWA category. The reason for the boom is simple: round-the-clock access. Traditional Wall Street closes on Friday evening, but on the blockchain trading goes on nonstop: up to 65% of tokenized stock trading volume is now conducted outside the standard working hours of U.S. exchanges.

People are massively using digital versions of Nvidia (NVDAx), Apple, and Tesla shares, as well as stakes in SpaceX, as collateral in DeFi protocols, forcing classic securities to play by the aggressive rules of the crypto market.

Despite the impressive figure of 1.4 million wallets, the real financial weight of this retail segment is still modest. Capital within Solana is distributed unevenly:

Stablecoins: the network's main safe, holding $14.6 billion.

U.S. Treasuries: a reliable instrument worth $1.5 billion.

Tokenized stocks: a modest $485.2 million.

In the global ranking of tokenized stock platforms (the entire market is valued at $3.42 billion), the bStocks platform ($1.2 billion, BNB Chain) leads, while the xStocks project, two-thirds of whose liquidity is tied to Solana, takes third place with a volume of $582 million.

At the same time, Solana's main challenge now lies in the operational plane. Serving 1.4 million active addresses is demanding: the real stress test for the infrastructure will be the first mass processing of corporate actions (dividend payments, splits, and shareholder votes), which require hundreds of thousands of simultaneous transactions.

Issuers are trying to solve the problem with the new regulated Token-2022 standard, but only the first large payouts will show the real resilience of this solution.

While the RWA sector celebrates its victory, the network's native token has ignored this triumph: the price of SOL remains squeezed in a $100–$107 corridor due to capital outflows from spot ETFs. It seems that while the ecosystem is building the rails of the finance of the future, exchange speculators simply haven't noticed.

#51. Mastercard Brings Its Fraud-Fighting Tools to Stablecoin Payments

Mastercard Brings Its Fraud-Fighting Tools to Stablecoin Payments

Mastercard is extending its fraud-fighting playbook to stablecoins, launching a tool that lets financial institutions scan dollar-pegged token payments for fraud, scams, and sanctions exposure before the money ever moves on-chain.

Unveiled Monday at the Money20/20 conference in Las Vegas, the product, called Stablecoin Security, combines Mastercard’s payment intelligence with blockchain analytics to assess risk across the full life of a transaction, from the moment a payment is initiated through its movement on a public ledger.

The company launched it with two initial program participants, Borderless.xyz and Keyrails, both alumni of its Start Path blockchain accelerator.

The pitch addresses a growing blind spot as stablecoins move into cross-border and business-to-business payments. Mastercard cited a Bank for International Settlements study of 593 million stablecoin transfers in 2025 that found nearly 60% were complex, multi-step transactions rather than simple one-to-one payments, making it harder for institutions to gauge risk across the whole journey.

Delivered through a platform-agnostic API, the tool analyzes signals like where funds originated, exposure to restricted parties and scam indicators, generating a risk score before a payment settles that slots into existing compliance and fraud workflows.

“Stablecoins are creating new possibilities for value exchange, but financial institutions need the right intelligence and controls to participate with confidence,” said Ann Johnson, Mastercard’s executive vice president of security solutions, framing the tool as an extension of the company’s fraud capabilities into digital assets.

The launch is the latest sign of Mastercard weaving stablecoins into its core business. The company recently rolled out a Global Money Platform with BVNK, the stablecoin infrastructure firm it acquired in August, letting businesses hold and move fiat and stablecoins through a single connection.

It has also secured a New York BitLicense covering stablecoins and tokenized deposits, moved to enable AI-agent payments alongside Coinbase and Ripple, and expanded stablecoin settlement to include Circle’s USDC and Ripple’s RLUSD.

Mastercard said Stablecoin Security builds on existing tools like Crypto Credential and Crypto Secure, and that it plans to extend the product’s reach in 2027, including through BVNK. The solution is launching first in North America, with worldwide availability expected next year.

#53. Deflationary Tokenomics 101: How Buyback-and-Burn Models Work

Home » Op-ed » Deflationary Tokenomics 101: How Buyback-and-Burn Models Work

Explore how buybacks, token burns, and revenue-driven demand shape deflationary crypto models.

“Deflationary” is one of crypto’s favorite buzzwords. A project announces a fixed supply, adds a burn mechanism, and the assumption is that fewer tokens must eventually mean a higher price.

Tokenomics aren’t that simple. Buybacks and burns reduce supply or create recurring demand for a token, but the details determine whether those mechanisms are economically meaningful. How many tokens can be created? Where does the money for buybacks come from? What triggers a burn? And, crucially, is there actual activity generating the money that keeps the system running?

Start with supply. A fixed maximum supply simply means a token cannot exceed a predetermined number. It does not necessarily mean circulating supply is shrinking. If 100 million tokens are trading today but another 500 million remain scheduled to unlock, circulating supply can continue growing even with a fixed cap.

A burn goes further because tokens are permanently removed from supply, usually by sending them to an inaccessible address or destroying them through a smart contract. If burns exceed new issuance and unlocks over a given period, supply genuinely contracts.

BNB is one of the longest-running examples. Its Auto-Burn mechanism uses a formula based on BNB’s price and blockchain activity, with the long-term goal of reducing supply to 100 million BNB. BNB Chain also burns a portion of gas fees in real time. The point is that the burn follows defined rules rather than simply relying on occasional discretionary announcements.

Then there are buyback-and-burn models. A buyback means tokens are purchased from the open market. Those tokens can then be burned, held in a treasury or used elsewhere. Buying alone does not make a token deflationary; permanently removing the purchased tokens does.

PancakeSwap provides an example of product activity feeding this process. Its current CAKE tokenomics model has a 400 million hard cap and targets annual deflation of at least roughly 4%. Portions of fees generated by products including spot trading, perpetuals, prediction markets and lotteries contribute to CAKE buybacks and burns. In its August 2026 burn report, PancakeSwap recorded its 36th consecutive month of net CAKE supply reduction.

Hyperliquid takes another route. Trading fees directed to its Assistance Fund are automatically converted into HYPE as part of the network’s execution, and the HYPE accumulated there is burned, permanently removing it from circulating and total supply. Trading activity therefore feeds directly into purchases and token removal.

The 1win token applies similar thinking to iGaming. According to 1win, the token is being designed around platform utility alongside buyback and burn mechanisms. $1WIN has a fixed supply of one billion tokens with no additional minting after TGE. Its burn mechanism is tied directly to use: 10% of $1WIN spent across supported products, including gaming and lottery activity, is intended to be permanently burned through a smart contract.

The second mechanism is a regular open-market buyback program. Rather than financing those purchases from a finite token reserve, 1win plans to connect buybacks to revenue generated through its gaming ecosystem.

That funding source is worthy of attention.

A project can put $10 million aside at launch and use it to buy its own token for several years. Those purchases may create demand, but the pool eventually runs dry. A revenue-funded system works differently: customers use the underlying product, the business generates revenue, and some of that revenue flows back into token purchases.

For 1win, the token is being introduced after the business. The company has operated since 2016 and says it has more than 30 million registered players across 100+ countries. Its existing activities include casino gaming, sports and esports, affiliate operations and crypto payments. The basic premise is therefore to connect $1WIN’s tokenomics to an economy that already operates without it.

None of these models creates a mathematical guarantee of higher prices. A token can become scarcer while demand falls even faster. Revenue can decline. Unlocks can outweigh burns. A fixed supply does not fix weak utility.

That is why “deflationary” on its own tells investors very little. The useful questions come one level deeper: What gets burned? What gets unlocked? Who funds the buybacks? And what economic activity pays for them?

Those answers tell you far more about a token than the word “deflationary” ever will.

#55. Strategy's price chart is about to flash a major bullish signal weeks after bitcoin did

This is an excerpt from CoinDesk newsletter 'Daybook.' Sign up here, if you haven't already.

Weeks after bitcoin’s (BTC) price chart flashed a major bullish signal, Strategy MSTR$135.98·Market Closed, the largest publicly listed accumulator of the cryptocurrency, is about to do the same.

The signal, a golden cross, occurs when a security’s 50-day average price rises above its 200-day average. Some traders read the transition as a decisive bullish shift in momentum that can lead to a prolonged rally.

For MSTR, which holds $69.81 billion in bitcoin, the cross could happen as soon as Monday. Since the company began buying the largest cryptocurrency for its balance sheet in August 2020, the stock has had two such crosses, and huge rallies followed both.

The first happened on Sept. 15, 2020, with the stock at about $15.57. MSTR climbed to $127.29 by February 2021, a gain of 717%. A death cross, the opposite of golden cross, followed in January 2022. By then, the stock was at $46.83, still triple the value on the day the bullish signal first appeared.

The second came on March 2, 2023, at $25.29. The shares peaked at $473.83 in November 2024, up 1,774%. When the death cross arrived in October 2025, MSTR was at $328.40, still 1,199% higher.

It’s worth keeping in mind that the signal isn’t especially reliable. In MSTR’s case, since 1999, the shares have registered 19 golden crosses. On 11 occasions, the stock was higher three months later, and after only 10 was it higher 12 months later, according to data analyzed by CoinDesk.

That’s a record of 50% accuracy. The median 12-month return was just 3.3%, and the two worst crosses, in 2001 and 2007, were followed by a 61% loss.

Since bitcoin confirmed its golden cross on Sept. 8, it has risen by nearly 5% to $82,000, extending the rally from July lows under $60,000. The price hit a high of over $87,000 early this month.

It remains to be seen if MSTR follows bitcoin’s lead. Stay alert!

#56. Mastercard launches stablecoin risk screening for banks and payment providers

The new service combines payment data and blockchain analytics to help banks detect suspicious stablecoin transactions before settlement.

Mastercard is extending its payment risk controls to stablecoin transactions by introducing a tool that lets financial institutions flag suspicious activity before funds move onchain, where recovering stolen funds can be difficult.

Unveiled Monday at the Money20/20 USA conference, Mastercard’s Stablecoin Security combines traditional payment data with blockchain analytics to identify fraud, scams, sanctions exposure and other financial crime risks. Borderless.xyz and Keyrails are the initial partners, with global commercial availability expected next year.

Banks already use fraud detection to monitor conventional payments. Stablecoins add complexity because funds can move across multiple wallets and blockchains, making it harder to assess risk throughout a transaction. Mastercard said Stablecoin Security can generate a risk score before a payment is completed, allowing banks to identify transactions that may require further review.

The launch marks another expansion of Mastercard’s stablecoin business following its $1.8 billion acquisition of BVNK in August. It also follows the company’s recent announcement of a Global Money Platform designed to bring stablecoin payments to businesses.

Mastercard’s stablecoin expansion comes as growth in the supply of digital dollars has slowed significantly this year, even as transaction volumes have accelerated, driven in part by remittances and cross-border payments. A recent Standard Chartered report suggests the stablecoin market could reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than its initial forecast.

#61. Why Some of America’s Biggest Companies Are Objecting to Tokenized Shares

Why Some of America’s Biggest Companies Are Objecting to Tokenized Shares

Wall Street’s push to put stocks onchain is running into an unexpected obstacle: the companies behind the stocks.

Nine issuers, including Verizon, Broadcom, and UnitedHealth Group, have objected to having their shares offered on OKXICE TSV, according to an Oct. 15 public notice from the venue.

OKXICE TSV is a planned tokenized stock platform from crypto exchange OKX and NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange. The other objecting companies are Cerebras Systems, AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave, and Applied Optoelectronics.

The notice didn’t say why the companies objected or whether the objections will keep their shares off the platform.

Nasdaq is also keeping its distance. The exchange operator, which isn’t among the nine, has said it would opt its own shares out of the SEC’s framework. A spokesperson told The Wall Street Journal that Nasdaq doesn’t want its stock trading on a venue that doesn’t show the best prices in real time or report trades to the consolidated tape. That’s notable given that Nasdaq won SEC approval earlier this year for its own tokenized securities pilot.

The venue is the first major test of the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate. The exemption lets qualifying platforms trade tokenized U.S. stocks without registering as exchanges. OKXICE plans to run around the clock using Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, with trades settled in stablecoins such as USDC and USDT.

The tokens are created by a third party, not the companies themselves. That outside “tokenizer” holds actual shares one-for-one through a registered broker-dealer, and token holders are supposed to receive the same dividends and voting rights as regular shareholders, according to the notice.

The notice also lays out what users give up. OKXICE isn’t registered with the SEC, isn’t subject to Regulation NMS rules designed to ensure investors get the best displayed prices, and doesn’t have to provide fair access to all participants. Trading is capped at a small slice of each stock’s normal volume, and administrators can upgrade the venue’s smart contracts without advance notice.

OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before announcing the 24/7 venue this month. In terms of appetite from traders and investors for tokenized stocks, the International Monetary Fund recently found real demand for tokenized stocks—especially outside of traditional market hours—but warned that the market remains volatile and illiquid.

#64. Revolut secures Gibraltar crypto license to support global expansion

The UK-based fintech will use the authorization to offer crypto services in additional international markets, though it has not disclosed specific countries or launch dates.

Revolut, a UK-based financial technology company and neobank, has received a cryptocurrency services license in Gibraltar, which it plans to use to expand its digital asset offerings into international markets beyond the UK and European Economic Area.

The Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) granted a Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) Provider license to Revolut Global Digital Assets Limited, a newly established subsidiary, according to a Monday announcement.

A Revolut spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the license will allow the company to offer crypto services in additional international markets, although specific countries and launch timelines have not been announced.

Revolut currently provides cryptocurrency services through Revolut Ltd in the UK and Revolut Digital Assets Europe Ltd across the European Economic Area, where its operations fall under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

The fintech reports more than 80 million retail customers worldwide, including about 16 million cryptocurrency users, according to its announcement.

The Gibraltar license follows Revolut’s in-principle approval to offer crypto services in Dubai in July and preliminary conditional approval from US regulators in September to establish a national bank offering digital asset custody and crypto-related payment services.

#66. SWIFT, Ripple (XRP) & BNP Paribas: Connecting The Dots

Home » Ripple (XRP) » SWIFT, Ripple (XRP) & BNP Paribas: Connecting The Dots

At Sibos 2026, BNP Paribas highlighted the potential of SWIFT to expand settlement options for clients worldwide.

In a video shared by SWIFT, a bank representative noted that the ledger would allow the institution to integrate “every single settlement route” into its banking offering, helping digital value move through trusted global infrastructure at scale.

SWIFT’s ledger, which moved from concept to live use earlier this year, is designed as an orchestration layer for tokenised deposits. It enables participating banks to support 24/7 cross-border payments while final settlement still occurs through existing systems.

🏦 BNP Paribas uses Metaco, a digital asset custody & tokenization technology provider, which Ripple acquired already back in 2023 🤭 $XRP 🤝🏼 BNP Paribas 🤝🏼 SWIFT https://t.co/e1zj25GLNT

BNP Paribas is among the early adopters that have already completed live transactions on the platform, including a notable corporate treasury payment alongside HSBC for Siemens.

The system aims to give banks greater flexibility for always-on liquidity without requiring clients to change how they bank. By the end of 2026, at least 19 institutions are expected to use the ledger across multiple currencies.

BNP Paribas has long worked with Metaco, a Swiss digital asset custody and tokenisation technology provider. Metaco’s Harmonize platform has been used by major banks, including BNP Paribas Securities Services, for institutional digital asset operations.

Ripple acquired Metaco in 2023 for approximately $250 million. The deal expanded Ripple’s institutional offerings in custody, issuance and settlement of tokenised assets. Metaco continues to operate as an independent brand under Ripple’s ownership.

The combination places a Ripple-owned technology provider inside the digital asset infrastructure of a major SWIFT ledger participant.

🚨 SWIFT has formed a board of fresh executives for it's shared blockchain based ledger. @Ripple already have existing connections to all three major banking giants 👇🏼HSBC utilizes digital asset infrastructure from Metaco (Ripple Custody).Citi and Ripple collaborate through… pic.twitter.com/rqqg6qrPIG

While the SWIFT ledger itself currently focuses on bank-issued tokenised deposits rather than public-chain assets like XRP, the overlap illustrates how traditional banking rails and crypto-native infrastructure are increasingly intersecting.

For the XRP community, the connection fuels ongoing discussion about potential future interoperability between regulated banking systems and blockchain networks.

BNP Paribas’s public comments on the SWIFT ledger, paired with its established use of Metaco, keep the conversation around institutional adoption and cross-network settlement active.

As SWIFT continues expanding its ledger and banks deepen their digital asset capabilities, partnerships of this nature will remain closely watched by both traditional finance and crypto markets.

#68. Crypto wallet activity: Two dormant addresses move nearly $34M in Bitcoin

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Two Bitcoin wallets dormant for more than 12 years moved about 417 BTC, worth $33.85 million, according to Lookonchain.

The movements brought Bitcoin held in the addresses for over a decade back into circulation between wallets. However, the available records do not say that anyone sold the coins or sent them to an exchange.

Arkham data show two main outgoing transfers. One address moved 248.854 BTC, valued at about $20.22 million, while the other transferred 167.84 BTC, worth around $13.63 million. Together, those transactions were 416.694 BTC.

The data also show earlier incoming transactions dating back roughly 12 and 13 years. For the larger wallet, the 248.854 BTC received was valued at about $88,460.

A crypto wallet transfer takes record of coins moving between addresses. But the transaction alone cannot tell why they moved or whether ownership changed.

In this case, the data does not identify the holders or show what they want to do. It also does not show exchange destination, which would suggest that the coins were being prepared for sale.

What can then be concluded defensibly is that two addresses associated with long-held Bitcoin saw huge outgoing transfers.

Bitcoin traded around $82,152 at the time of this writing, following a retreat from recent highs near the $87,000 price area.

At the time of this writing, there were smaller price swings around the $81,000–$83,000 price level. This suggests that the decline had slowed down, but Bitcoin was yet to show a clear recovery sign.

The nearby area around $82,500 remained an initial hurdle, while the $80,000–$80,500 below it is an area to watch. If it is able to hold that lower area, it would help it preserve the recent stabilization it is seeing.

Shiba Inu's daily burn rate has jumped 2,349%, but the real figure behind the surge remains surprising. Despite the sharp rise, the total value of Shiba Inu tokens burned during the reported period amounted to just about $5.

According to the Shibburn page, Shiba Inu burn activity rose 2,349% in the last 24 hours, with 1.10 million SHIB burned in the timeframe, amounting to just $5 in monetary terms. This highlights how a relatively small number of token burns can produce a striking percentage increase when activity in the preceding period is low.

The burn rate alone does not reveal how many tokens were destroyed. If there was little or no burning in the prior period, a small transaction can cause a large percentage increase.

Here, the reported $5 of burned SHIB suggests that the growth is due to a large percentage change rather than a large drop in Shiba Inu's total supply.

#71. US Orders Civilian Agencies to Rip DeepSeek Out of Government Systems

US Orders Civilian Agencies to Rip DeepSeek Out of Government Systems

The U.S. Department of Homeland Security ordered civilian government agencies on Monday to remove DeepSeek, China’s best-known AI chatbot, from their computer systems and to stop buying it, along with any outside service built on top of it.

DHS says the models pose “multiple threat vectors,” meaning several separate ways things can go wrong. Using them “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC”—the People’s Republic of China—if government employees or vendors use them, and could produce “actionable intelligence on U.S. persons and/or government agencies.”

Deepseek is an open source model that can run locally or hosted by any provider, not just China based. For example, Perplexity runs its own servers located in the United States. That said, the developers host a version in servers located in China for those using Deepseek.com’s services.

The ban reaches past DeepSeek’s own app to third-party services developed using it.

A July DHS memo, made public Monday, had already told agencies to monitor traffic flowing in and out of government websites for DeepSeek-related risks. The Commerce Department and the Navy previously banned DeepSeek on government devices, and New York, Tennessee and Virginia have taken similar steps. The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately comment.

DeepSeek, a Hangzhou-based startup, became a household name on Jan. 27, 2025, when its open-source model, built for under $5 million, knocked Nvidia’s stock down 16% and erased about $600 billion of the chipmaker’s value. U.S. tech as a whole lost an estimated $1 trillion that day, because Deepseek proved to be similarly capable than America’s best models while costing a fraction of the price, with the possibility of running for free on the appropriate infrastructure.

Italy’s data protection authority also ordered DeepSeek to block its chatbot days later, calling the company’s answers to its privacy questions “totally insufficient.” In April 2025, a House select committee on the Chinese Communist Party alleged that DeepSeek secretly sends American user data to the Chinese government..

The same committee said DeepSeek may have used about 60,000 Nvidia chips, including 20,000 restricted under U.S. export controls, the rules that bar selling the most advanced AI chips to China.

DeepSeek has kept shipping since: the preview of its V4-Pro model, released in April, is priced about 98% below OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 Pro and is free to download and modify under an MIT license, and this week it released an updated version of its V4.1-Flash model aimed at efficiency with big quality gains.

The notice lands in the middle of a wider federal push against Chinese technology as the Federal Communications Commission votes on October 29 on barring all Chinese labs from testing electronics for U.S. use.

#74. Metaplanet to take 93.7% stake in Super League through 2,100 BTC deal

The transaction would give Metaplanet access to US capital markets, where it plans to use preferred stock offerings to finance additional Bitcoin purchases.

Shareholders of Super League, a Nasdaq-listed gaming and digital media company, approved a deal that would give Japanese Bitcoin treasury firm Metaplanet a 93.7% ownership stake, paving the way for its expansion into US capital markets through a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company.

According to a Monday announcement and filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), shareholders approved the issuance of as many as 435.9 million common shares under agreements involving Metaplanet and Evo Fund. Metaplanet will contribute 2,100 Bitcoin (BTC) and $2.5 million in cash in exchange for 44.86 million common shares, 100 shares of convertible perpetual preferred stock carrying governance rights and 10-year warrants for additional common stock.

The transaction would give Metaplanet control over the company, including the ability to designate a majority of its board and approve major corporate decisions. Metaplanet’s common shares will be subject to a five-year lock-up.

As part of the deal, Super League plans to rebrand as Superplanet and adopt the Nasdaq ticker SUPA, with a strategy focused on increasing its Bitcoin holdings per share.

Rather than relying primarily on debt, Superplanet intends to finance additional Bitcoin purchases through senior, non-convertible perpetual preferred shares. Metaplanet will also have the option to invest up to $210 million in junior preferred stock to provide additional financial support.

Source: Dylan LeClair, Metaplanet director of Bitcoin strategy

The deal comes as Metaplanet continues to expand its Bitcoin holdings. The company has accumulated 44,000 BTC, making it the second-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder behind Strategy, according to industry data.

Related: Metaplanet to issue $329M convertible bonds to pay debt, fund share buybacks

The deal would enable Metaplanet to raise capital in US dollars through preferred stock offerings, complementing its existing yen-denominated financing in Japan.

In an Oct. 15 SEC filing, Super League said the US market for preferred securities issued by Bitcoin treasury companies has grown large enough to support new entrants. The proposed financing structure would provide another source of funding for Bitcoin purchases without relying primarily on conventional debt.

The expansion comes as Metaplanet revises its broader investment strategy. Earlier this month, the company proposed allocating up to 15% of its total assets for strategic investments to help finance Bitcoin purchases and dividend payments.

Related: Metaplanet CEO shuts down Bitcoin sale speculation after $322M transfer

#79. 'Right Way for Ethereum?' Zcash Cofounder Backs Vitalik's Quantum-Ready Approach

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

There is an ongoing debate on X about lattice versus hash-based cryptography in blockchain design, with Zcash cofounder Eli Ben Sasson, Ethereum cofounder Vitalik Buterin, and Delphi Labs GC Gabriel Shapiro joining the discussion.

The conversation began with a16z crypto making the case for embracing lattices in a recent X post. In a write-up, a16z crypto explained its rationale; it claims Ethereum's planned hash-only signature aggregation design relies on SNARK recursion, with the coordination overhead, bug surface, and unestablished security that come with this approach.

Engaging with a16z crypto's post, Zcash cofounder Eli Ben Sasson strongly disagreed, noting that lattices have a juicy mathematical structure that is ripe for AI to attack.

According to a16z crypto, relying solely on hash-based cryptography may appear safer, but in such designs, it can result in more brittle systems. Expanding the conversation further, Delphi Labs GC Gabriel Shapiro shared his take on X: "I think the Ethereum approach remains the best option here for Ethereum," disagreeing with a16z crypto's take.

Ethereum's Lean consensus roadmap includes fully replacing BLS signatures with hash-based signatures (some variant of Winternitz) and using STARKs to do aggregation. Shapiro suggested utilizing lattice cryptography for accounts and wallets through a precompile if it is proved to be AI-secure, adding that hash-based cryptography allows Ethereum to go full speed.

Vitalik Buterin weighed in on the discussion, agreeing with Shapiro: "we could still ultimately do lattice stuff for accounts and wallets through a precompile if it is proved to be AI-secure."

"The ideal route to support everyone's cryptography is imo through 8288. You make whatever signature you want locally, then STARK it, and then it gets included through the stark aggregator machine. Don't need any calldata onchain. Ethereum can then never add a new precompile again," Buterin added.

@VitalikButerin @lex_node agree this is the right way for Ethereum

To this, Zcash cofounder Eli Ben Sasson responded, saying, "Agree, this is the right way for Ethereum."

Aside from Bitcoin, most large blockchains use proof of stake, which allows validators to vote on each block by signing it. Large validator sets are practical because of signature aggregation. Ethereum utilizes BLS signatures, which have an algebraic structure that allows them to combine tens of thousands of validator signatures per slot into a single group element.

However, as beneficial as BLS is, it is not post-quantum because no known post-quantum signature schemes aggregate in this manner.

Explaining the quantum resistance roadmap earlier this year, Buterin mentioned the solution to be protocol-layer recursive signatures and proof aggregation. He spoke about adding native account abstraction through EIP-8141, which provides a framework abstraction for transaction validation, execution, and gas payment so that first-class accounts could use any signature algorithm.

#81. JPMorgan's JPM Coin Arrives on Ethereum, Putting Bank Dollars on a Public Blockchain

JPMorgan's JPM Coin Arrives on Ethereum, Putting Bank Dollars on a Public Blockchain

JPMorgan Chase is putting JPM Coin on Ethereum, which gives its biggest clients a way to move dollars in seconds on a Sunday night as easily as on a Tuesday morning.

A normal wire between banks only moves during business hours and can take days to land, which is why JPMorgan started experimenting with blockchain technology. The idea is using JPM Coin to cut that wait to seconds.

The token is a deposit token, so each unit stands for a dollar already sitting in a JPMorgan account, and the bank's site says clients can redeem it for dollars at any time with no lock-up. A stablecoin, by contrast, is a token pegged to the dollar by a private company that holds the reserves somewhere else.

Only vetted, approved counterparties can hold JPM Coin, so this is not a coin anyone can buy on an exchange.

JPMorgan first put the token on Base, a cheaper and faster network built on top of Ethereum and incubated by Coinbase, in November 2025. That followed months of testing with Mastercard and Coinbase, and holders can now move the token between the two networks.

In January, the bank also said it would bring JPM Coin to Canton Network, a privacy-focused blockchain built for financial markets. It has also issued two tokenized money-market funds on Ethereum, in December 2025 and May 2026, which are funds holding short-term debt that are represented as tokens.

Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan's blockchain unit, pointed to the money and tokenized assets (traditional investments such as shares, debt and funds, issued as blockchain tokens) already circulating on Ethereum, where about $50 billion sits in applications, according to DefiLlama.

Crypto firms are expected to use the token for payments, while financial institutions can use it to pay for trades in tokenized assets or to post collateral, meaning a guarantee against a deal.

“We’ve clearly been in a year of further convergence between Wall Street and crypto,” Landriault told Bloomberg. Matthew Dawson, co-founder of Ethereum Institutional, called the move “a clear signal that institutional finance is moving onto public, verifiable infrastructure.”

The bank is also fighting for the same customers as stablecoin issuers. A consortium of more than 100 companies including Visa, Stripe, and Mastercard launched its own dollar stablecoin last month, while Kinexys co-head Naveen Mallela has said deposit tokens are “a compelling alternative” to stablecoins because they “can be yield-bearing,” meaning they can pay interest.

Kinexys, the unit behind the token, has handled more than $4 trillion in cumulative transactions and averages about $7 billion a day, against roughly $12 trillion a day across JPMorgan's wider payments business.

JPMorgan, Citigroup and other large banks plan to launch a shared 24/7 tokenized deposit network as early as the first half of 2027.

#86. France advances crypto-to-stablecoin tax proposal by just one vote

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

French lawmakers just approved an amendment that would make crypto-to-stablecoin conversions taxable.

It’s not law yet. But perhaps it’s time for French traders to rethink the way they push their money around.

On October 16, France’s National Assembly adopted Amendment I-3898. The amendment passed by a single vote, with 38 lawmakers supporting it, 37 opposing it, and 25 abstaining.

It started life as a committee amendment I-CF1826, introduced by MP Nicolas Sansu and approved on October 7.

What would it actually change? Right now, swapping Bitcoin [BTC] for a stablecoin in France doesn’t trigger taxation. Under this amendment, that swap would count as a taxable incidence.

The amendment would also change how gains are calculated. For cryptocurrencies bought at different prices, it proposes using a weighted-average purchase cost to determine the gain when those assets are sold or exchanged.

It’s not law yet, though. The Assembly is set to vote on the first part of the 2027 Finance Bill tomorrow. A few other crypto proposals are on the table as well, but it’s not quite known which ones would come up on the day.

The stablecoin swap tax isn’t the only crypto idea on the table.

On the same day, lawmakers shot down a proposal that would’ve let investors carry forward realised crypto losses for 10 years. That one wasn’t close at all, with 18 in favor and 75 against. 3 abstained.

Amendment I-CF1822 would extend France’s exit tax to crypto. If your total crypto portfolio is worth more than €800,000 [$895,000] and you move abroad, you could be taxed on gains you haven’t even cashed in yet.

Then there’s Amendment I-2701. It would require people to declare what’s in their self-custodial wallets if the total value goes over €100,000 [$112,000] in a given tax year.

French crypto holders have a lot to keep an eye on this week.

XRP’s burning mechanism is the silent partner working along in the OG altcoin’s ecosystem, now expanding towards more DeFi services than ever before. With the new utility cases in lending, multi-currency liquidity & direct cross-border settlement via banking partners, XRP’s market size could see a substantial influx.

Some analysts argue the XRP burning mechanism is the catalyst everyone’s missing out on: with the transaction growth on the XRP Ledger growing to unprecedented figures, more XRP gets burned on-chain. According to Dr. Kamilah Stevenson, the supply shrinking every day enables a dual force in XRP’s eventual price appreciation.

Renowned technical crypto chart analysts like ChartNerd or Egrag Crypto have been floating $10 XRP theses based on historical price data or trading instruments. Dr. Kamilah Stevenson refrained from making one, but the implication is still crystal-clear.

More institutional adoption, combined with a deflationary tactic, is a perfect bullish setup in the long-term, the wealth-focused market connoisseur argues: “Here’s what most people miss: every single transaction on the XRP ledger burns XRP. Not sent somewhere. Not stored. Gone. Permanently.”

According to CryptoTuts’ daily dataset, the total XRP burned rose from approximately 14.38 million on Sept. 15 to 14.41 million on Oct. 15. That counts up to 24,745 XRP eliminated from circulating supply in 30 days, averaging roughly 825 XRP per day. That’s 2.696K in 7 days. Still a tiny fraction of the 100 billion supply, it can start to contract rapidly upon adoption.

If that kind of pace continues for a year, approximately 301,000 XRP is taken out of the game. Just 0.0003% of the nearly 100 billion XRP remaining. The XRP Ledger’s documentation explains that transaction costs protect the network against spam and denial-of-service attacks.

The minimum fee is 10 drops, equivalent to 0.00001 XRP. At the standard minimum of 100,000 transactions, 1 XRP is destroyed. So one billion transactions paying that fee would destroy 10K XRP. Also, the drop-based structure could technically require a higher price upon high usage.

Deflationary token tactics, met with proper demand, should increase the asset’s price in theory. The amplitude of that highly depends on the network’s usage, parameters & market sentiment.

#88. Revolut secures Gibraltar crypto licence to support international expansion plans

Get The Block’s latest crypto news and price alerts for the coins you follow, right in Chrome. Add our free extension here.

Revolut Global Digital Assets Limited will support the fintech's international crypto services alongside its existing UK and European operations.

Global fintech Revolut has secured a Distributed Ledger Technology provider licence from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission for a newly formed entity, the company said in a statement shared with The Block on Monday.

The new entity, Revolut Global Digital Assets Limited, will support the company's international crypto operations, it said.

“Securing our DLT authorization from the GFSC reflects our commitment to operating at the highest standards of regulatory compliance,” Emil Urmashin, Revolut’s general manager for crypto and new bets, said in the statement.

Revolut already offers crypto services in the UK through Revolut Ltd and across the European Economic Area through Revolut Digital Assets Europe Ltd, which operates under the EU’s MiCA rules.

The company has more than 80 million retail customers worldwide and over 16 million crypto users, per the statement.

Revolut has doubled down on expansion this year. In March, the company received approval to launch Revolut Bank UK after British regulators lifted restrictions on its banking license. Last month, it secured conditional approval from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency as it pursued a U.S. banking charter.

The company also began rolling out its euro-pegged EURR stablecoin to selected customers in Denmark, Poland, and Portugal in August, with broader availability across the EEA planned later this year.

Revolut did not say which markets its Gibraltar entity will serve or when. It said details on target regions and rollouts would come in due course.

#90. JPMorgan brings JPM Coin, representing dollar deposits, to Ethereum

JPMorgan(JPM), the largest U.S. bank, brought its almost year-old crypto token, JPM Coin, to Ethereum as part of a plan to expand beyond Base, the layer-2 blockchain built by Coinbase Global COIN$168.31·Market Closed.

JPM Coin, which represents dollar deposits at the bank, was technically deployed on the Ethereum mainnet on Monday and is available for institutional clients’ use, the bank said in an emailed statement.

The bank chose Ethereum because the blockchain offers more liquidity than rival networks and is already used by institutional clients, Emma Landriault, the head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan’s blockchain division Kinexys, said in an interview with Bloomberg, which reported the news earlier.

“Issuing JPM Coin first on Base and now on Ethereum is a meaningful step towards providing our institutional clients with multi-chain optionality for moving wholesale money across both the web3 and traditional finance ecosystems,” she said in the emailed statement.

The banking giant flagged a move outside Base back in January, saying it was planning to take the token to the Canton Network. Broadening its availability aims to serve crypto firms that want to make blockchain payments and financial firms that need a digital token to settle trades or back tokenized assets, Landriault said.

Tokenization is the process of converting real-world assets and financial assets into a digital form that’s recorded and traded on a decentralized ledger. The advantage is speed, including faster settlement of trades, quick movement of money while bypassing delays and frictions involved in traditional rails.

Banks have embraced tokenization, but mostly away from public networks. In the U.S., JPMorgan, Citi (C), Bank of America (BAC) and Wells Fargo (WFC), along with more than a dozen other banks, have plans to start a shared network for tokenized deposits.

JPMorgan’s private blockchain network, Kinexys, already handles more than $7 billion a day, a small piece in the bank’s $12 trillion a day payments business. Almost $50 billion worth of crypto assets are locked in Ethereum-based applications, according to DeFiLlama.

Abroad, JPMorgan is among more than 30 banks that are helping Swift, the interbank messaging service, define the features and governance of its blockchain-based ledger. In July, Swift said 17 banks, including Citi and Wells Fargo, were preparing to pilot live transactions on it. JPMorgan wasn’t on that list.

#91. Abandoned Bitcoin? Wallet Targeted by Noah Doe Lawsuit Moves $33 Million

Abandoned Bitcoin? Wallet Targeted by Noah Doe Lawsuit Moves $33 Million

Another long-sleeping Bitcoin whale has stirred, and this one is named in a lawsuit claiming its coins were abandoned.

An address beginning with "13Coop" that had never sent a single coin since it was first funded on Sept. 11, 2013, moved 411.45 BTC, worth roughly $33.4 million, on Sunday, according to Galaxy Research. Arkham data shows the coins landed in a single new address, where they remain.

When the wallet was funded, Bitcoin traded around $130, according to Arkham, meaning the stash cost about $54,000. Galaxy put the holder’s average cost basis near $127 and the paper gain at more than 64,000%. It’s unclear whether the owner plans to sell, since the transfer went to an unlabeled address, not an exchange.

Galaxy tagged the sending address as “Noah Doe #970,” marking it as one of 39,069 dormant addresses named in a New York lawsuit filed this year by a pseudonymous plaintiff called Noah Doe and two Wyoming companies.

🏚️ 💤 Address awakened — dormant 13+ years — 411.45 BTC sent

This address had never sent coins (first funded 2013-09-11, 13.1y ago); it just spent 411.45 BTC ($33.44M) in block 972,036

Address: 13Coop8xFbYj9JR9WyF5EqzGa9GiZmxs7C

Coins moved: 411.45 BTC in 2 UTXOs — all held…

— Galaxy Research (@glxyresearch) October 18, 2026

The plaintiffs argue that the wallets, which hold about 3.8 million BTC, qualify as abandoned property under the state’s lost-and-found law, even though they hold none of the private keys.

Galaxy also flagged the address as one of those “dusted” in a 2025 campaign that sent tiny amounts of Bitcoin carrying embedded messages to dormant wallets, which Galaxy has described as groundwork for the abandonment claim. Arkham’s data shows a string of those dust deposits, some labeled as phishing.

Each move chips away at the lawsuit’s premise. Spending coins requires the private keys, which suggests at least some of the targeted wallets are anything but abandoned. Galaxy head of research Alex Thorn has said the pace of dormant “Noah Doe” coins moving onchain has been accelerating month over month.

The wallet joins a growing list of old coins on the move. Bitcoin’s oldest coins have been waking up at an unusual clip in 2026, according to Galaxy Research data.

Just a little over a week ago, a Satoshi-era wallet mined in 2010 moved for the first time in 16 years. In late September, about $161 million in decade-old Bitcoin was transferred over the course of roughly two weeks. And just last week, a whale moved a whopping $377 million after holding through every major market crash since 2020.

The token now supports peer-to-peer transfers within the Ethereum Virtual Machine ecosystem, including Base and Ethereum.

JPMorgan has brought its USD-denominated deposit token JPM Coin (JPMD) to Ethereum for institutional clients, as the bank continues its tokenization drive.

In a Monday statement shared with The Block, Kinexys by JPMorgan said Ethereum's "established depth of onchain liquidity and tokenized assets" makes it a natural next public blockchain for JPMD, which was first launched in November 2025 on Base.

JPMD serves as a representation of JPMorgan's existing bank deposits on a public blockchain, enabling institutional clients to make onchain native payments with enhanced speed and efficiency, according to its website.

The token now supports peer-to-peer transfers within the Ethereum Virtual Machine ecosystem, including Base and Ethereum.

"Tokenized financial infrastructure is no longer theoretical. It’s already restructuring liquidity, settlement, and digital asset workflows," Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs at Kinexys by J.P. Morgan, said in the statement.

The latest expansion builds on the lender's broader push to bring traditional instruments onchain. In December 2025, it launched its first tokenized money-market fund on Ethereum, followed by a second fund in May 2026.

The bank said Monday that the Kinexys platform has handled over $4 trillion in cumulative transactions to date, with an average daily transaction volume of $7 billion.

"We're delighted to see J.P. Morgan Payments bring JPM Coin to Ethereum. It builds on a clear trajectory: JPM Coin is already live on Base, J.P. Morgan Asset Management has tokenized money market funds on Ethereum, and the Kinexys platform itself is built on Ethereum Virtual Machine technology," said Matthew Dawson, co-founder of Ethereum Institutional.

"It's a clear signal that institutional finance is moving onto public, verifiable infrastructure," Dawson added.

#98. Binance Completes 37th BNB Chain Burn: This Is How Many Tokens Were Burned

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. The thirty-seventh quarterly BNB token burn is done. It was achieved directly on BNB Smart Chain (BSC), and it eliminated a massive quantity of BNB from circulation for good. According to the official data, 1,646,196 BNB have been burned.

At current prices, that quantity is worth about $1.197 billion. The tokens have been sent to a burn address, so no one can use them again.

A burn gets rid of tokens from the total supply. When the supply goes down, every remaining token becomes a larger proportion of the whole. This is the primary reason BNB holders pay attention to each quarterly burn.

After this burn, the rest of the supply stands at 131,512,500 BNB. That is the quantity still left in existence. The supply has been falling since the first burn, and the process is planned to continue until half of the original supply is gone.

The thirty-seventh burn is close to the scale of recent ones. The thirty-sixth burn eliminated 1,615,827 BNB, and the thirty-fifth eliminated 1,569,307 BNB. The thirty-fourth burn was 1,371,803 BNB, and the thirty-third was 1,441,281 BNB. So this burn is a bit larger than the last few, which suggests a gradual upward trend after a dip.

Some earlier burns were much larger. The 14th burn eliminated 3,619,888 BNB, and the 11th eliminated 3,373,988 BNB. The first burn was 986,000 BNB. Burn sizes have changed a lot over the years, but the quarterly schedule has stayed the same.

The burn quantity depends on two things: the BNB price and the number of blocks produced on BNB Chain during the quarter. When the price is higher or the network is busier, the burn changes. Because of this, no two burns are exactly the same.

The auto-burn system makes the process fair and transparent. Anyone can check the numbers on chain, and the quantity follows a clear formula rather than a decision made behind closed doors.

Many investors see the burn schedule as a long-term plan to reduce supply. Fewer tokens in circulation can support the price over time, if demand remains the same or grows. But a burn does not guarantee a price rise. The market can move up or down for many other reasons.

Still, a burn worth more than $1 billion is a strong signal. It shows that the project keeps its promise to reduce supply on a regular basis. The next burn will take place next quarter, and the community will watch to see if the quantity grows again.

#100. Bitcoin Tests Key Support as Oil and AI Fears Squeeze Markets

Bitcoin Tests Key Support as Oil and AI Fears Squeeze Markets

Bitcoin continues to defy seasonal ‘Uptober” expectations, as macroeconomic factors weigh heavily on the digital asset.

Bitcoin is hovering around $82,000 on Monday, up about 1% on the day, after tagging $83,000 early and handing some of it back.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, trades near $108 a barrel after weekend attacks on Persian Gulf tankers and Russian crude facilities. Pricey oil raises the cost of fuel and freight, which feeds inflation. The consumer price index (CPI), what households pay, rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, while the producer price index (PPI), what businesses pay, jumped 6.3%, the biggest annual rise since 2022.

That likely pushes the Federal Reserve toward raising interest rates, which makes borrowing costlier. Markets see roughly a 15% chance of a quarter-point hike next week. You can see it in Treasury yields, the return investors earn lending to the U.S. government: when hike bets rise, bond prices fall and yields climb. The 10-year sits at 5.08% and the 2-year at 4.72%, CNBC data shows.

A near risk-free 5% competes with stocks and crypto for the same money, and it raises the debt costs of the AI giants that borrowed heavily for data centers. Bitcoin trades with that risk basket, so AI selloffs tend to drag it down.

The pain was concentrated in companies paying for the AI buildout with borrowed money. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% on Friday and closed its worst week since June, with AMD down 6% and Micron down 5.6% on the day. CoreWeave, a so-called “neocloud” that rents out AI computing power, lost about 24% over the week, and it funds much of its data center spending with debt and new share sales rather than cash flow.

Hotter inflation and higher yields make that kind of debt costlier to carry, so the stock selloff and the bond market are really the same story.

Bitcoin trades at $82,164 on the daily chart, up 0.18% in today’s forming candlestick, sitting right on the 0.236 Fibonacci retracement at $81,603. Fibonacci levels mark where pullbacks tend to pause, and 23.6% is the shallowest, so holding it keeps the climb from the $87,422 high intact. The bounce is weak, though: a week of small candle bodies says neither side is in control.

Bitcoin’s current price is also inside the $81,847 to $82,305 "golden zone" of the recent $80,365 to $84,246 swing, where buyers often show up.

The 50-day exponential moving average, or EMA, weights recent prices more heavily and sits at about $80,548, above the 200-day EMA at about $75,932, with current price above both. That formation, known as golden cross, reads bullish because short-term buyers are paying more than long-term holders.

The Average Directional Index, or ADX, measures trend strength, and currently reads 21.6. Below 25 means no firm trend and more false breakouts. The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, is at 49.3, basically dead neutral with neither bulls nor bears dominating the market.

So, without a clear trend, the Squeeze Momentum Indicator has been "on" for 13 days, meaning volatility is compressed like a spring. Momentum at -1.42 leans mildly down.

A daily close below $81,603 opens $81,196 and the 50-day EMA. Bulls need closes above $83,330 and $84,246, ideally with a rising ADX. The Fed meeting next week and major earnings calls (like Meta and Tesla) this week are the next catalysts to follow.

#101. Crypto vault deposits top $10 billion as lending risks draw regulatory scrutiny

Crypto lending vaults have attracted more than $10 billion in deposits, as investors seek returns on their digital assets, according to the Financial Times.

Deposits have risen from $4 billion at the start of last year, highlighting growing demand for strategies that put stablecoins and other tokens to work.

Vaults operate through smart contracts on decentralized finance platforms. Each has a “curator”, effectively an investment manager, who selects lending strategies, sets risk limits and collects fees. Returns typically range from 3% to 10%, although riskier strategies can generate as much as 20% or more.

The appeal comes with considerable risks. Loans can be backed by illiquid tokens, crypto-backed stablecoins or tokenized private credit, leaving depositors exposed if collateral loses value or becomes difficult to sell.

Automatic liquidations can intensify market declines, while hacks, coding errors and flawed pricing mechanisms create additional vulnerabilities. Publicly accessible smart contracts offer transparency, but investors may focus on headline yields without understanding the underlying exposure.

Fintech companies, digital asset treasury businesses and hedge funds are among the main depositors, according to the article.

Bitcoin backed lender Two Prime are among the firms entering the market. In September, it rolled out a bitcoin lending vault on Pareto targeting annual yields of 1.5% to 2% through institutional lending. The vault accepts wrapped bitcoin, requires a minimum deposit of 5 WBTC and has roughly $10 million of Two Prime’s capital committed to absorb initial losses.

Regulators are examining whether existing rules should apply. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has raised questions about vaults holding securities, while European regulators have proposed oversight of intermediaries providing access to DeFi.

#103. Made an ‘honest’ mistake with crypto taxes? New bill offers way out

A proposed US bill would let crypto investors correct past tax reporting mistakes through a dedicated disclosure program, with reduced penalties for eligible taxpayers.

Crypto investors who failed to report trades in previous years may soon breathe a sigh of relief thanks to legislation currently advancing in the US Congress.

Section 502 of the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act, H.R. 10357, would require the Treasury secretary to establish a Digital Asset Voluntary Disclosure Program within 12 months of the bill becoming law.

That would allow eligible taxpayers to correct any past digital asset tax violation by filing amended returns and paying the tax owed, along with interest and a program penalty.

The House Ways and Means Committee approved the bill by a 38-5 vote on Sept. 16, but it has not become law yet; it still has to pass the House and Senate and be signed by the president.

“It’s a big change that would help a lot of ordinary taxpayers, and it has gotten very little attention,” Andrew Gordon, executive director of Digital Asset Tax Action, tells Magazine.

Crypto investors in the US are already grappling with the first filing season under the new 1099-DA broker reporting rules, which give the IRS greater visibility into crypto transactions.

Gordon says those rules should make reporting easier going forward, but they fail to address the years before coming into effect.

The House Ways and Means Committee approved the bill by a 38-5 vote. Source: Ways & Means

“A large share of investors didn’t report correctly over the years,” he says, and existing procedures don’t offer taxpayers who made “honest mistakes” a predictable way to resolve their liabilities.

Related: Greece plans 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies

“Today, a crypto investor who learns they didn’t properly report their crypto or has not reported at all has no good way to fix it,” he says; investors can discover years later that they misunderstood the tax treatment of crypto-to-crypto trades or reporting activity across multiple platforms.

The IRS’s existing Voluntary Disclosure Practice is aimed at taxpayers who willfully violated tax rules and face potential criminal exposure.

For taxpayers with errant reporting skills, they can currently correct their mistakes by filing amended returns, but the penalty treatment is not as predictable as provision 502’s proposed crypto-specific program.

Sharon Yip, a certified public accountant (CPA) and founder of Crypto Tax Advisors, says reporting errors among ordinary crypto investors are common.

In her firm’s experience, some clients did not report crypto because they believed no tax was due until they cashed out, while others relied on incomplete exchange records or incorrectly classified transactions.

“There is no standardized process that gives non-willful crypto investors predictable penalty treatment or a clear resolution,” Yip tells Magazine.

She says a crypto-specific program could “fill this gap” by providing a “defined correction period, reduced and predictable penalties and greater certainty for taxpayers who come forward voluntarily.”

Under Section 502, taxpayers would generally have to file amended returns within 24 months of the program being established, and the bill sets out two penalty tracks.

There are lower rates for taxpayers who certify under penalty of perjury that their violations were neither fraudulent nor willful. They would face a 0% penalty on the first $25,000 of tax deficiency per year and 5% on amounts above that, if they file within the first 12 months of the program.

For those who don’t certify, rates of 25% on the first $25,000 and 40% above it apply, with the rates increasing if taxpayers miss the initial window.

49% of crypto users understood selling crypto can be a taxable event. Source: Cointracker

There is also relief from specified civil penalties, and taxpayers who don’t certify are protected from criminal referrals based on information properly disclosed for the tax offenses covered by the provision.

Yip says taxpayers should check their transaction histories across exchanges and wallets to identify which years need correcting before assessing whether their mistakes were genuinely non-willful.

Because falsely certifying carries a penalty of perjury, she advises seeking professional guidance where taxpayers are unsure.

Section 502 could come as a welcome relief for many US crypto users; a 2026 report by CoinTracker and Coinbase found that only 49% correctly understood that selling crypto can be a taxable event.

#105. South Korea Faces Fresh Push To Delay Crypto Gains Tax Until 2029

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

South Korea is approaching another decision point on its long-delayed cryptocurrency gains tax, with exchanges and policymakers preparing to discuss whether the January 2027 start date is realistic.

TL;DR: The country’s planned crypto tax has already been deferred three times. A new proposal would push implementation toward 2029, but no additional delay has been enacted.

Finance officials are expected to meet representatives of major domestic exchanges on October 20. The industry is arguing that the systems needed to handle different transaction types and calculate cost bases are still incomplete. A rushed launch, exchanges say, risks creating inconsistent tax treatment or driving activity to offshore platforms.

South Korea’s planned rate is commonly described as 22% after local tax is included, rather than a simple 20% all-in charge. The question now is less about whether crypto gains should ever be taxable than whether the supporting reporting infrastructure is ready for millions of transactions across different venues.

A lawmaker’s proposal would link the effective date to cross-border data sharing through the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, potentially moving the start to 2029. That measure requires legislative action; a meeting with exchanges cannot, by itself, change the law.

For investors, the current scheduled date remains January 2027 unless lawmakers decide otherwise. For exchanges, a later timetable could buy time to build reporting systems, but another postponement would also prolong policy uncertainty. South Korea has reached this crossroads before, which is why a proposed delay should not be reported as a settled outcome.

#106. World launches World ID suite for banks, makes Zoom deepfake check generally available

Get The Block’s latest crypto news and price alerts for the coins you follow, right in Chrome. Add our free extension here.

The identity project co-founded by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman named Bain Capital and VanEck Funds among its design partners but did not name a bank that has started using the product.

World Worldcoin (WLD), the identity project co-founded by Sam Altman, launched a version of its World ID verification product for banks and financial firms on Sunday, its first offering aimed at a specific industry.

World co-founder Alex Blania unveiled the product at the Money20/20 conference. The suite combines three existing products, which World said can help institutions guard against deepfake fraud and AI-driven impersonation across customer accounts, employee workflows and AI agents, per a press release.

The World ID app is an identity wallet that stores and presents what World calls "Proofs" about a user. World ID for Zoom lets people on a call confirm that the person they are speaking with is human and not a deepfake. World ID for Agents, which the release also refers to as AgentKit, lets a person delegate those Proofs to an AI agent that can then present them to a third-party platform.

World also said World ID for Zoom is now generally available and that Tools for Humanity, the main developer behind World, has joined Zoom's independent software vendor exchange program. Zoom began offering the feature in a limited beta in April as part of a broader World ID upgrade that also included a Tinder integration. World said it will also present the technology at Zoom's Zoomtopia conference and at Cloudflare Connect.

"As AI becomes increasingly prevalent in all aspects of our lives, enterprises are requesting individuals provide 'Proofs' about themselves to help mitigate fraud and increase trust," Tools for Humanity President Sandro Herbig said in the release. "World ID for banking and finance offers a suite of tools to add an AI-safe trust layer across their internal and external systems."

World said it is working with OpenExchange, Bain Capital, VanEck Funds and Outtake as design partners to "explore" how its technology can support banking and financial services. The release did not name a bank using the product or disclose pricing. VanEck was the only finance firm World named among testers of the Zoom beta in April, according to a World blog post.

The release cited a Deloitte forecast that AI-enabled fraud losses in the U.S. could reach $40 billion by 2027, up from an estimated $12.3 billion in 2023. World said more than 18 million people now hold a Proof of Human. In March, World said it had verified nearly 18 million people across more than 160 countries when it released AgentKit in beta using Coinbase's x402 protocol.

The launch follows World's release last month of World Money, a self-custody app with stablecoin payments available in more than 150 countries. In July, the World Foundation raised $52.5 million through a WLD token sale with a one-year lockup.

The Block has reached out to World for comment.

Core banking infrastructure now relies on digital payments, and Ripple is the frontrunner of this shifting landscape.

Ripple has teamed up with Cross River Bank to integrate its RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger directly into the bank’s proprietary Core Operating System.

The move, announced on October 15, positions RLUSD as a native payment rail alongside traditional options like ACH, wire transfers, and real-time payments.

Fintech partners of Cross River will now be able to access XRP native stablecoin RLUSD through a single API connection without needing to build or maintain separate blockchain infrastructure.

Customers can move seamlessly between U.S. dollars and RLUSD, settle cross-border payments and treasury transfers around the clock, and take advantage of the XRP Ledger’s near-instant settlement—typically 3 to 5 seconds at a fraction of a cent.

The partnership aims to give issuers and acquirers greater flexibility for intraday settlement while reducing latency in payment networks.

Cross River’s Head of Fintech Banking, Adam Goller, highlighted that businesses should not have to juggle multiple providers to move money globally, noting the integration expands existing stablecoin capabilities already under development at the bank.

RLUSD, which launched in late 2024 under a New York trust company charter, has grown past $2.5 billion in market capitalization, with more than $1 billion issued on the XRP Ledger.

RLUSD payments are becoming part of the banking infrastructure fintechs already use.We’re partnering with @CrossRiverBank to integrate RLUSD on the XRP Ledger into its core banking platform, providing 24/7 settlement within payment networks and greater flexibility to settle… pic.twitter.com/ZBLw9f40Oy

The stablecoin is purpose-built for institutional use and operates 24/7, free from traditional banking hours.

Markus Infanger, Senior Vice President of RippleX at Ripple, described the collaboration as a step toward making stablecoins a standard part of the banking infrastructure fintechs already rely on.

By combining regulated banking rails with the speed and efficiency of the XRP Ledger, the partnership simplifies real-time, cross-border money movement for businesses and their customers.

The service is currently available in a limited number of U.S. states as Cross River and Ripple continue expanding access. This XRP chain integration marks another concrete step in bringing institutional-grade stablecoin payments deeper into everyday banking operations.

Tom Lee’s Bitmine Adds $30 Million in Ethereum as Buying Nears Its Finish Line

Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept its weekly Ethereum buying streak alive, adding 12,535 ETH worth about $30 million, even as a market-wide selloff battered crypto prices and the firm closed in on the end of its accumulation.

The NYSE-listed company said Monday its holdings now total 6,041,481 ETH, valued at roughly $14.3 billion at a reference price of $2,365 per coin. That represents 4.9% of Ethereum’s 122.1 million token supply, leaving Bitmine, by its own count, 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, a target it calls the “Alchemy of 5%,” reached in just 15 months.

Lee pinned the recent weakness on a broad contraction in risk appetite, citing anxiety over AI funding and model safety, escalating U.S.-Iran tensions, midterm-election jitters, and rising global bond yields.

He argued that selloffs in AI and semiconductor stocks in markets like Korea and Taiwan, where crypto is widely held, spilled over into digital assets, and framed the dip as a historically attractive risk-reward entry when fundamentals stay strong.
