#111. Public companies object to OKX-ICE’s tokenized stock plan

Nine public companies objected to having their shares offered in tokenized form by OKX and ICE, testing whether platforms can create blockchain-based markets without issuer consent.

Nine listed companies have formally objected to having their shares offered in tokenized form on the proposed tokenized stock platform backed by OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

The companies included Cerebras Systems, AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave, Verizon Communications, Applied Optoelectronics, Broadcom and UnitedHealth Group, according to a Thursday notice by OKX and ICE.

The notice did not disclose the reason behind the objection. Under the Securities and Exchange Commission’s Sept. 17 innovation exemption announcement, tokenized venues must give issuers written notice and an opportunity to object before listing third-party tokenized stocks.

“Issuers aren’t objecting to the blockchain. They’re objecting to not knowing what happens to their price once it trades there,” Robin Nordnes, CEO of trading validation platform Raiku, told Cointelegraph. “On a public chain, the validator building the block sets the order. Until desks can measure their distance to that point, best execution is a promise, not a number.”

The objections highlight a potential hurdle for tokenized stocks and test whether crypto platforms can create blockchain-based markets for public company shares without issuer cooperation.

Cointelegraph has approached OKX for comment on the ramifications of the objection but had not received a response by the time of publication.

Companies need to see the “upside and a track record of efficient pricing,” Misha Putiatin, co-founder of collateral markets platform Symbiotic, told Cointelegraph, adding that more “real-world data would help everyone assess the benefits and risks.”

He said that additional institutional tokenization initiatives, such as the Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation’s (DTCC) tokenization services, could instill more confidence in tokenized offerings.

Related: Nasdaq-listed Tron sets up $200M ATM share offering to fuel TRX acquisitions

CoinShares’ senior research associate, Luke Nolan, said the objection does not amount to a rejection of tokenization generally, but mostly against being tokenized without consent. He told Cointelegraph:

Nolan said the concerns are valid, adding that market participants have previously taken advantage of specific market mechanics to cause “squeezes” or “short-term swings” in the underlying asset’s price.

#113. Crypto.com, Novig sue Missouri over sports event contracts; Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood hold off

Get The Block’s latest crypto news and price alerts for the coins you follow, right in Chrome. Add our free extension here.

Two of the six companies Missouri's attorney general ordered to stop offering sports event contracts went to federal court on Friday. Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Underdog have not filed suit.

Crypto.com's prediction market exchange and Novig sued Missouri officials in federal court on Friday, asking judges to bar the state from enforcing its sports wagering laws against their event contracts as cease-and-desist deadlines set by Attorney General Catherine Hanaway ran out.

Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood and Underdog received the same letters in September. None of the four had filed suit in Missouri's Eastern or Western federal districts as of Sunday, according to a review of court records by The Block. The four firms did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Block.

Hanaway sent the letters on Sept. 16 and 17, giving each operator 30 days to stop offering sports event contracts to Missourians or get a license from the Missouri Gaming Commission, which has overseen legal sports wagering since voters approved it in November 2024, and pay the state's 10% wagering tax. Her letter to Crypto.com also said the platform lets users as young as 18 trade, while Missouri’s minimum age for sports betting is 21.

"Companies cannot repackage sports bets as 'event contracts' to evade Missouri law," Hanaway said on X.

North American Derivatives Exchange, the CFTC-registered exchange behind Crypto.com's OG prediction markets platform, filed its lawsuit in the Western District of Missouri. The suit argues that the Commodity Exchange Act gives the CFTC "exclusive jurisdiction" over its contracts and preempts state gambling law, and it seeks a declaratory judgment and a permanent injunction.

The complaint says Hanaway "incorrectly addressed" her letter to Foris DAX, Inc. instead of the exchange. It also says obtaining a sports betting license is not an option, since Missouri's constitution allows only two direct mobile sports wagering licenses and both have been awarded.

Novig, which has sued officials in several other states including Wisconsin, filed its lawsuit in Missouri's Eastern District through its exchange operator, Ludlow Exchange LLC. Novig's suit asks for a preliminary and permanent injunction.

The prediction market, known for its partnership with the New York Mets and its viral advertisement featuring actress Sydney Sweeney, argues the court should grant a preliminary injunction to preserve the status quo while the 8th Circuit, which covers Missouri, hears an appeal on the same question in a Kalshi case from Iowa.

Other federal appeals courts have split on the question of whether federal law preempts state gambling laws for sports event contracts, with the 6th and 9th Circuits ruling against Kalshi and the 3rd Circuit siding with it.

Kalshi was the first of the six companies to respond to Hanaway's letters, and the attorney general's office described "ongoing discussions" with the company, Spectrum News reported on Oct. 2. Underdog sued Connecticut last month over a similar crackdown but has not taken Missouri to court.

Crypto.com, Novig and the Missouri attorney general’s office also did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

#114. Kraken Parent Payward Moves Into European Banking With Saldo Deal

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Payward, the company behind crypto exchange Kraken, has agreed to acquire Lithuania-based Saldo Bank, taking a route into European banking that goes beyond obtaining another exchange registration.

TL;DR: The proposed acquisition would give Payward an existing licensed banking operation in Europe. The deal remains subject to regulatory approval and is expected to close in 2027.

Saldo provides banking products including loans and deposits. Bringing it into Payward would potentially put cash accounts, crypto assets and lending under a more connected product offering, rather than forcing customers to move between a separate crypto venue and their bank every time they need to borrow, spend or settle funds.

This is an important difference from a cryptocurrency firm simply partnering with an external payments provider. Ownership of a bank brings a regulated operating business, supervisory obligations and a different level of responsibility for customer money. Payward will not acquire unrestricted banking powers across Europe merely by signing the purchase agreement; the necessary approval and post-acquisition controls are still ahead.

The European push also fits a wider industry pattern. Crypto companies are pursuing banking relationships and charters as tokenized securities, stablecoins and conventional financial accounts become more closely linked. Existing lenders, meanwhile, are building crypto products of their own.

For Kraken users, the immediate message is about direction rather than a product they can use today. A completed acquisition could eventually make financing and fiat services feel less fragmented. Until regulators approve the transaction and the integration is completed, the promised benefits remain plans rather than available services.

Ripple is preparing for its next big event, Swell, scheduled for October 27 to 29, 2026, in New York.

Ripple senior software engineer Vito Tumas shared a countdown to the Swell event in an X post, saying "one week to go" and highlighting the technology driving AI breakthroughs in mathematics and its potential applications for securing the XRP Ledger.

One week to go! Technology driving AI breakthroughs in maths applied to secure XRP Ledger! @CommonPrefix , @RippleSwell

Tumas will be participating in the Swell event alongside Dejan Cabrilo, staff software engineer at Common Prefix, to discuss "Proof Over Trust: Formally Verifying the XRP Ledger."

#116. Bitcoin mining offshoot Nscale loses Microsoft AI deal as power delay stretches into 2030s

Technology giant Microsoft MSFT$533.48·Market Closed walked away from a planned U.K. AI data center run by Nscale, a company spun out of bitcoin BTC$82,836.58 mining, after the local grid operator said it may not be able to power the site for a decade.

The site in Loughton, Essex, about 6 miles northeast of London, was meant to house 23,040 Nvidia chips and supply 50 megawatts of computing to Microsoft’s Azure cloud by early 2027, according to the Guardian, which followed initial reporting by the Financial Times. UK Power Networks, which runs the local grid, told Nscale there may not be enough capacity until the early-to-mid 2030s.

Nscale announced the project last year alongside Microsoft, Nvidia NVDA$217.02·Market Closed and OpenAI. When the Guardian visited in February, the site was still a working scaffolding yard. Nscale has since cleared the location and is looking at other ways to bring in power. It said its other Microsoft contracts remain in place.

Nscale grew out of Arkon Energy, which built sites for bitcoin mining. Its founder, Josh Payne, took that experience in locking down land and power and turned it into a business selling computing to AI companies. Much of the listed mining industry is now running that playbook.

When CoinDesk looked at the industry shift in March, public miners had announced more than $70 billion in AI and high-performance computing contracts. They had also cut their combined bitcoin holdings by more than 15,000 BTC from their peaks, partly by selling coins to pay for the buildout.

Mining was already getting squeezed then. The report put the average listed miner’s cash cost to produce one bitcoin near $80,000 in the fourth quarter of 2025, and bitcoin was trading around $70,000 by March.

AI contracts pay steadily for years, but the sites are far more expensive to build. Estimates suggest an AI-ready facility runs $8 million to $15 million per megawatt, compared with roughly $700,000 to $1 million for bitcoin mining, and AI customers expect the servers to stay up around the clock.

The money also takes time to show up. In its latest mining report, fund manager CoinShares counted more than 4 gigawatts of AI capacity under contract across the miners it tracks, with only about 550 megawatts actually billing customers. Contract backlogs topped $100 billion, while annualized AI revenue stood at just over $1 billion.

Unless Nscale finds its own power or gets the grid to move a lot faster, the site it just cleared could sit idle for years.

Meanwhile, Britain’s grid queue is long. Energy regulator Ofgem says data center projects have requested connections totaling about 73 gigawatts of demand. It is weighing tougher rules because some applicants may never build, which holds up projects that are ready to go.

#118. Strategy Buys $22M in Bitcoin, Buys Back $193M of STRC

Strategy Buys $22M in Bitcoin, Buys Back $193M of STRC

Strategy bought 267 BTC for $22.1 million last week and repurchased $193.1 million of its STRC preferred stock, the company said on Monday.

The Bitcoin treasury firm paid an average of $82,900 per coin, including fees, between October 12 and 18, according to an SEC filing. That compares with $86,194 a coin for the 250 BTC it bought the week before, Decrypt reported. Strategy now holds 848,517 BTC, acquired for a total of $64.02 billion at an average of $75,446 per coin.

Strategy has repurchased $193M of $STRC and acquired 267 $BTC. As of 10/18/26, we hold 848,517 BTC and $5.3B of USD Assets. We have also increased the size of our Digital Credit Securities Repurchase Program from $2.0B to $3.0B. $MSTRhttps://t.co/4o0bQBaTb0

The purchase is in line with last week's $21.5 million buy, and a fraction of the $142.7 million Strategy spent on Bitcoin in the last week of September.

Strategy co-founder Michael Saylor had hinted at the purchase in a tweet on Sunday, writing: "We found room for more orange."

Strategy paid for the purchase with $22 million raised by selling 140,872 shares of its MSTR common stock through its at-the-market offering program, plus $0.1 million of cash. It sold none of its preferred stock during the week.

The company bought back 1,938,780 shares of STRC, its variable-rate Stretch preferred stock, using $193.1 million of what it calls USD Cash, money set aside for general purposes including buying Bitcoin.

Strategy's board also raised the total authorized under its digital credit securities repurchase program, which covers its preferred stock, to $3 billion from $2 billion. Last week's buyback had left $354.8 million in the program; after this week's purchases and the increase, $1.16 billion remained available as of October 18. A separate program to buy back MSTR common stock has $1 billion left.

The company also used $45.5 million from its USD Reserve, which is meant to cover preferred dividends and interest on its debt, to pay dividends. As of October 18, the reserve held $4.83 billion and USD Cash $447.3 million, down from $4.88 billion and $640.5 million a week earlier.

The repurchase extends a run of weekly STRC buybacks. Strategy bought back $192.4 million of the stock the previous week, and $176 million the week before that, as it bought $29 million in Bitcoin and posted a $21 billion third-quarter gain. In the last week of September, it repurchased $151.7 million of STRC as it took its holdings to a then-record 847,666 BTC.

The company is also facing possible removal from MSCI's widely tracked equity indexes. On October 15, the index provider finalized a rule that treats "non-operating companies," those whose balance sheets are dominated by a single asset, as ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30. MSCI will publish the list of affected companies on November 11.

Removal would force funds that track the indexes to sell the affected shares. Saylor had urged MSCI to drop what he called a "discriminatory" rule.

#119. AI Predicts Bitcoin Shrugs Off $110 Oil as Last Year’s Sellers Quietly Disappear

AI Predicts Bitcoin holds $82,000 through a $110 oil shock as exchange inflows from last year’s buyers quietly collapse 86%.

AI Predicts Bitcoin holds the $82,000 area through a geopolitical shock that would normally have moved it: the supply that used to meet every rally has stopped arriving on exchanges. BTC trades at $82,198, up 0.21% over 24 hours, with market cap at $1.65 trillion.

The news flow says this should be a worse day. Brent crude pushed above $110 after the United States warned Americans in twelve Middle Eastern countries to prepare for cancelled flights and closed airspace, with alerts saying hostilities could spread and that Iran and its allies may target US interests. Oil moved roughly two dollars in a matter of hours.

BREAKING: 🇺🇸 Brent crude oil surges above $110 as the US warns Americans in 12 Middle East countries to prepare for cancelled flights and closed airspace.

The alerts say hostilities could spread, and Iran and its allies may target US interests including American businesses. pic.twitter.com/0Hszo1ty6e

— Bull Theory (@BullTheoryio) October 19, 2026

Bitcoin barely registered it. The move over the same period was a fraction of a percent, and the current four hour candle is down 0.52% after trading between $82,071 and $83,009.

One number does stand out. Volume rose 84.8% to $24.7 billion while price went nowhere, which means a considerable amount of stock changed hands without either side gaining ground.

The explanation for that stability sits in exchange inflow data rather than in sentiment. CryptoQuant tracks what happens to coins that were bought six to twelve months ago, which in practice means the cohort that accumulated through the strongest stretch of 2025. The question is simple: when those holders move their coins, do the coins go to an exchange, which usually means they are being sold, or somewhere else.

For most of this year the answer was that they were selling heavily. In the thirty days to June 17, some 63,800 BTC from that cohort landed on exchanges, which was 40.4% of everything the group moved. The following window brought 46,800 BTC at 30.9%.

Then the pattern broke. The share fell to 9.8% by mid August, to 3.7% by mid September, and sits at 4.4% in the window ending October 15, representing 9,100 BTC.

That is a decline of roughly 86% in absolute terms from the June peak. The holders who had been distributing into every advance for the first half of the year have largely finished, and what reaches exchanges now is a small fraction of what used to.

It explains why a week of genuinely difficult macro news has produced a sideways market rather than a broken one. The marginal seller has thinned out, so each piece of bad news has less supply behind it to convert into a decline.

EXPLORE: Is MARA Preparing Another Bitcoin Sale After 1,000 BTC Moved to Exchanges?

The data above describes a market where fewer and fewer coins are moving anywhere at all. That is supportive for price in the short run, and it is also a fair description of what Bitcoin asks of the people who own it, because holding is more or less the only thing the asset is built to do. Coins that stay off exchanges tend to stay out of everything else as well, since the network settles slowly and offers no native programmability of its own.

That gap is what Bitcoin Hyper ($HYPER) targets. The project describes itself as a Bitcoin Layer 2 with Solana Virtual Machine integration, intended to bring smart contracts and faster execution to the existing network rather than to a separate chain.

Stated features include low latency Layer 2 processing and a decentralised canonical bridge for Bitcoin transfers. The presale is priced at $0.0136875, with more than $33 million reported raised.

Research Bitcoin Hyper before making any decision.

The flat reaction today is not the same as no reaction at all, and this is the part worth watching into next week. Crude at $110 is an inflation input before it is anything else. It feeds into transport, manufacturing and energy costs, and those costs show up in producer prices first. September PPI already came in at 6.3% against a 5.3% forecast, missing by a full point and reaching its second highest reading since November 2022. September CPI arrived at 3.7%.

An oil shock on top of that makes the October data harder to call, and the Federal Reserve meets on October 29 with a rate increase still on the table. The transmission takes weeks rather than hours, which is precisely why the market can absorb the headline today and still be dealing with it in November.

Selling pressure extended beyond the reported institutional deposit, with ENA’s spot and derivatives markets showing similar conditions.

According to CryptoQuant, Ethena’s Spot Taker Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) showed seller dominance at press time. This indicated that aggressive spot sell orders exceeded aggressive buy orders over the observed period.

Meanwhile, Futures Taker CVD also showed seller dominance, reflecting similar activity across leveraged markets.

Together, these readings supported a bearish outlook for Ethena. Buyers would need to absorb that selling pressure to reduce the risk of further weakness.

ENA’s derivatives positioning, on the other hand, presented a different story despite the persistent seller dominance.

#121. Verizon & Ericsson Complete First Outdoor 6G Test in 7 GHz

Home » Blitz news » Verizon & Ericsson Complete First Outdoor 6G Test in 7 GHz

A landmark test at a Verizon commercial site transitions next-gen network architecture from lab simulations to live field conditions.

Wireless carrier Verizon Communications Inc. (NYSE: VZ) and telecom vendor Ericsson (NASDAQ: ERIC) have completed what they cite as the world’s first outdoor pre-standard 6G field call in the 7 GHz spectrum band. The milestone was officially announced on October 15.

The test took place at a Verizon commercial network site in Concord, California, taking early-stage 6G proof-of-concept technology out of controlled laboratory environments and placing it into real-world radio frequency conditions.

According to the announcement, the field trial utilized Ericsson’s 6G proof-of-concept hardware running a pre-standard protocol stack over a continuous 400 MHz carrier in the 7 GHz centimeter-wave band.

The cell site base station was housed directly within a standard Verizon commercial site shelter.The mobile user equipment was placed inside a mobile test enclosure measuring approximately 12 by 8 feet. The enclosure featured diverse wall and window materials to evaluate signal loss.

The companies said further testing will examine how 6G signals travel from outdoors into buildings, including the effects of walls, windows, foliage and other obstacles. They are also evaluating coverage, throughput, latency, connection stability and other radio characteristics.

The milestone represents technical validation rather than a commercial product launch. Verizon and Ericsson still need to analyze the test results, refine the technology and align development with emerging 6G standards.

Commercial 6G deployment is generally anticipated around 2030, although standards and implementation details remain under development.

The companies point to potential future uses including AI-native network services, immersive communications, industrial automation and robotics.

This trial represents a shift in 6G development from theoretical simulations to field validation. For investors and industry watchers, the test underscores long-term spectrum and infrastructure positioning for both companies without altering near-term financial metrics.

#122. Strategy buys $22M in Bitcoin, repurchases $193M in STRC

Strategy added 267 Bitcoin to its holdings as it bought back 1.94 million STRC shares and boosted its preferred stock buyback program to $3 billion.

Michael Saylor’s Strategy, the world’s largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder, continued buying Bitcoin last week while spending nearly nine times as much repurchasing its preferred stock.

Strategy bought 267 Bitcoin for $22.1 million at an average price of $82,900 between Oct. 12 and Oct. 18, bringing its holdings to 848,517 BTC, according to a Monday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

The company also repurchased 1.94 million shares of its Stretch (STRC) preferred stock for $193.1 million and increased its digital credit securities buyback authorization to $3 billion from $2 billion.

The latest transactions extend a trend of management spending more on preferred stock repurchases than Bitcoin purchases, even as Saylor expects a return to a Bitcoin bull market.

Strategy funded its latest Bitcoin purchase primarily through $22 million in proceeds from selling 140,872 shares of its common stock, MSTR, while using existing cash for the STRC repurchases.

The company has spent $459.2 million repurchasing STRC shares so far in the fourth quarter, more than six times the $72.3 million it spent acquiring 851 Bitcoin over the same period.

Related: Strategy conditionally declares daily dividends as STRC hovers below $100

STRC is a variable-rate preferred stock designed to pay regular dividends. Strategy has previously said it intends to repurchase shares trading below their $100 stated value to help support the stock’s price.

The company reported a $4.83 billion USD Reserve to support preferred stock dividends and debt interest payments, alongside $447.3 million in separate USD Cash holdings.

The heavier spending on STRC buybacks comes as Saylor expressed optimism about Bitcoin’s outlook during a discussion at ParaFi Investor Day on Saturday.

“We’re moving back into a bull market,” Saylor said, pointing to Bitcoin’s recovery above its 200-day simple moving average, a widely followed indicator of longer-term price trends.

Saylor identified restrictive trade, foreign and monetary policies as headwinds for BTC, while highlighting growing bank adoption and the tokenization of traditional financial assets as potential drivers.

Ahead of Monday’s Nasdaq open, MSTR shares were trading more than 2.5% higher in premarket activity, according to Yahoo Finance. The shares closed Friday down about 9.6%, at $138.83 apiece. STRC shares also gained around 0.8% in premarket trading to $98.45, after falling 1.8% on Friday.

#123. Cysic suspends bridge after attacker mints tokens and moves $727,000 to Ethereum

Get The Block’s latest crypto news and price alerts for the coins you follow, right in Chrome. Add our free extension here.

Onchain records show the attacker minted 10 million CYS tokens, sold 7.2 million of them, bridged the proceeds off BNB Chain and received 306.6 ETH on Ethereum before Cysic blacklisted the address.

An attacker minted 10 million CYS tokens on BNB Chain by exploiting Cysic's cross-chain bridge on Saturday, the project confirmed. The attacker managed to sell 7.2 million of the unauthorized tokens and bridge about $727,000 in proceeds to Ethereum before the project blacklisted the attacker's receiving address, freezing the remaining 2.8 million tokens, according to onchain records reviewed by The Block.

Cysic, founded in 2022, builds specialized hardware and runs a Layer 1 network for generating zero-knowledge proofs. The company raised a $6 million seed round led by Polychain Capital in 2023. Cysic's bridge moves tokens, including CYS, between the Cysic chain and other networks such as BNB Smart Chain and Base.

The Cysic Foundation said in an incident report posted to X on Sunday that the attacker "gained unauthorized access to a database used by services supporting the bridge and exploited a vulnerability in the relevant processing logic to submit a fraudulent mint message." Cysic said it suspended the bridge and tasked a security firm, which it did not name, with investigating and tracing the funds.

The foundation said the incident was confined to the bridge's message-processing and minting functions and did not affect the Cysic mainnet. "Existing user assets were not stolen," the foundation said. Cysic has not disclosed a dollar figure for its losses, noting that the number of tokens minted "does not, by itself, represent the final loss in U.S. dollar terms."

The attacker's unauthorized mint took place at 8:31 a.m. ET on Saturday, per onchain data. BscScan records show the receiving address began moving CYS five minutes later, sending out 7.2 million tokens in 26 transfers across 15 transactions by 8:59 a.m. ET.

The address sold the tokens in two rounds. Between 8:36 and 8:41 a.m. ET, it sold 5.65 million CYS in 11 transactions for a combined 588,315 USDT, or about 10 cents per token. Between 8:57 and 8:59 a.m. ET, it sold the remaining 1.55 million CYS in four transactions for about 220 BNB.

Twelve of the 15 transactions were routed through OKX’s DEX aggregator, which split the orders across exchanges including PancakeSwap.

Cysic blacklisted the address in the CYS token contract at 9:47 a.m. ET, according to its report and onchain records, meaning the attacker's remaining 2.8 million CYS holdings can no longer be transferred. The blacklist landed 76 minutes after the initial exploit transaction, and 48 minutes after the attacker's address stopped sending out tokens.

At 8:44 a.m. ET, the address sent 100,000 USDT to a BridgersSwap contract operated by cross-chain swap service SWFT, and about a minute later received 40.88 ETH on Ethereum from a SWFT contract. It sent the remaining 488,315 USDT to cross-chain protocol Mayan in six transfers between 8:46 and 8:53 a.m. ET.

After the second round of sales, the address bridged its BNB as well, sending 80 BNB through Mayan at 9:05 a.m. ET and 139 BNB through deBridge a minute later.

On Ethereum, the address received seven payouts from Mayan totaling about 224.66 ETH and a 41.05 ETH payout from deBridge, with the last arriving at 9:06 a.m. ET, Etherscan records show. Including the SWFT transfer, the address received about 306.6 ETH, worth roughly $727,000 at Sunday's ETH price of about $2,372.

The address then sent 306.52 ETH in five transfers to a second wallet by 9:11 a.m. ET. That wallet, which first received funds about two hours before the mint, held about 309.5 ETH as of Sunday morning. Cysic's blacklist applies only to CYS on BNB Chain and does not affect the ether.

Cysic said the bridge will remain closed until a security review is complete, and that it will publish a follow-up report on verified losses and its efforts to trace the funds.

The Block has reached out to Cysic and its PR representatives for comment.

#126. German Savings Banks Begin Crypto Trading Rollout Inside Sparkassen App

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Germany’s Sparkassen savings-bank group is beginning a phased cryptocurrency-trading rollout inside its existing banking app, taking an asset class it once treated cautiously into a familiar retail-finance setting.

TL;DR: The first participating Sparkassen banks are offering crypto trading from October 19. The rollout is gradual, with 30 to 40 institutions expected to join each month, and is handled through DekaBank.

There is no national switch that turns the service on for every customer at once. Each regional savings bank decides when to participate. The group’s association told German news agency dpa that the opening selection includes Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana and Polygon, with a substantial number of interested institutions expected to be connected during the first half of 2027.

DekaBank is providing the service with Börse Stuttgart involved in custody arrangements. Customers can access the product through the Sparkassen app instead of creating a separate account at a crypto exchange. That convenience is central to the strategy, but the banks say the product is intended for customers making their own trading decisions rather than for a mass marketing drive.

The cautious messaging is deliberate. Sparkassen continues to describe cryptocurrencies as highly speculative and warns of steep volatility and total loss. Traditional savings products remain its preferred route for broad long-term wealth building.

This is a meaningful change for the German retail market nonetheless. Banks built on deposits and household relationships are responding to demand that previously went to specialist exchanges and mobile-first financial apps. How quickly individual branches opt in will matter more than the headline customer reach of the entire network.

#128. Morning Minute: Crypto Rebounds as 'Black Monday' Looms

Morning Minute: Crypto Rebounds as 'Black Monday' Looms

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Thirty-nine years ago today, the Dow fell 22.6% in a single session. Nobody saw it coming, and the notorious “Black Monday” turned into trading history.

Crypto enters that anniversary bruised but not broken. Bitcoin sits at $82,161, down just 1.4% on the week and actually up about 1% over the last 30 days. That’s the good news and it’s nearly the only good news.

Everything else got hit harder. Ethereum fell 5.3% to $2,415. BNB dropped 3.3%, Solana 6.2%, XRP 7.2%, Dogecoin 9.4%, Hyperliquid 8.6%, Zcash 13.2%. Across the majors, the average decline outside Bitcoin was 7.5%—roughly five times what BTC gave up.

Further out it gets ugly. Starknet lost 45% on the week, LayerZero 24%, Pump.fun 22%, Ethena 20%, Fetch 20%, Midnight 19%, Canton 18%, Jupiter 18%, Filecoin 17%, Raydium 18%. The top twelve weekly losers averaged losses of more than 20%. And all of this happened in just seven days.

The ETFs bled out as well. Spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $228.4 million across the week, Ethereum ETFs $320.1 million, for a combined $548.5 million. For October, the two complexes have now bled $1.86 billion. Ethereum’s situation is the more fragile one: $14.5 billion in net assets against $12.9 billion of cumulative inflows leaves barely $1.6 billion of cushion before the entire product line is underwater on a mark-to-market basis.

But for context, what turned a bad Friday into Black Monday back then was automated selling feeding automated selling, with no circuit breakers to interrupt it. Equities have those now, and Korea’s Kospi actually tripped one last week. Crypto has none. It trades through the weekend, through the open, through everything, and we already watched what that looks like on October 10, 2025 when the liquidation cascade repriced the whole market in hours.

The setup today is the opposite of a cascade. Slow bleed, orderly exits, Bitcoin holding while the tail gets cut off—and over the weekend, a modest bid returning across the board. And there is broad concern for a “Black Monday” occurring today. Which very likely in itself means it won’t happen. Crashes don’t occur when everyone is expecting them and ready with cash on the sidelines.

The bears may want a Black Monday, but they are very unlikely to get it. At least today…

#130. Will Chainlink’s 431900 LINK Reserve haul outweigh ETF withdrawals?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Strategic reserve accumulation can cut both ways.

On one hand, new additions can fuel short-term speculation, with traders betting on a potential supply squeeze.

On the other hand, continued accumulation could bolster a token’s long-term narrative by anchoring token demand to actual network revenue and adoption.

Chainlink is now at the center of this debate.

Notably, its reserve has increased its holdings of the native token by 89,200 LINK, worth $1.11 million, taking total holdings to 6.29 million LINK. In fact, over the past 30 days, it has accumulated another 431,900 LINK worth $5.41 million.

The catch? These tokens aren’t being spent on network development right now.

As the chart above shows, not a single LINK token has left the Chainlink Reserve.

And that is because, from a technical perspective, the prolonged accumulation could create a supply-demand imbalance on the market. Should buying pressure come on while the holdings are still rising, there is a possibility of a scarcity-driven rally.

Notably, Chainlink’s [LINK] 27% rise in September adds weight to the bullish case, as the Reserve has been accumulating 431,900 LINK worth nearly $5.41 million over the last 30 days.

However, does this make LINK’s recent momentum more speculative than fundamentally-driven?

Analysts believe LINK’s supply dynamics could help set the stage for a new all-time high.

LINK has a maximum supply of 1 billion tokens, with approximately 767 million currently circulating. The remaining 233 million represent a potential supply overhang, although their market impact depends on when they enter circulation.

At 6.29 million LINK, the reserve held roughly 0.82% of circulating supply. Its purchases could absorb some supply, but their scale remains modest.

That said, analysts flagged that reserve holdings remained small relative to overall supply. ETF purchases also offer no guarantee of sustained demand.

On the 16th of October, spot LINK ETFs recorded $397,000 in net outflows, only their third net-outflow day.

One negative session does not establish a lasting institutional retreat. It does, however, show that ETF demand can reverse.

Therefore, for LINK to reclaim its $52.70 all-time high, demand must grow fast enough to absorb new supply and support a market cap of roughly $40 billion at today’s circulating supply.

In this context, while Chainlink’s Q3 surge was supported by fundamental factors, its 27% increase seems to be primarily driven by speculation surrounding scarcity.

Until institutional investors absorb the bulk of supplies, it is possible that further gains will continue to be propelled by similar narratives rather than actual demand for the asset itself.

Chainlink’s Reserve added 431,900 LINK worth $5.41 million in 30 days.

LINK’s 27% September rally may be driven more by supply-squeeze hype than strong institutional demand.

World Liberty Financial’s USD1 stablecoin has shed over $400 million in market capitalization over the past two weeks, driven by large redemptions on Ethereum and BNB Chain.

On Monday, CoinGecko data showed USD1’s market capitalization at about $4.02 billion, down from $4.43 billion on Oct. 6. That’s a decline of approximately $401 million, or 9.1%. World Liberty Financial’s proof-of-reserves dashboard separately showed approximately $4.01 billion in reserves.

The decline extends a period of concentrated redemptions on Ethereum and BNB Chain, according to blockchain research firm Onchain Benchmark. The research platform found that nearly $200 million in BNB Chain redemptions originated from a single unidentified address, although they could not establish who controlled the funds or why they were redeemed.

Despite the redemptions, USD1 maintained its dollar peg throughout the period examined by Onchain Benchmark, trading between $0.998 and $1.000. Onchain Benchmark found no evidence of a sustained depegging event, indicating that the decline in circulating supply was not accompanied by a significant loss of the token’s dollar value.

USD1’s 30-day market cap chart. Source: CoinGecko

According to Onchain Benchmark, Ethereum accounted for $184.60 million in net USD1 redemptions across 63 token burns between Oct. 6 and Oct. 15. BNB Chain recorded $200.43 million across 12 burns.

On Ethereum, more than 99% of tokens sent for redemption passed through a wallet labeled BitGo, USD1’s current issuer and custodian, while the BNB Chain transfers from the unidentified address were made in batches of $30 million to $50 million.

Transfers between Ethereum and BNB Chain totaled less than $1 million, according to the report, suggesting the missing supply wasn’t simply shifted between those networks.

Nine U.S.-listed companies have objected to tokenized versions of their stock trading on OKXICE, the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange, according to a public notice from the venue.

The notice, dated Thursday, lists objections from Cerebras Systems (CBRS), AppLovin (APP), Applied Digital (APLD), Rocket Lab (RKLB), CoreWeave (CRWV), Verizon (VZ), Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI), Broadcom (AVGO) and UnitedHealth Group (UNH). It does not give reasons for any of the objections.

A spokeswoman for Applied Optoelectronics told the Wall Street Journal the fiber-optic maker objected because it was unsure how tokenization would affect its stock price, liquidity and volatility. She also cited the risk of investors being confused about the company's involvement in an offering it did not sponsor or endorse, and said the company saw no clear benefit "to AOI or our shareholders" that justified the uncertainty.

Eight of the nine objectors were among the 63 tickers OKXICE named on Oct. 4 as stocks it intended to offer. Cerebras was not on that list. OKXICE told the Journal it still plans to launch trading for dozens of U.S.-listed companies, including Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Tesla, JPMorgan Chase and Walmart.

OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo, the former governor of New York who took the role when the venture formed in June, said in a recent interview with the Journal that he expects companies to be skeptical of tokenizing their stock. He described the venue as a first step toward tokenizing securities.

Nasdaq said it would opt out of having its own shares tokenized under the SEC's framework, according to an FAQ on its website. A Nasdaq spokesperson told the Journal the company does not want its shares trading on a venue that does not display best prices in real time or report to the consolidated tape, and said the exchange remains committed to tokenization.

The SEC approved a Nasdaq pilot to trade tokenized equities, The Block reported earlier this year. Nasdaq has argued that tokenized trading outside the national market system could drift away from the broader market on price and transparency, according to the Journal. Citadel Securities raised similar concerns about a "shadow" U.S. equity market in a letter to the SEC last year.

OKXICE plans to operate under the SEC's innovation exemption, a five-year order issued Sept. 17 that lets tokenized securities venues trade tokenized versions of U.S.-listed stocks without registering as exchanges. When a third party rather than the company itself tokenizes a stock, the venue must notify the company at least 30 calendar days before trading begins, according to summaries of the order by law firms Sullivan & Cromwell and O'Melveny & Myers.

The company then has 30 calendar days to file a notice of issuer objection. If a company objects in time, their objection bars that venue from offering the stock token, though companies are not required to affirmatively approve listings — silence means the listing may proceed. An objection applies only to the venue that sent the notice, so each new venue starts its own 30-day clock.

Securitize President Brett Redfearn told the Journal that companies could object to one venue without rejecting tokenization altogether. Stocks tokenized by Securitize, which launched tokenized U.S. stocks on Oct. 8, are expected to trade on OKXICE, the Journal reported. Rodrigo Seira, a partner at law firm Cooley, told the Journal the SEC is using the exemption to gather information for its permanent rules.

OKXICE notified the SEC of its plans on Oct. 4, The Block previously reported. The venue will run permissioned liquidity pools on X Layer, a layer-2 network, with each stock paired against USDC, USDG or USDT. Traders must pass identity and sanctions screening and hold a non-transferable "soulbound" token to access the pools, according to the notice, which does not give a launch date.

AMC Entertainment has separately publicly criticized Robinhood's stock tokens, which Robinhood describes as debt securities issued by an offshore affiliate and not offered in the States. AMC CEO Adam Aron called the tokens tied to AMC "contemptible, outrageous, disgusting, detestable, inexcusable, vile" in a Sept. 3 post on X, and said AMC had no connection to them.

Robinhood SVP Johann Kerbrat called AMC's criticism "mostly a marketing stunt" in an interview with The Block earlier this month. He said the exemption's caps on volume and asset types would limit Robinhood's ability to bring its stock tokens to the U.S.

Morgan Stanley expects to support tokenized equities in the first quarter of 2027, The Block reported earlier this week.

The value of tokenized stocks totaled about $3.5 billion as of Oct. 15, up from about $680 million at the start of the year, according to The Block’s data.

OKXICE and the nine companies did not immediately respond to The Block's requests for comment.

CME Group has scheduled the introduction of Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap futures for October 19, giving institutional derivatives traders two more cryptocurrency markets to access through a regulated venue. TL;DR: CME previously announced BCH and UNI futures for an October 19 launch, subject to regulatory review. Standard and micro contracts are planned for both assets. Uniswap is a particularly interesting addition because its token sits in the decentralized-finance sector. The existence of a listed futures contract does not itself establish demand for a future exchange-traded fund, nor should a derivatives launch be treated as evidence that regulators have approved any spot ETF. CME says the planned additions respond to customer demand for risk-management tools. The exchange’s crypto product range already extends beyond Bitcoin and Ether, and the new contracts continue that approach. The remaining detail traders should watch is the exchange’s confirmation of regulatory clearance and live trading. A published target date is not the same as confirmation that every contract has begun trading. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

#136. Bitcoin whale moves $34 million in BTC it got in 2013 when coins traded at $131

A bitcoin BTC$82,836.58 wallet, dormant since 2013, has come back to life.

On Sunday, the wallet moved all 411.45 of its BTC to a new address, according to blockchain data from Arkham Intelligence. At today’s price of about $82,600 per coin, that stash is worth roughly $34 million. When the owner first acquired those coins, the entire balance was worth just $54,000.

This awakening is part of a broader trend of historic supply shifting wallets this month. Just a day prior, two other wallets dormant for over a decade moved a combined 417 Bitcoin, and the week before, a large whale wallet static since the pre-Covid crash migrated its funds.

The pattern is highly reminiscent of 2025, when isolated mega-whales repeatedly woke up from a prolonged slumber. Just like last year, these sudden movements of long-dormant supply tend to spark speculation about a potential sale. But, as was the case then, most of the coins have been moved to new private wallets, a sign of custodial maintenance rather than an impending market dump.

The specific wallet behind Sunday's move received the bulk of its funds, some 411 BTC, on Sept. 11, 2013. Back then the cryptocurrency traded around $131. Over the next 13 years, the owner didn't buy, sell, or move a single coin. They simply sat tight as the asset's value skyrocketed more than 600 times, holding through three halvings, the 2017 boom, the 2022 FTX collapse, and the launch of spot bitcoin ETFs in 2024.

While the owner remained completely inactive, the wallet itself did see some activity over the years. Dozens of tiny deposits trickled in, each worth less than a dollar. Several came from addresses that Arkham labels as phishing. It’s a common scam tactic known as “address poisoning.” Fraudsters send trace amounts of crypto ("dust") to high-value wallets, hoping the owner will accidentally copy the scammer's address from their transaction history during a future transfer.

At 18:23 UTC on Sunday, the owner sent the entire fortune to a new address, paying a transaction fee of just 337 satoshis, a fraction of a single cent.

So far, the funds have not been moved to an exchange. The new destination wallet has only received this single transfer and has not initiated any outgoing transactions. That lack of movement points to routine custodial housekeeping rather than a market sell-off.

The original 2013 wallet relied on an outdated address format, whereas the new destination utilizes SegWit (P2WPKH type), which is the modern standard that offers better security and lower transaction fees. Long-dormant holders frequently migrate to these upgraded formats to secure their assets before making any major financial moves.

Hoskinson also addressed whether Cardano had reached the point where its development could be considered complete, in response to a follower who asked him directly.

He explained that Cardano would then have the main components he wanted to build, including decentralized consensus, governance and development, its extended unspent transaction output (eUTXO) model, Plutus smart contracts and formal verification.

Hoskinson also pointed to the network’s independent node implementations and its ability to improve recursively, alongside the millions of people who hold ADA.

For context, Leios is designed to increase Cardano’s transaction capacity by changing how blocks are produced and validated. Development is ongoing, so Hoskinson’s statement describes the intended completion of the network’s core architecture, not the end of all future development.

#138. ‘Terrifying Precedent’: Dutch Hand US Data From Seized Anti-Fascist Server

‘Terrifying Precedent’: Dutch Hand US Data From Seized Anti-Fascist Server

A Dutch-based server belonging to an anti-fascist political group was seized by police in Amsterdam last week. It followed a request from U.S. authorities, the NL Times reported Saturday, after the Trump administration designated the group as a "global terrorist" organization.

The seized server belonged to Italian internet service provider Autistici/Inventati (A/I), an anti-capitalist and anti-fascist group which offered free email and web-hosting services for organizations and activists. Police seized the server from a data center in Amsterdam's eastern district, and Dutch authorities are now handing its data over to the U.S.

Privacy advocate Harry Halpin told Decrypt that "politically motivated server seizures" set a "terrifying precedent." And one legal expert questioned whether the Dutch considered their legal right to refuse.

Halpin, CEO of privacy infrastructure firm Nym, told Decrypt, argued that the targeting of Autistici/Inventati servers by the Trump administration was "due to their political beliefs," adding that, "The fact that the Dutch authorities co-operated with them to shut down a server means that the Netherlands is nothing more than a colony of the United States."

The U.S. designated Autistici/Inventati as a "Specially Designated Global Terrorist" in August, claiming that it operates the "digital infrastructure for violent Antifa cells and other far-left militants."

The designation prevents U.S.-based people and organizations from doing business with them. In turn, Autistici/Inventati disbanded as its users and donors faced potential repercussions.

One legal expert said the designation has no standing in the Netherlands and that another legal power was exercised.

"An FBI agent in Amsterdam has roughly the powers of a tourist," Yuriy Brisov, lawyer and partner at Digital & Analogue Partners, told Decrypt. "So states ask each other permission. For the United States and the EU states, the rulebook for asking is a Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty, or MLAT, signed in The Hague in 1981."

Brisov explained that everything is done "under Dutch law, by Dutch officers, with Dutch powers," but entirely at the request of the U.S. For that reason, he said, Dutch authorities seized the server and not the U.S.

Prosecutors operate on a “trust principle,” the legal expert told Decrypt, meaning they don’t assess whether the seizure is proportionate or whether the U.S. investigation actually needs the material.

However, Brisov said, the Dutch could choose to refuse the request if it "harms its essential interests, concerns a political offence, or amounts to double jeopardy." Seizure is also only allowed if the alleged conduct is a crime in both countries carrying more than a year in prison.

It is important to note that designating a group as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist doesn't require a conviction or a court to hear the case, Brisov added, and neither the Dutch government nor the European Union followed the U.S. designation.

"Here is the Dutch problem: Washington's label underpins the request, and the Netherlands does not share it," Brisov told Decrypt, questioning whether "anyone in The Hague asked the political-offence question" that Dutch law reserves for Minister of Justice and Security David van Weel personally. "Internet hosts are not normally liable for what their users do," Brisov noted, adding that the rule is written into both U.S. law and EU law through the Digital Services Act.

Halpin told Decrypt that the request should have been scrutinized due to its political nature.

"Any country that believes in sovereignty should push back against politically motivated server seizures," he said. "This shows that only a multi-jurisdictional setup with true decentralization, as attempted by many blockchain projects, is the only way to resist nation-state-level attacks on digital infrastructure."

#139. Qubic hit by major exploit – 87.1% of stolen funds frozen within hours

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

On the 17th of October, Qubic suffered a major exploit on its protocol. The exploit resulted from the protocol’s lack of randomness while generating seed values in some version of Apple’s products.

As a result, the attacker could drain over 2.9 billion QU tokens worth roughly $1.3 million. A total of 1404 wallets were compromised, and the whole process took less than two hours.

In simple words, the bug could allow an attacker to predict wallet seeds offline, without needing to compromise the Qubic protocol, the network, or individual devices in real time.

However, the bug was limited to wallet creation software and did not affect the overall Qubic protocol.

Recovery of lost funds will depend upon the Computer Quorum decision regarding frozen balances and will require coordination among those who have been impacted by the breach.

Meanwhile, hackers were able to transfer only 12.9% of the stolen QU into their new wallet account. This is because Qubic was able to freeze 87.1% of the stolen QU that hackers transferred into their new wallet account.

Additionally, validators were able to freeze the entire network at block 85,371,949. Thus, virtually all the stolen funds remain frozen. MEXC did eventually freeze the new wallet account containing the remaining 12.9% of stolen QU about an hour after its creation, limiting additional loss.

Qubic has made attempts to minimize the financial impact of the hack by limiting where money can flow from and to within the system. Despite that, ultimately they will need to devise a plan to recover the lost funds.

To prevent similar attacks, Qubic released wallet version 4.26.4. This upgrade would curb the seed-generation weakness, hence securing the platform from future attacks of the same manner.

Looking forward, broader adoption alongside independent testing will determine whether the patch closes the vulnerability.

Regaining user confidence in Qubic will depend upon how quickly and successfully the network returns to normal. However, there is no record of past transactions since all current activity on the network is zero and none of the existing addresses on the blockchain have any activity.

Once transactions resume, a steady increase in transactions and active addresses will prove that users are participating on the network once again. Healthy node participation will ensure that the network continues to operate smoothly and efficiently.

Additionally, exchange support for deposit and withdrawals must also exist before a “technical restart” occurs. If exchange functionality does not include accepting deposits and withdrawing QU, then even though a functional Qubic network exists, there will likely be very little activity.

[Update 11:30 UTC, Oct. 19 - Updates with comment from Penning Financial Services in the sixth paragraph.]

The European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) register added nine crypto-asset service providers (CASPs), including BingX, bringing the total to 375 unique providers.

The European Securities and Markets Authority’s (ESMA) Friday register update included crypto exchange BingX’s Austrian entity, MEGE zweite. It also listed the Italian subsidiary of YouHodler, a crypto lending platform offering yield products, with authorization for custody, crypto exchanges, order execution and transfers.

Both BingX and YouHodler announced their authorizations last week. BingX EU CEO Daniel Lai said the approval would allow the company to operate under a clear regulatory framework as it prepares to launch regulated services across the European Economic Area.

Other additions included Spain’s Prakma Markets, associated with the Goin crypto app, which operates a savings and investment platform.

New CASPs listed in ESMA’s MiCA register update on Friday. Source: ESMA

Germany’s additions included Openbank Deutschland, a subsidiary of Spanish banking group Banco Santander, alongside cooperative lenders VR-Bank Alb-Blau-Donau and VR Bank im südlichen Franken.

Denmark’s Penning Financial Services is no longer listed, despite appearing in register updates dating back to July 3. A spokesperson for Penning told Cointelegraph that its MiCA authorization remains unchanged and that it had received no communication from Denmark’s financial regulator about any changes. Cointelegraph has contacted ESMA and Denmark’s Financial Supervisory Authority for clarification but had not received a response at the time of publication.

The e-money token (EMT) register was unchanged at 50 entries representing 25 unique entities, while the asset-referenced token (ART) register remained empty. The register of non-compliant crypto-asset service providers (NCASPs) increased by five entries to 178.

Turkish Justice Minister Akın Gürlek confirmed on Saturday that Hex and PulseChain founder Richard Heart was detained in Istanbul, and said police seized $7.15 million in cash and six cold wallets in related searches.

#145. Ethereum Sets October 26 Hoodi Test For Glamsterdam Upgrade As 200M Gas Limit Nears

Ethereum’s next major upgrade has another date on the calendar, though it is not a mainnet launch. Developers have scheduled Glamsterdam to activate on the Hoodi test network on October 26, a further step in testing changes to how Ethereum produces blocks and accounts for execution costs. TL;DR: Glamsterdam is scheduled for Hoodi at 17:42:48 UTC on October 26. The testnet‘s gas limit will rise to 200 million at the same point, but Ethereum has not announced a mainnet activation date. The Ethereum Foundation says the upgrade will activate at Hoodi epoch 132,352, slot 4,235,264. It follows the upgrade’s October 6 activation on Sepolia, giving developers another environment to check software compatibility before choosing a date for the main chain. Two changes sit at the heart of Glamsterdam. Enshrined proposer-builder separation, or ePBS, moves the relationship between block proposers and builders into Ethereum’s protocol instead of relying as heavily on outside arrangements. Block-level access lists are intended to make it easier for clients to process and validate parts of a block in parallel. The upgrade also changes gas accounting, including how Ethereum charges for state creation and access. That matters to application developers whose contracts or tools rely on fixed assumptions about gas costs. Validators and node operators on Hoodi, meanwhile, will need compatible execution and consensus clients before the activation. A 200-million gas limit on a test network is an important engineering milestone, not a promise that mainnet capacity will instantly quadruple. The Hoodi exercise will help determine whether the planned changes behave as expected under real operating conditions. Mainnet users have no action to take yet. #146. Zcash developers plan a fix to keep ZEC swaps private from future quantum computers

Zcash is designed to make crypto payments private. But a future quantum computer could theoretically exploit a small gap in NEAR Intents, a cross-chain swapping service, to connect a user’s private ZEC transactions to their wallet, undermining that privacy.

Fortunately, the team behind Zakura, a newer version of the software that runs the Zcash network, is taking steps to address that. In a new engineering post, it proposed giving every ZEC swap made through NEAR Intents its own private key. The change would close a gap that a future quantum computer could use to piece together a user’s payment history.

NEAR Intents is a service that lets users swap tokens across different blockchains. When someone swaps private ZEC for USDC through it, the service posts one of their private Zcash addresses on NEAR’s public chain, so it knows where to send back any unused ZEC. That address goes up as soon as the deposit lands and stays there even if the swap goes through and no refund is ever needed.

Such addresses give away no information on today’s computers. Each Zcash address carries a public key built from the wallet’s viewing key, the secret a wallet uses to spot payments sent to it, using one-way elliptic-curve math similar to what protects bitcoin and ether wallets.

Ordinary computers can’t run that math in reverse, but a large enough quantum computer running Shor’s algorithm, a method published in 1994 for exactly that job, could theoretically work backward from the address to the key.

That’s the real threat hanging over Satoshi-era bitcoin, whose public keys already sit onchain for anyone to copy. Last week, Google said its Willow quantum chip had produced near-perfect versions of one of the components such an attack would burn through, a step toward a machine powerful enough to try it.

Quantum computers capable of that are still likely years away (and no one has a firm timeline for when one could be built), but it’s a problem developers across the industry are rushing to solve.

Zcash’s architecture creates its own problem. A Zcash wallet can generate many addresses that look unrelated, but they usually share one viewing key.

An attacker who cracks that key from a single published address could link every payment the account ever received and read the amounts and the private notes, or memos, attached to them.

Spending takes a separate key, so the funds themselves would stay safe. Zakura’s fix gives each swap its own viewing key and leaves the spending key with the user’s main account. An attacker who someday cracks a refund address on NEAR would see only the payments tied to that one swap.

The design also deals with a practical snag.

A wallet that has made hundreds of swaps would end up with hundreds of keys, and restoring it from a backup would mean scanning the entire Zcash chain with every one of them.

Zakura’s answer is a database the wallet can query privately using a technique called private information retrieval. The wallet asks where its refunds landed, and the database answers without learning which addresses the wallet asked about.

As such, no quantum computer has been demonstrated that can recover these keys. Zakura says wallets built on its open-source libraries, including Vizor, could add the feature in the coming weeks, with hardware wallets following once their firmware supports it.

That would put the fix in users’ hands ahead of the January target Zcash developers set earlier this month for quantum-resistant payments.

#147. Sam Altman's World Takes Proof-of-Human IDs to Banks, Citing $40B AI Fraud Risk

Sam Altman's World Takes Proof-of-Human IDs to Banks, Citing $40B AI Fraud Risk

World co-founder Alex Blania has unveiled World ID for banking and finance, a suite of tools that lets financial institutions confirm a real person is behind transactions, trades and customer requests, the company said on Sunday.

Bain Capital, OpenExchange, Outtake, Pantera Capital and VanEck Funds are initial design partners, according to World.

The offering is built on three cryptographic proofs available through the World ID app. Proof of Human establishes that someone is a real and unique person through a one-time visit to one of World's Orb devices. Proof of Presence uses a selfie liveness check on a phone, while Proof of Attributes confirms details such as nationality or age from a government ID, revealing only the requested information.

Banks could use the proofs to require a verified human to approve ACH and wire transfers, or to recover an account, without collecting documents or storing other personal data, World said. AgentKit, a developer toolkit still in beta, lets users delegate certain proofs to AI agents so they can transact on a person's behalf.

The suite also includes World ID for Zoom, which builds on the project's earlier integrations with Zoom and Tinder. Participants verified at one of the project’s Orb devices get a "Human Badge" on their video tile after a live selfie check, and hosts will soon be able to require verification in the waiting room before a call.

World pointed to the case of an employee at engineering firm Arup who wired about $25.6 million in early 2024 after a video call in which every other participant was a deepfake. Deloitte forecasts that AI-enabled fraud losses in the U.S. could reach $40 billion by 2027, up from $12.3 billion in 2023, the company noted.

More than 18 million people hold a Proof of Human ID, according to World, with the World Foundation raising $52.5 million this year to scale the network.

In 2024, an employee at engineering firm Arup transferred $25.6 million after joining a video call where every other participant was a deepfake. Since then, AI has advanced significantly and is making impersonation increasingly convincing, causing challenges for financial… pic.twitter.com/J06gnULw8H

World's iris-scanning model has faced pushback from regulators around the world over its handling of biometric data.

Hong Kong's privacy watchdog ordered the project to stop its iris-scanning operations in 2024, while later that year South Korea's privacy regulator fined the project $830,000. That December, Spain's data protection agency told it to delete all iris scan data.

Last year, a Kenyan court ordered it to delete biometric user data, and Brazil's data protection authority denied its appeal against a ban.

#149. France advances stablecoin tax, eyes self-custodial wallets and exit tax proposals

France’s National Assembly adopted a crypto tax amendment targeting certain stablecoin swaps, while separate proposals on exit taxes and self-custodial wallet reporting remain under consideration.

French lawmakers narrowly approved a new crypto tax amendment on Friday that could make crypto-to-stablecoin swaps taxable events starting in 2027.

France’s National Assembly adopted Amendment I-3898 on Friday, with 38 votes in favor, 37 against and 25 abstentions. The measure was initially introduced as committee amendment I-CF1826 by French MP Nicolas Sansu and adopted on Oct. 7.

The Assembly is scheduled to vote on the first part of the 2027 Finance Bill on Tuesday, according to its official schedule. Other crypto-related proposals remain under consideration, although it is unclear whether each will be debated or voted on that day.

If enacted, the stablecoin amendment would tax certain crypto-to-stablecoin swaps and change how the country calculates crypto capital gains tax.

French National Assembly advances Amendment I-3898 on crypto-to-stablecoin tax swaps. Source: assemblee-nationale.fr

Under the proposal, investors converting their Bitcoin (BTC) or other cryptocurrencies into stablecoins would trigger a tax on the gains, even without converting gains into fiat. The calculation would use the acquisition cost of the sold crypto asset and the weighted average purchasing price.

Related: Deutsche Bank prepares German crypto custody launch, eyes Asia: Report

Separately, the Assembly rejected a proposal on Friday to carry forward realized crypto losses for 10 years, with 18 votes in favor, 75 against and 3 abstentions.

French lawmakers are preparing to discuss other crypto-related proposals as part of next year’s budget. Amendment I-CF1822 proposes to extend France’s exit tax regime to cover unrealized gains when taxpayers with aggregate crypto portfolio values exceeding €800,000 ($895,000) transfer their residences abroad.

Lawmakers are also weighing amendment I-2701, which would require individuals to declare the holdings of the self-custodial wallets if their total value exceeded €100,000 ($112,000) in the relevant tax year.

As of Monday, both proposals remain under consideration for the 2027 Finance Bill.

#150. ‘XRP Community Is Tired’: Crypto Influencer Calls Out Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse Over Endless Partnerships and Lackluster XRP Price

Ripple may be racking up partnerships, but not everyone in the XRP community is celebrating. A prominent crypto influencer has publicly confronted Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse, voicing growing frustration among XRP holders who have waited years for the company’s expanding business footprint to translate into meaningful gains for the token.

The criticism came shortly after Ripple unveiled a new tie-up with global brokerage infrastructure provider DriveWealth. The collaboration is designed to strengthen digital asset services across payments, settlement, custody, and institutional financing, marking another step in Ripple’s push to expand its presence in traditional finance.

In a post on X, John Squire argued that XRP holders were growing weary of Ripple’s steady stream of partnership announcements without seeing tangible benefits for the token itself.

“The XRP community is tired,” Squire opined. “We’ve spent years watching Ripple announce partnership after partnership. Yet morale across the XRP community is at rock bottom. We believe in the vision, but people need to see that progress reflected in XRP itself. Hope needs results, Brad.”

His remarks reflect a recurring frustration among XRP investors who question why Ripple’s expanding business operations have yet to translate into stronger price performance for the payments-focused cryptocurrency.

At $1.31, XRP is down roughly 5.1% over the past 24 hours and nearly 30% since the beginning of the year. The token briefly climbed to $1.70 in August before surrendering those gains, leaving investors waiting for a sustained recovery.

XRP’s prolonged struggle to break into higher price territory has further tested holders’ patience, particularly as Bitcoin has climbed to six-figure valuations. For many XRP supporters, the central question is whether Ripple’s growing influence in the financial sector will eventually translate into meaningful upside for the token.

Ripple, meanwhile, continues to expand its institutional footprint through high-profile partnerships and multibillion-dollar acquisition deals, highlighting the growing gap between the company’s business momentum and XRP’s recent market performance.

Ripple has teamed up with DriveWealth to bring stablecoin settlement, cross-border payment capabilities, and digital asset custody to its brokerage infrastructure. The rollout will begin in Europe, with plans to extend the services to the U.S. market later.

The deal will leverage Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger, enabling DriveWealth clients to fund and manage collateral accounts using stablecoins that can be converted into cash almost instantly. The two companies are also exploring equity financing opportunities through Ripple Prime, potentially broadening the partnership beyond payments and settlement.

The DriveWealth deal adds to Ripple’s growing push to embed RLUSD into institutional financial services. Earlier this week, Standard Chartered introduced custody services for RLUSD on the XRP Ledger, while Ripple and LMAX Group previously agreed to expand institutional stablecoin adoption through a $150 million financing deal.

Ripple has also partnered with Stripe-owned Privy to bring embedded wallets to XRPL, giving developers a simpler way to integrate blockchain-based services into their applications.

These recent deals signal that Ripple’s ambitions stretch far beyond crypto payments. As RLUSD gains traction across institutional finance, the big question is whether this growing adoption will eventually translate into stronger demand for XRP and a lasting boost to its price.

#151. DriveWealth-Ripple Partnership Tests XRP Demand in RLUSD Settlement

DriveWealth’s Ripple partnership uses RLUSD for settlement, but its structure does not show that the deal creates meaningful XRP demand.

The latest Ripple news is a partnership with DriveWealth, which is integrating Ripple’s stablecoin infrastructure to support settlement in Europe, with plans to expand to the United States.

The announced structure lets clients fund and manage collateral accounts using stablecoins that convert to cash in near real time. The agreement does not require counterparties to purchase XRP. That makes the deal a potential institutional infrastructure milestone, not a clear new source of XRP demand.

This is not simply a stablecoin integration. It is a test of whether institutional use of Ripple’s rails can translate into demand for the network’s native token, and the disclosed mechanics do not establish that link. The distinction between RLUSD adoption and XRP demand is central to assessing what the partnership means for the token.

DriveWealth’s arrangement also illustrates why growth in a stablecoin’s use on XRPL does not automatically create meaningful XRP demand: RLUSD can serve as the settlement asset while the ledger processes it.

Global investing is evolving. The infrastructure behind it should too.

We're partnering with @DriveWealth across RLUSD settlement on the XRP Ledger, cross-border payments, custody and prime brokerage to modernize how money moves across global markets.

DriveWealth provides brokerage infrastructure used by trading applications, rather than operating only as a consumer-facing trading app. In its partnership announcement, the company said RLUSD on XRPL would support settlement in Europe, with a planned U.S. expansion. The announcement describes an integration plan, not a fully deployed service across those markets.

The intended funding mechanism is straightforward: clients use stablecoins to fund and manage collateral accounts, and those stablecoins convert to cash in near real time. That could reduce dependence on international bank wires, intermediary banks and transfer cutoff windows. The release also identifies Ripple Payments for cross-border fund acceptance and work with Ripple on digital-asset custody in Europe, with expansion to other markets planned.

Equity financing is a separate, exploratory workstream. DriveWealth and Ripple are exploring opportunities via Ripple Prime’s Delta One business; no products, volumes, dates, or financial terms were disclosed.  Those possibilities should not be treated as live financing facilities.

The critical distinction is that RLUSD is the dollar-denominated asset, XRPL is the ledger carrying it, and XRP is the ledger’s native token. The partnership announcement does not say participants must purchase XRP or use it as a bridge currency. A related institutional settlement use of RLUSD likewise highlights the role of the stablecoin as an asset in its own right, separate from the question of XRP’s function.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

DriveWealth CEO Naureen Hassan framed the funding challenge around matching the availability of capital to the company’s 24/5 trading operation. Her stated rationale was that cross-border transfer windows can leave clients waiting to move funds; the stablecoin integration is intended to help clients manage collateral when needed. Faster funding may improve the utility of DriveWealth’s brokerage infrastructure without requiring XRP to be the asset moved.

XRP still has a limited technical role in XRPL transactions. The primary analysis describes fees as small amounts of XRP that are deducted and destroyed, while accounts also require a minimal XRP reserve. It characterizes these amounts as fractions of one XRP per transaction and about one XRP per account, too small on their own to establish a substantial new source of token demand.

This Ripple news may benefit the company commercially if RLUSD circulation and use grow, because stablecoin issuers can earn income on the assets backing their tokens. XRP holders, however, do not receive Ripple’s reserve income or brokerage fees. More RLUSD activity could increase XRPL throughput, but that is not equivalent to more XRP being purchased or held.

The scale comparison also needs care. The primary analysis put RLUSD’s market capitalization at approximately $2.4 billion, compared with about $184 billion for Tether’s USDT and $72.6 billion for Circle’s USDC.

Those figures describe relative stablecoin scale; they do not establish why DriveWealth selected RLUSD, or show that the choice amounts to an endorsement of XRP.
