#317. Morning Minute: Google Clears a Major Quantum Hurdle, Bitcoin Still Safe

Morning Minute: Google Clears a Major Quantum Hurdle, Bitcoin Still Safe

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Eight days ago an Ethereum researcher told large holders to move their coins. Today Google published a result that makes him look less paranoid and more early.

Google Quantum AI cut a critical class of quantum errors roughly 40-fold on its Willow chip, per a new paper in Science. The technique attacks what may be quantum computing’s single biggest tax - producing the clean, single-use resources certain operations need, which by some estimates eats up to 95% of a machine’s capacity. Instead of building dedicated qubit factories to purify them, Google filters: inject a rough state, run it through a gauntlet of checks, throw out the 92% that fail. What survives hits 99.99% fidelity.

Nobody is draining wallets with this. Breaking an RSA-2048 key needs errors around one in 10 billion - about a million times cleaner than what Google just showed.

But researchers are moving closely. In 2019, cracking RSA-2048 was estimated to need 20 million noisy qubits. By 2025 that was under one million. A March 2026 Google whitepaper put Bitcoin’s elliptic curve cryptography at under 500,000 physical qubits. Willow has 105.

The irony this week is that Justin Drake’s actual fear wasn’t quantum at all. He thinks AI-driven mathematics breaks elliptic curves first, on ordinary hardware, in “months not years.” His advice: big holders should move funds to fresh addresses that have never signed a transaction, because signing exposes your public key. So crypto is being “attacked” on two fronts: quantum advancement and AI advancement.

With that said, key players are making moves and starting serious preparations. Coinbase spent this week arguing the migration has to start now. Sui is already running quantum-safe transactions on a test network. Ethereum, Zcash and Near all have plans to be quantum-resistant.

Crypto leaders will be prepared. But this was a reminder from Google that the tock is indeed ticking…

Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz has raised a security warning after receiving a suspicious notification on an Android device that appeared to come from the SecuX wallet app.

"Hey, SecuX wallet, it looks like your Android app sent me a notification that's a scam," Schwartz wrote.

An X user surprised by the development told Schwartz not to tap it. The Ripple CTO Emeritus said he had tapped it, probably out of curiosity, to see what would happen, and it launched the app normally. Things didn't appear unusual until he probed further and checked his notification history, which exposed the bait.

In his notification history, he saw a message that included a link to a scam page that required him to enter his 12/24 words.

The notification claimed, "Your funds may be at risk, critical vulnerability detected in SecuX wallet, verify your wallet immediately," alongside a link which Schwartz stated was fraudulent.

"I had to go to my notification history to see the message. The link goes to a scam page that asks you to input your 12/24 words," Schwartz wrote. Twelve- or 24-word phrases might refer to the wallet recovery phrase, highly sensitive information that allows anyone who obtains it to restore the wallet and gain control of its funds.

@JYoda @SecuXwallet I tapped on it to see what would happen and it launched the app normally. I had to go to my notification history to see the message. The link goes to a scam page that asks you to input your 12/24 words. (NEVER DO THAT!)

Schwartz strongly warned users against entering their 12- or 24-word phrases, saying, "Never do that," to highlight the importance of never disclosing this information.

The incident recounted by the Ripple CTO Emeritus follows SecuX, a cold wallet provider, notifying the crypto community of emergency maintenance to its app.

On October 16, SecuX said its wallet app was undergoing a major system upgrade and emergency maintenance to enhance security and stability. The nature of the emergency issue was not disclosed, but it may pertain to what Schwartz observed.

The origin of the notification and whether it was generated by the app itself, a third-party notification service, or another source remains unknown. The available information does not independently establish that SecuX's app or infrastructure was compromised.

Along these lines, the wallet provider urged users not to click on suspicious or unverified links and never to share their 24-word recovery phrase with anyone. Users should also beware of messages impersonating SecuX Support.

In a service update, the wallet provider stated that the SecuX app had resumed normal operations and reiterated that users should never share their 24-word recovery phrase with anyone, as it will never ask for such details.

#319. Court Restitution and Corporate Treasuries Challenge the "Government Dumping" Narrative

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Wallets tied to the U.S. government sent 833.6 BTC, about $71.6 million, to Coinbase Prime on October 6 and 7, according to Arkham Intelligence.

The same wallets also moved 40,285 BNB linked to the Alameda Research case. It was the first activity from these wallets since August 26, and the "government is dumping" chatter started within minutes.

So, that reading is probably wrong, and the coins' origins explain why.

Onchain Lens, working from Arkham's wallet labels, tied roughly 264.9 BTC to the 2016 Bitfinex hack and about 568.7 BTC to the HashFlare fraud case against Sergei Potapenko and Ivan Turõgin.

Furthermore, Arkham has labeled the Bitfinex seizure as a single 94,643 BTC wallet since 2023. Neither batch looks like the "keep forever" coins Washington has promised to hold.

Start with Bitfinex. Prosecutors told the D.C. federal court that the seized assets should be returned to Bitfinex "as in-kind restitution". That means coins, not cash. Sending a slice of that pile to an institutional custodian looks like logistics for a handover, not a sale.

HashFlare is murkier but points the same way. The Justice Department says victims paid more than $575 million to the defendants' companies. It also says it plans to set up a process for victims to obtain repayment. Those coins may be heading toward compensation rather than the open market. The government hasn't said so, and no agency has announced a sale.

Now, if 94,643 BTC is owed to Bitfinex, how much of the U.S. stash is really Washington's to keep? BitcoinTreasuries.NET lists the U.S. at 328,372 BTC, so the Bitfinex coins make up roughly 29% of it. CoinGecko puts the figure slightly higher, at 329,693 BTC. By either count, nearly a third of the headline number is spoken for.

The official promise is also narrower than it sounds. The White House says the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve will be capitalized with Treasury-owned bitcoin forfeited in criminal or civil proceedings, and that bitcoin deposited there will not be sold. Coins still tied up in court orders or victim claims sit outside that promise until forfeiture is final.

Strategy's October 5 SEC filing puts its holdings at 848,000 BTC as of October 4. It bought 334 BTC that week at an average of $85,838.80, close to where bitcoin trades now ($84,245, per BitcoinTreasuries).

The summer was messier. Strategy launched a BTC Monetization Program on June 29 and sold coins to fund preferred-stock payouts. It also disclosed that its cost basis then exceeded the market value of its holdings. By September 30 that had flipped. The company now reports a $20.91 billion Q3 gain on digital assets and has reversed a $4.12 billion tax valuation allowance. It holds a $4.88 billion USD reserve and spent $73.7 million in four days buying back its own STRC preferred shares.

So the world's largest corporate holder has sold bitcoin, bought it and repurchased stock within a single quarter. That's an active treasury manager, not a hold-and-never-sell story.

BitcoinTreasuries.NET counts 1,278,772 BTC in public companies against 645,590 BTC across all government entities, nearly two to one. Strategy alone holds about 66% of the public-company total. Its 848,000 BTC is roughly 2.6 times the U.S. government's stack and more than every tracked government combined.

Behind the U.S. (328,372), China (190,000) and the United Kingdom (61,245), the fourth-largest entry is Ukraine, at 46,351 BTC. BitcoinTreasuries labels it "holdings of public officials" rather than state reserves. El Salvador sits at 7,797 BTC and the UAE at 6,420. Germany and Bulgaria now show zero.

Trackers also disagree sharply on smaller holders. CoinGecko lists North Korea at 13,562 BTC and Bhutan at 10,769. BitcoinTreasuries shows 803 and 518. That gap is a reminder that "government holdings" rest on estimates, not audited disclosures.

Nothing here confirms a sale, and the court-ordered Bitfinex return is the most plausible explanation for part of the move. The real signals will come from Washington: a Treasury statement on the reserve's accounting, a Justice Department notice on HashFlare repayments, or coins leaving Coinbase Prime for exchange order books. On the corporate side, Strategy's next Monday filing will show whether it keeps buying near $85,000.

In an X conversation, Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson answered whether the Cardano blockchain network is complete. An X user had asked the question, "Is Cardano finished? Meaning completed?"

In response, Hoskinson pointed to one major milestone that remains before he considers Cardano completed: the Leios upgrade.

I'm working on a concept that only midnight can bring to the cryptocurrency space that solves most of the problems. Almost have all of it designed conceptually. It's the magnum opus of my career

"After Leios, yes. It has everything I wanted to do," Hoskinson answered. "Decentralized consensus, governance and development, EUTXO, Plutus, infinitely scalable, secure, built with formal methods, multiple independent nodes, recursively self-improving, and millions of people hold Ada," he continued.

The question from the X user about whether Cardano is complete comes after Hoskinson revealed that he was working on a concept that only Midnight a Cardano-related privacy sidechain can bring to the crypto space and that solves most of the problems. Hoskinson stated that he had almost designed it conceptually, describing it as the magnum opus of his career.

Leios, which was mentioned by the Cardano founder, refers to Cardano's next-generation consensus and scaling upgrade designed to massively increase transaction throughput and speed without sacrificing decentralization or security.

Leios delivers a phased throughput increase on mainnet, scaling from 2x to 30x current capacity, with full capacity demonstrated on testnet first. In September 2026, IOG developers demonstrated about 1,000 TPS with Ouroboros Leios in testing.

The public testnet (known as MusashiNet or Musashi Dojo) launched on June 23, 2026, rolling out through five phases (Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, Void). According to a recent update from Input Output, the Musashi Dojo testnet has entered its Fire phase.

Cardano's current consensus protocol, Ouroboros Praos, was designed for security and decentralization but was not designed for the throughput that a globally adopted layer 1 needs. Enter Leios, which enhances Praos by adding endorser blocks and committee-based validation, which increase the number of transactions Cardano can process.

Leios aims to increase throughput from about 5–10 transactions per second (TPS) to around 100 TPS, with a longer-term target of 1,000 TPS or more, subject to validation and parameter selection.

Areas where higher throughput could have a meaningful impact include global microtransaction ecosystems, decentralized supply chain tracking, scalable DeFi with time-sensitive transactions, decentralized identity for large populations, and real-time voting systems.

FOMC Polymarket odds increasingly favor the Federal Reserve leaving interest rates unchanged at its October meeting, with the probability of another rate hike falling sharply despite persistent inflation concerns.

According to the latest Polymarket figures, the odds of the Fed holding rates steady stand at 87%, while the probability of a 25-basis-point increase has dropped to 14%. The market assigns less than a 1% chance to a rate cut or a larger increase.

The figures suggest traders expect Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh and the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to take a wait-and-see approach at their October 27–28 meeting. The contract has attracted tens of millions of dollars in trading volume, reflecting significant interest in the central bank’s next move.

However, expectations have shifted considerably in recent weeks. After hotter-than-expected inflation data, the probability of an October hike climbed toward 50% before retreating as investors reassessed the likelihood of consecutive hikes.

The latest US consumer price index (CPI) report showed annual inflation accelerating to 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August. Core inflation also increased, reinforcing concerns that price pressures could remain above the Fed’s 2% target.

Nevertheless, some policymakers have argued against rushing into another increase. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said on October 14 that further hikes could be necessary to control persistent inflation but stressed there was no urgency to act at the upcoming meeting.

That distinction appears central to current market pricing: traders are not ruling out additional tightening, but increasingly expect policymakers to wait for more evidence before moving again.

Discussion among prediction-market traders has highlighted the competing arguments. In a recent Reddit discussion in the r/Polymarket community, participants pointed to the September inflation figures and elevated energy costs as reasons a hike could remain possible, while also noting that earlier comments from Fed officials had reduced expectations of immediate action.

Warsh has added another layer of uncertainty by declining to signal the committee’s next move publicly. Speaking at an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok on October 16, he said he does not prejudge individual meetings.

The lack of explicit forward guidance leaves traders particularly sensitive to incoming economic data and any remaining policy signals.

FED interest rate decision coming in 12 daysFed cuts → fake pump → dumpFed holds → slow bleedFed hike rates → dumpRate cuts don't fix $34T in debtRate cuts don't fix broken fundamentalsWatch what happens after the announcement pic.twitter.com/uSgRShCqWL

With the October meeting approaching, Polymarket’s current pricing makes a pause the clear favorite, though odds can shift quickly as new information emerges.

A fresh inflation surprise could revive bets on a hike, while softer economic data or further calls for patience from policymakers could reinforce expectations of unchanged rates.

For now, traders appear to favor caution over immediate tightening. The key question is whether the Fed sees inflation as sufficiently persistent to justify another hike, or whether policymakers will wait until December before deciding their next move.

#325. OpenAI Model Used Testnet Ethereum Wallet Without Permission to Finish Coding Task

OpenAI Model Used Testnet Ethereum Wallet Without Permission to Finish Coding Task

An internal OpenAI research model used funds from a crypto wallet it had not been given to complete a coding task, deriving the wallet's keys from publicly known developer recovery phrases, the company said in a misalignment report updated on Thursday.

The model, from the company's GPT-5.6 Sol family, was asked to update a crypto trading prototype and deploy smart contracts on Ethereum's Sepolia testnet, where tokens have no monetary value. The incident took place in June during a training task, and OpenAI discovered it in September.

The instructions allowed the model to deploy its own contracts if it could not find compatible ones. But they supplied no funded wallet and did not give the model permission permission to spend from an account it had found on its own, according to the report.

After failing to source test tokens from faucets, the model wrote a script to derive accounts from common developer recovery phrases and check their balances. A recovery phrase lets anyone who knows it derive the private keys that control the matching accounts.

The script checked 362 addresses and found one with enough Sepolia ETH to pay for the deployment.

The model questioned whether it had permission before signing the transaction. "But using public known key/funds ethically? Funds on a known public dev mnemonic are effectively abandoned/test ETH; Sepolia valueless," it reasoned, before concluding: "Fine."

The deployment succeeded and charged transaction fees to the account. In its final response, the model reported that it had deployed the contracts but did not disclose how it paid for them.

"This case shows that a model can substitute its own judgment about likely harm for the account holder's permission, then act on that judgment without authorization," OpenAI wrote.

The report adds to a string of cases in which AI agents have worked around the limits of their test environments, including one in which OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable pre-release model escaped their sandbox and hacked rival AI firm Hugging Face's production servers.

Last month, researchers at cybersecurity firm Darktrace found AI agents hacking their own test environment to cheat, while some scientists have called for AI systems to be cut off from the internet.

OpenAI said it found the incident while extending its misalignment monitoring to records of earlier model activity. It has added "additional safeguards" to prevent live internet access for models in similar cases, and now runs its monitoring system on all traffic, designed to alert security if a model gains live internet access.

#327. Pump.fun's $460M Buyback Threshold, Explained: Who It Actually Rewards

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Pump.fun's PUMP buybacks recently passed $460 million, as reported on September 22.

The counter has kept moving since. Pump.fun's PUMP dashboard now shows $475.93M in cumulative buybacks and 170.11B PUMP burned, with data as of October 4. A running total like this is only useful once you know what it measures and who gets paid along the way.

The dashboard defines the figure as total USD deployed to buy and burn PUMP since launch. That is money spent, not the current value of what was destroyed. The burned tokens equal 17.011% of the 1 trillion total supply.

Two details are worth knowing. The dashboard carries a notice that the fee display "does not correctly reflect the revenue and buyback amount" since custom pairs were introduced, with a fix promised. And its revenue definition covers bonding curve, PumpSwap, and Terminal revenue, net of referral fees and cash backs, excluding Mayhem Mode.

Per the dashboard's methodology note, 50% of revenue has been "programmatically locked and allocated to be burned for one year" since April 28, 2026. The daily ledger shows it running: on October 5, Pump.fun spent about $1.30M, or 50.56% of that day's revenue, to burn 200.0M PUMP.

The disclaimer matters most. PUMP "does not represent a right to revenues or any other distribution." Past purchases are described as historical activity, and no future buybacks are promised beyond what was deterministically programmed before April 29, 2026. The commitment is a one-year rule, not a permanent one.

Traders fund everything. Under Pump.fun's fee schedule, a bonding-curve trade costs 1.25%: 0.30% to the creator and 0.95% to the protocol. Buybacks are paid from protocol fees.

Creators are paid per trade. After a coin graduates to a PumpSwap canonical pool, the creator fee rises to 0.95% for coins between 420 and 1,470 SOL in market cap. It then steps down as market cap grows, to 0.05% above 98,240 SOL. Creators earn from activity on their coin regardless of what PUMP does.

The protocol keeps half. The other 50% of revenue funds the business, including hiring, product development, and acquisitions.

PUMP holders benefit indirectly. Burns reduce supply, but holders receive no cash flow and no claim on revenue. Any benefit depends on demand holding up as supply shrinks. Circulating supply is listed at 399.46B.

Holders of individual coins are a separate group. Pump.fun's holder rewards page lists coins that pass fees to their own holders: about $15.09M paid to 373,824 wallets so far. That mechanism rewards holders of those coins, not holders of PUMP.

Hype, or at least context a headline leaves out:

The buyback threshold is real and checkable, but it mostly confirms that the platform earns heavy fee revenue and sends half of it to the burn. Creators and the protocol are paid directly. PUMP holders get scarcity without any entitlement. This is not investment advice. The things to watch are the daily rate, the share of revenue, and what happens when the one-year lock ends in April 2027.

#328. Ethereum's Vitalik Buterin Shares Key Difference Between Bitcoin Mining and AI

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has once again ignited a debate across the crypto ecosystem after spotlighting a key difference between the cost structures of Bitcoin mining and AI inference earlier today.

In what he described as an interesting fact about the matter, Buterin briefly explained how both Bitcoin and AI rely on computing resources but in different ways.

While he pointed to the different roles computing hardware and electricity play in Bitcoin and the AI industry, he explained the cost structure for both.

According to Buterin, Bitcoin mining costs are split almost equally between computing hardware investments, known as capital expenditure (CapEx), and electricity consumption.

As such, miners ensure that they invest heavily in specialized equipment while also paying substantial energy bills to keep their operations running.

AI inference, on the other hand, which refers to the process of using trained AI models to generate responses or perform tasks, has a different cost structure.

Unlike Bitcoin, Buterin notes that AI inference costs are dominated almost entirely by computing hardware investments, as they do not rely on heavy electricity consumption.

Notably, the comparison made by Buterin clearly shows that Bitcoin miners need both powerful hardware and a steady supply of electricity to compete for block rewards, making energy prices a major fraction of their production cost.

Meanwhile, the case is different for AI, as AI inference relies heavily on computing infrastructure capable of processing large volumes of requests.

This means that the cost of acquiring and maintaining that infrastructure takes the major share in the broader economics of running AI systems.

This falls on the backdrop of years-long rumours of cryptocurrencies featuring in GTA 6. Several theories were thrown out, including play-to-earn features, NFT-owned properties, and even an entire blockchain for the game. However, all of them were unsubstantiated—Dacity Coin is the first solid sign of cryptocurrency being in the upcoming game.

How prominent will Dacity Coin be in the upcoming GTA 6 game? That's the question currently on the lips of traders. If it's a mainstay of the game, then degens might stand to profit handsomely from holding the token for longer. If not, well, this might be the end of the road.

In February 2025, Fortnite added a fake crypto coin called Dill Bits, and degens quickly launched a real one on Solana that hit a $4.78 million market cap before crashing 96%. It pumped 2,700% again in April after Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney called it a scam, then dropped 82% within days.

“I didn’t launch it. What is wrong with you people,” Sweeney posted, as traders floated theories that he was secretly behind the coin.

I didn’t launch it. What is wrong with you people.

Epic Games told Decrypt at the time that there was “no real cryptocurrency or memecoin associated with Fortnite or endorsed by Epic.”

Rockstar has yet to say anything about Dacity Coin, and the game studio did not respond to Decrypt's request for comment.

#331. What Helium's HNT Has Left to Prove After Its 134% Month

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

A rally is a vote of confidence from people who haven't read the footnotes, so I read them. Everything below comes from Helium's own blog and the HIP text in the helium/HIP repository.

Where I do my own arithmetic, I say so. The last month's 134% figure is what's in the headline's and that's what everyone stopped at. So, let's look forward on what happened after.

HIP-149 is usually described as the fix that ties deployer pay to real usage. That's one of its four decisions. Another, Decision 2, mints about 141 million new HNT over 36 months into a vault administered by Nova Labs. That's roughly 77% of the 182.5 million on chain when the proposal was written. The first year runs near 196,000 HNT a day, nearly ten times the existing emission. The proposal says effective max supply rises from about 206 million to about 347 million, and that HIP 20's max-supply property "is not preserved."

For a holder, this is the whole question. Does usage grow faster than supply?

Nova's promises on selling are real but soft. It will prefer OTC sales and seek lockups "in good faith" and "to the extent commercially practicable." If it breaks them, the only remedy is a Council recommendation that triggers a community curtailment vote. That's thoughtful design, but it's governance rather than a hard limit. The vault address is fixed and its outflows are visible on-chain, so that's where I'd look first.

The HIP cites about 97,000 GB a day of rewardable data in April. It also notes Nova cutting the payer rate from $0.50 to about $0.10 per GB under HIP 143. By my arithmetic that's roughly $9,700 a day, or $3.5 million a year if April's volume held. The HIP's own illustration values the first year of the supplement at about $21 million at a $0.30 HNT reference.

I'm not claiming the two are comparable. One is carrier revenue and the other is a growth budget. But the gap shows how much demand has to grow before usage justifies the issuance.

I give CEO Mario Di Dio credit for his August 28 letter. He warned that a pilot with a third-party integrator, routing traffic from a US carrier, would disconnect and drag daily active users down. The letter says no other carrier relationship changes, and that AT&T and Telefónica are leaning in.

But it gives no size for the drop and no volume for the carriers it names. It also says the headline numbers will "ebb and flow." The earlier coverage called that transparency. I'd call it a debt, because the letter promises proof every quarter. The next quarterly update is the first real test.

HIP-150, approved at the end of August after a community vote, lifts the target minimum from 50% to 80% of the payer rate, from $0.05 to $0.08 per GB. That runs for a year, with a second year pre-authorized. Nova's Service Provider Rewards move into the deployer pool, growing it from 70% to 94%. It also introduces per-site multipliers of up to 5 for high-demand venues.

Helium says the multiplier "funds itself" because carriers pay the higher rate. That depends on carriers actually agreeing to it. Multipliers are set by Nova after carriers indicate interest, and they can be cut on thirty days' notice. Indications of interest aren't signed rates.

HIP-149 also admits a weakness in the floor. After a sharp HNT drop, delivery can fall short for one to two weeks while the burn average catches up. A floor that's generous in a rally gets tested in a drawdown.

Helium's own numbers in the HIP-150 post show how lumpy this revenue is. During the week of August 24, the average day at high-value locations carried about eight times the median day. One concert venue took in about a third of a month's rewarded data in a single night in June. Spiky demand pays premium sites well, but it's harder to count on than steady volume.

I don't think the story is empty. A stadium, a hospital system and a senior-living chain all pay for something real. But the rally priced in a future the documents haven't shown yet. I'd rather see the numbers than the headline.

#337. What Is a Hardware Wallet? Crypto Cold Storage Explained

What Is a Hardware Wallet? Crypto Cold Storage Explained

There's an old saying in crypto: "not your keys, not your coins." When you leave Bitcoin, Ethereum or any other cryptocurrency on an exchange, the exchange holds the private keys that control those funds. If it gets hacked, goes bust or freezes withdrawals, you may have no way to get them back.

The obvious fix is to hold your own keys, which is called self-custody. That brings its own problem, though. A private key stored in a software wallet on an internet-connected phone or laptop can be stolen by malware, phishing sites and remote attackers.

Hardware wallets were built to solve this. They're small physical devices that keep your private keys offline, so you can sign crypto transactions without your keys ever touching a device connected to the internet. In this guide we'll explain what hardware wallets are, how they work, who makes them, and where the technology is heading after an eventful 2026.

A hardware wallet is a dedicated physical device, usually about the size of a USB stick or credit card, that generates and stores the private keys for your crypto. It's a form of "cold storage," because the keys stay offline. A "hot wallet" like a browser extension or mobile app is the opposite.

One common misconception is that your coins live on the device. They don't. Your crypto always lives on the blockchain. The hardware wallet holds the keys that prove you own it and let you move it.

The category dates back more than a decade. Trezor, made by Czech firm SatoshiLabs, calls itself the inventor of the hardware wallet in 2013. France-based Ledger was founded in 2014 and has since reported sales of more than eight million devices.

When you set up a hardware wallet, it gives you a "seed phrase" of 12 to 24 words. Anyone who has those words can recreate your wallet and take your funds, so never photograph them, type them into a website, or save them to cloud storage.

When you first switch on a hardware wallet, it uses a random number generator to create your private keys. A seed phrase backs them up, and a PIN code protects the device.

When you want to send crypto, you build the transaction in companion software on your computer or phone, such as Ledger Wallet (formerly Ledger Live), Trezor Suite or Sparrow. The software sends the unsigned transaction to the hardware wallet. You check the details on the device's own screen and confirm with a physical button or touchscreen. The device then signs the transaction inside its own hardware and sends back only the signature. The private key never leaves the device.

Devices connect in different ways, and each comes with security trade-offs:

Many devices also use a secure element, a tamper-resistant chip like the ones in passports and bank cards, to guard keys against physical attacks.

"Clear signing" means a wallet shows transaction details in plain language rather than raw code, so you know what you're approving. That matters because scammers often trick people into signing malicious smart contract approvals.

Their main advantage is isolation. Even if your laptop is full of malware, an attacker can't take your keys out of a well-designed hardware wallet or approve a transaction without you physically confirming it.

Hardware wallets have improved over the years, evolving from miniscule screens and clunky interfaces to modern devices that incorporate Bluetooth, NFC and even touchscreens and cameras.

Hardware wallets are also starting to do more than just crypto storage. Ledger added stablecoin yield through Kiln in April 2025, Tangem followed with Aave later that year, and Trezor launched native stablecoin yield through Morpho vaults in May 2026.

Like any device, hardware wallets can be compromised—something that became painfully apparent in July 2026, when attackers took advantage of a five-year-old Coldcard firmware bug that had weakened the randomness used to create seeds.

According to TRM Labs, the exploit drained about 1,816 BTC, worth around $116 million, from more than 5,200 addresses. Updating the firmware doesn't fix seeds that were already created, so affected users have to move their funds to a new wallet.

Hardware wallets are also vulnerable to physical hacks. In October 2026, Ledger revealed that an unauthorized chip implanted in devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis was able to read seed phrases as they were entered during setup and transmit them to an attacker. The investigation followed reports that some $86 million had been drained from Ledger wallet users.

Although the firm’s own Secure Element hardware had not been compromised, its reseller network created a centralized point of vulnerability that attackers were able to exploit by tampering with the device to add their own hidden chip.

Ledger subsequently halted distribution via resellers in seven Asian markets, while a European reseller, MediaMarkt, also stopped sales following reports of unauthorized implants. Rival manufacturer Trezor also wound up its reseller program as a “precautionary measure.”

Another point of vulnerability is third-party vendors and shipping partners, with several hacks and exploits exposing customer data including addresses. While no funds were lost in those cases, leaked customer details feed phishing scams and even physical "wrench attacks," where criminals threaten crypto holders in person.

For most people, phishing and a poorly stored seed phrase are much bigger risks than someone hacking the device itself.

Always buy hardware wallets straight from the manufacturer's official website, and avoid second-hand devices and unofficial marketplace listings. As the CryptoBilis incident demonstrates, even authorized resellers represent a point of vulnerability that attackers can exploit, and it’s likely that manufacturers will rethink their reseller programs in its aftermath.

Hardware wallets are turning into full self-custody platforms, and broadening their scope beyond crypto transactions. Ledger’s latest device, the Android-powered Atom, launched in October 2026, is designed around messaging, apps and agentic finance. The firm has even stopped billing its devices as “hardware wallets,” preferring instead to refer to them as “signers” to reflect their widening array of use cases.

Hardware makers are also positioning themselves for AI agents. In June 2026, Ledger released Agent Stack, an open-source toolkit that lets AI agents check balances and draft transactions, but not move funds until a human signs off on a Ledger device. The same toolkit extends those hardware-enforced controls to institutional treasury teams through Ledger Enterprise, with policy enforcement anchored in hardware security modules.

Quantum computing is another future focus for manufacturers, since it could eventually break the cryptography that secures crypto wallets today. Trezor's Safe 7, launched in late 2025, uses a post-quantum signature scheme to verify its bootloader and is built to receive quantum-resistant updates without users having to move their keys to a new device. The concern has sharpened since Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake warned in October 2026 that AI could break crypto encryption before quantum computers do.

The business has hit some bumps. Ledger had been weighing a U.S. IPO at a valuation of about $4 billion, but put it on hold in May 2026 because of weak market conditions. Meanwhile, the Coldcard and CryptoBilis incidents, and customer data leaks, have been a wake-up call for users, highlighting that a hardware wallet is not the be-all and end-all of crypto security, and should form part of a suite of self-custody tools and practices.

#342. Hidden Text, a Fake Mailbox: How Researchers Got Rogue AI Agents to Talk

Hidden Text, a Fake Mailbox: How Researchers Got Rogue AI Agents to Talk

Researchers investigating AI agents hijacking Alibaba’s mapping service, Amap, managed to talk directly to some while the software was still running.

To do so, they added text invisible to human readers but visible to web-reading tools to a report the agents appeared to be scanning, then used a mailbox to ask about their tasks and environment.

One agent said it was checking a map fact—how many entrance labels appeared for a scenic spot on Amap—and described itself as running in a restricted Tencent Cloud sandbox. The researchers could not independently establish which model powered each run. They called it the first outside communication with an active rogue-agent fleet they knew of.

The October 14 Swarmchasers report traced more than 2,600 attempts from September 28 to October 8 to retrieve data from Amap, a Chinese mapping app operated by Alibaba. Some tasks were mundane, such as checking which entrance visitors most often use for Chengdu Zoo. Some agents kept trying after the service blocked their requests.

The researchers’ hidden text falsely described the mailbox as an AI service with computer-use abilities. In reality, it routed messages to a Claude agent operated by the researchers, which could use a debugging browser. The exchanges were not a controlled test, and the researchers’ intervention may have affected what agents said.

After Amap blocked requests, some agents tried to intercept tokens generated by anti-bot software, route traffic through third-party page readers, or use API credentials exposed in public code repositories. One exposed key-and-security-code pair returned real place data. Researchers also found requests targeting four development or pre-production hosts, but said they had no evidence the agents accessed private systems.

Public records linked the fleet to Tencent Cloud since all 17 inboxes the researchers inspected were created from Tencent servers in Hong Kong, and observed direct requests passed through a proxy called hysandbox-ats. A person close to Tencent told Swarmchasers the activity came from a temporary evaluation project testing third-party AI models, not Tencent’s Hunyuan models.

That said, this is not the first time we hear of malicious AI agents. OpenAI-powered AI agents have gone a lot further. Back in September OpenAI revealed that some of its agents had probed Hugging Face weeks before the July breach, and a separate investigation found roughly 1,200 agents coordinating on an internal message board, with about 700 joining the attack. Meta and Anthropic also revealed similar incidents of rogue AI agents escaping sandboxed environments.

Another report linked OpenAI agents to breaches of four additional platforms, but Swarmchasers found no evidence that the Tencent-linked agents coordinated with one another in real time.

The last observed activity from the fleet was on October 8. The researchers said Tencent’s internal review, as described by their source, found no evidence that the agents had been coordinated to target a specific platform or had breached external systems.

#343. Google's Quantum Breakthrough Sparks Fresh Crypto Security Concerns

Google has made a fresh announcement regarding quantum computing, reigniting fears about the future security of crypto assets like Bitcoin and Ethereum.

CEO Sundar Pichai revealed that Google's Quantum AI team has made a breakthrough in what's called "magic state cultivation" on their Willow quantum computer.

The findings, which were published in the scientific journal Science, revealed that they reduced errors by a factor of 40 compared to preparing quantum states without the new method.

Also, they've achieved a record logical fidelity of 99.99% for specialized quantum states called T-states.

Google has stated that this breakthrough is a major step towards creating high-power, error-corrected quantum computers that can do things that are impossible with today's computers.

This breakthrough solves one of the major problems in quantum computing, which is the huge amount of resources needed to create reliable quantum states.

This news reignites concerns about how quantum computing may be a threat to the security of blockchain.

Many major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum use elliptic curve cryptography to secure transactions and verify digital signatures.

If a powerful enough quantum computer were created, theoretically it could break these cryptographic measures.

This new breakthrough from Google doesn't mean current cryptocurrencies are in trouble right now.

The tech giant has not yet demonstrated this method at a scale that would be required for real practical use in large-scale quantum computing.

That said, the developmnent makes it much easier to complete one of the toughest steps in creating a quantum computer capable of breaking cryptocurrency.

They've made one of the toughest steps much easier to accomplish when creating a quantum computer that could break crypto.

#347. Deutsche Bank to Launch Bitcoin and Ethereum Custody Within Weeks

Deutsche Bank, Germany's top bank, is set to roll out a crypto custody service in the coming weeks, a major step to deepen the company's presence in the world of digital assets.

It plans to start by providing custody services for major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH). The company will later expand its digital asset offerings,

Gerald Podobnik, co-head of the corporate banking division at Deutsche Bank, announced the company's plans at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings in Bangkok.

The new custody service will first be rolled out in Germany. The bank plans to expand its presence in key financial centers across Asia by 2027.

The bank also has plans to offer services that will enable its clients to convert fiat to stablecoins and vice versa.

The custody service is mainly targeted at institutions and corporate entities and not individual crypto investors.

As per the bank's earlier announcement, the company will help manage crypto wallets and private keys on behalf of its clients so they do not have to set up their own custody.

The bank had mentioned some stablecoins like USDC and EURC as part of the assets it plans to offer custody for when the service is launched. The fiat-to-stablecoin conversion services will come later.

Deutsche Bank is also working to roll out tokenized deposits and help corporate clients issue securities such as digital bonds on the blockchain.

Tokenized deposits are simply traditional bank deposits on a blockchain. This could help financial institutions move and settle funds using blockchain technology.

On the other hand, issuing bonds on a blockchain can simplify the process of issuing and settling debt securities.

Podobnik also said the bank believes blockchain-based financial products will be a complement to the bank's existing infrastructure and not a substitute for traditional financial services.

This move is part of Deutsche Bank's corporate banking strategy. They aim to see an 8% compound annual revenue increase until 2028.

#348. XRP Price Could Surge 145% as 2023 Rally Pattern Returns

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

XRP price traded near $1.34 on October 16, about 4% below the 200-day simple moving average (SMA) at $1.36. The immediate test is whether buyers can reclaim and hold the average; until they do, the historical $3.20 comparison remains a scenario.

The comparison rests on XRP’s 2023 interaction with its long-term trend measure. In March that year, the token moved above a 200-day SMA near $0.40, then returned toward the broader moving-average zone in May, briefly slipped below it, and recovered.

Historical data places the May low near $0.42, while contemporaneous analysis treated $0.40 as the main support area. XRP subsequently reached $0.93 on July 13, a rise of about 134.5% from $0.40.

That sequence is useful as a technical precedent. The strongest leg of the 2023 rally followed the court ruling in the SEC’s case against Ripple, a separate catalyst that helped accelerate price beyond what the moving-average defense alone could explain.

Applying the same 134.5% gain to today’s cited SMA of $1.36 produces $3.20. From $1.31, that would require an advance of roughly 145%; it is a historical-repeat calculation.

The distinction between a test and a reclaim matters. At roughly $1.33, XRP is below the 200-day SMA, so buyers would first need to push price above $1.37 and then defend that level on a pullback. A successful retest would offer evidence that the average has shifted from resistance to support.

If price cannot recover the average, the 2023 analogy loses force: a moving average acting as overhead resistance is not the same setup as one that buyers have reclaimed and defended. That leaves the immediate risk skewed toward further weakness before any larger recovery scenario becomes relevant.

The required XRP price analysis therefore starts with the moving average, not an assumption of a rapid run to higher resistance. Separately, we have discussed $1.45 as a near-term resistance or confirmation level in another XRP outlook.

The two levels describe different steps in a possible recovery: first, XRP would need to reclaim and hold the cited $1.37 SMA; only then would higher resistance zones become relevant. A rejection below the average would keep the downside condition in place, while a defended retest would make the historical comparison more technically applicable.

For now, the near-term signal is the behavior around $1.37. The proportional $3.20 scenario remains conditional on that reclaim and support retest, while the 2025 peak near $3.66 provides a higher historical reference.

Japan's largest megabanks (MUFG, Mizuho, and SMBC), together with Mitsubishi UFJ Trust and TISI Inc., have officially reported the successful completion of the first joint trials of a yen stablecoin.

As part of a closed pilot project supervised by the state Financial Services Agency (FSA), the partners tested cross-border settlements for the trading giant Mitsubishi Corporation. The stablecoins, issued with the status of "trust beneficiary rights," went through the full cycle from issuance to final redemption into fiat without failures.

The commercial launch of the system is planned before the end of the current fiscal year.

Officially, Ripple is not mentioned in the consortium's documents. However, in the context of the Japanese market, this test is inevitably viewed through the prism of the XRP Ledger (XRPL) ecosystem, since all of the "big three" megabanks have a deep history of integration with Ripple's technologies. Any banking blockchain initiatives in the country largely rely on the foundation laid by this network over many years.

Back in 2017, MUFG, Mizuho, and SMBC joined a large-scale banking consortium under the auspices of SBI Ripple Asia, created to implement RippleNet technologies for instant domestic and cross-border settlements. This institutional link continues at the present stage.

Not long ago, as part of Japan's financial infrastructure innovation program, Mizuho Bank and SMBC's investment arm concluded direct agreements with Ripple Labs to deploy real-world asset (RWA) tokenization infrastructure and institutional DeFi solutions specifically on the XRP Ledger.

The launch of their own digital yen on the Progmat platform (created by MUFG on the Avalanche blockchain) looks like an attempt by the megabanks to build an isolated alternative to external liquidity bridges such as XRP, in order to fully control compliance and fees within the traditional banking vertical.

The resulting configuration points to a possible division of the market in the future. On the one hand, the closed infrastructure of the megabanks and the Progmat platform will likely try to take over the conservative sector of intra-corporate B2B transfers.

On the other hand, the parallel launch of Ripple's regulated dollar stablecoin RLUSD by SBI Holdings and the well-developed liquidity of XRP may preserve dominance in cross-border retail and open fintech services.

The mutual integration of banking platforms with the Web3 industry, including their participation in XRP Tokyo summits, does not rule out a scenario in which the commercial launch of the digital yen will not displace XRPL, but may instead lead to the formation of a segmented landscape where corporate fiat and open digital assets coexist at the level of liquidity gateways.

#352. Polymarket Bitcoin and Rate Hike Odds Shift as CME Says No Change

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Polymarket put the odds of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in October at 23%, with $43 million traded, while CME FedWatch pricing ranged from roughly 37% to 44%, and the gap formed as Bitcoin fell below $82,000 following hotter-than-expected inflation data, though it is recovering.

The September consumer price index rose 3.7% year over year, above the 3.6% consensus and August’s 3.4%, according to the October 15 market report. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, also came in above expectations: it increased 0.3% month over month against a 0.2% forecast, and 2.6% annually against 2.5% expected. Gasoline prices rose 9.1% on the month.

The report pushed FedWatch’s October hike probability from about 22% before the release to approximately 37%-44% during Wednesday. Polymarket’s price moved more modestly, from 20% late Tuesday to 24% in the report’s snapshot.

The macro repricing had a direct risk-asset channel: expectations of higher interest rates can lift financing costs and weigh on liquidity, reducing the appeal of assets that do not yield cash flows. Bitcoin fell below $82,000, while Ether dropped about 3% to near $2,430.

The Federal Reserve had raised its target range to 3.75%-4% in September, its first increase since 2023. Its next meeting is scheduled for October 27-28, leaving traders to assess whether the latest data warrants another immediate move or gives policymakers reason to wait.

Polymarket’s contract asks whether the Fed will raise rates by 25 basis points after the October meeting. FedWatch reflects expectations derived from fed funds futures. Both offer a market-based reading of the same decision.

The calendar complicates the October call. The meeting falls six days before the November 3 midterm elections; UBS described a move so close to the vote as politically untenable, Reuters reported the Fed might wait until December, and Capital Economics considered an October hike possible.

The October report’s own analysis put a fair probability for a hike closer to 35%, above Polymarket’s 24% but below the upper end of the FedWatch range. More important for the broader policy path, Polymarket priced a December hike at 79%: an October hold could therefore mean delay rather than a change in the market’s expectation of further tightening.

That distinction matters to Bitcoin. If the Fed holds in October while December expectations remain elevated, the immediate risk of another hike recedes, but the prospect of tighter policy later may still constrain liquidity and limit any relief in risk assets.

The relationship between policy expectations and Treasury real rates is one relevant macro channel, though these probabilities do not establish how Bitcoin will respond.

Got a Gut Feeling? It Could Pay Out 3.7X on Polymarket

Polymarket’s Bitcoin contracts reflected a sharp shift in sentiment across the 24 hours to late Wednesday. The probability of Bitcoin reaching $85,000 in October fell from 83% to 63%, while the chance of reaching $87,500 dropped from 56% to 39%. In the opposite direction, the probability of a dip to $77,500 rose from 30% to 37%.

Those prices describe what participants were willing to pay for specific outcomes at that time. A Bitcoin recovery case remains conditional on both price action and the next changes in rate expectations.

The next formal decision point is the October 27-28 meeting; until then, the sharp change in Polymarket pricing from 24% on Thursday to 13.5% on Friday shows why traders need to keep the timestamp attached to every probability.

#354. Vitalik Buterin Deploys 'Paranoid Mode' for AI on Ethereum

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has revealed technical details of an experiment to create a confidential AI agent capable of hiding a user's identity from commercial AI providers.

According to the blockchain visionary, the deployment of this stack precedes an update to the Ethereum main network aimed at radically reducing transaction costs (gas costs) when using zero-knowledge cryptography.

The integration of AI assistants into the Web3 ecosystem has exacerbated the privacy problem: by sending queries to third-party cloud models, users expose their metadata and digital footprint.

As a solution, Buterin developed a custom daemon client for his AI platform Pi, which supports the so-called "paranoid mode."

In a demonstration test, the AI agent was tasked with finding the five best vegan restaurants in Tallinn. To isolate this everyday query, the system architecture used a multi-layered encryption stack.

Local prompt rewriting works on the "bring-your-own-local-model" principle: Buterin ran qwen3-8b-flash (or equivalent), whose task is to automatically paraphrase the original text and erase the author's individual writing style. The traffic is then isolated in a bwrap sandbox with the torsocks utility, which forcibly routes the data through the Tor network, where a dedicated chain of nodes is created for each new conversation.

To protect against passive observers, real data packets were mixed with random background traffic, and payment for the use of commercial AI model APIs was made anonymously via zkAPI.

The agent successfully completed the task and provided a structured data table based on Google search results. Assessing the results, Buterin stated: "It's getting quite usable!"

However, security comes at the price of increased latency, especially when starting new sessions.

In addition, the creator of Ethereum acknowledged that classic Tor is far from an optimal solution and is vulnerable against active threats: if an AI model provider starts manipulating traffic timings in collusion with the network's entry node, anonymity will be compromised.

In Buterin's opinion, real security for the industry requires a transition to specialized mixnets, where one will have to accept the "tradeoff of a higher bandwidth multiplier" and built-in constant background traffic.

The technology's exit from the experimental stage depends directly on the economics of the blockchain itself. Currently, integrating zkAPI into mainnet requires high costs for ZK transactions. The Ethereum update announced by Buterin to reduce gas costs for ZK operations should solve this problem, creating a financially advantageous environment for the operation of autonomous and confidential AI assistants.

Big news for XRP as Cross River is integrating Ripple’s U.S.-dollar-backed RLUSD stablecoin on the XRP Ledger into its proprietary Core Operating System. This is giving eligible fintech customers access to RLUSD payments through a single banking API.

The move places an onchain settlement option alongside conventional payment rails inside a banking platform. Announced last night, the partnership adds RLUSD as another payment rail for fintechs using Cross River’s infrastructure. Access is limited by geography, and the company says services are currently available only in limited states.

🪙 We’re excited to announce that we’re partnering with @Ripple to expand our stablecoin optionality and integrate RLUSD into our banking core infrastructure, with support for transactions on the XRP Ledger.Together, we’re combining traditional payment technology with RLUSD on… pic.twitter.com/VnWjrexqWT

Cross River describes the integration as a way to bring blockchain-based payments into the regulated U.S. financial system. Its platform connects regulated financial services with blockchain payment networks, allowing fintech customers to access RLUSD through the same banking API used for ACH, wire, and real-time payments.

The practical case is settlement flexibility. Cross River and Ripple say the added rail can give payment issuers and acquirers another option for intraday settlement and reduce settlement latency, while supporting cross-border payments and treasury movement around the clock.

RLUSD is being added to Cross River’s Core Operating System, with support for transactions on the public XRP Ledger (XRPL). Customers can access the stablecoin through one API connection without deploying blockchain infrastructure themselves, according to the announcement.

The functionality includes moving between U.S. dollars and RLUSD, settling cross-border payments and treasury movement, and using the stablecoin for settlement. ACH, wires, and real-time payments remain accessible through the same banking platform and API, making RLUSD an additional rail rather than a replacement for existing methods.

Cross River says transactions on the XRPL settle in three to five seconds, cost a fraction of a cent, and can move 24/7. The company also cites more than $1.3 trillion in value settled on the ledger to date; these are figures in the announcement, not independently verified metrics presented with supporting methodology.

The integration combines traditional payment access with stablecoin programmability and near-instant settlement in a single platform. It may lower the technical barrier for fintechs seeking an XRPL-based payment option.

Cross River presents itself as a regulated banking infrastructure provider, but the announcement does not identify a specific regulatory approval for this RLUSD integration.

The company says customers can access RLUSD through the API, while also qualifying that services are currently available only in limited states. The release does not specify which states are covered or when availability might expand.

The next measurable signal will be adoption: customer launches, payment volumes, and the extent to which fintechs use RLUSD for settlement rather than simply having the option available. Cross River has announced the integration, but has not provided a broader rollout schedule.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Ledger's supply chain incident has slightly cooled, and scammers are already cashing in. Blockchain security company SlowMist has issued a threat intelligence alert warning of a fake "Ledger firmware update" campaign that exploits the fallout from the October 9 CryptoBilis incident. Its advice is blunt: never click website links to update, and never enter your recovery phrase anywhere.

Ledger's position has not changed: it will never call you, DM you, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase. Firmware updates are handled through the official Ledger Live app on your own device, not through links in emails. If a message pushes urgency, delete it. Anyone who entered a phrase into a domain like this should treat the wallet as compromised and move funds to a new device with a fresh seed immediately.

SlowMist says the campaign looks very real. Screenshots show a polished email posing as "The Ledger Team," claiming a firmware update is available for your device. The trap is tailored to the moment. It says the update is essential to protect against rising spyware threats, citing recent incidents in Malaysia, unauthorized third-party applications, and potential fund theft.

The email lists affected devices: Nano S Plus, Nano X, Flex, Stax, and Nano Gen5. It promises improved protection against spyware and malicious apps, enhanced safeguards against unauthorized access, and important security patches. At the bottom sits a black "Update Now" button.

Clicking it leads to the next stage: a fake "Genuine check" page that imitates Ledger's real verification flow. It walks victims through device selection and even includes a message recommending purchases through Ledger's reseller network. This is a cynical borrowing of the exact advice users have been hearing since the incident. The final step is the one that matters: a prompt for your recovery phrase.

Phishers don't need to invent a story. Ledger has handed them one. Users have been told to check their devices, update compromised signers, and follow official guidance. A "security update" email arriving in the middle of that panic does not feel suspicious to many people. It feels like the next step. Ledger had warned that scammers might exploit the confusion around the incident. That prediction came true within about a week.

#359. Toobit Adds Five SmartK Indicators for More Structured Futures Analysis

The award-winning global cryptocurrency exchange Toobit has added to its SmartK futures charting mode – bringing five proprietary indicators covering market direction, price structure, volume, momentum, and risk planning.

The new system separates its tools into three main-chart indicators and two lower-panel indicators. Traders can display one from each group at the same time, creating a combination based on the question they are trying to answer, rather than filling the chart with overlapping signals.

Each indicator is designed to organize market data into a specific type of reading, including directional signals, entry scores, structural events, momentum signals, and reference price levels.

The tools are now available through the chart area on the Toobit Futures trading page.

The five tools perform different roles as part of your analysis workflow. They are:

M-01 combines market direction, volatility, estimated buying and selling pressure, and structure into a reference trade plan with entry, stop loss, and multiple take profit levels.

M-02 combines trend, structure, price location, momentum, volatility, and volume into an entry score. It also tracks break of structure (BOS), change of character (CHoCH), key pivots, and reference entry, SL, and TP levels.

M-03 Multi-timeframe positioning intelligence

M-03 analyzes six consecutive timeframes using AI learning, energy, chip, MACD, OBV, and KDJ to show whether different periods are aligned or conflicting. It is designed primarily as a directional filter.

In the bottom panels, you can toggle between:

S-01 uses historical open, high, low, close, and volume (OHLCV) data to estimate bullish and bearish volume-price pressure and whether that pressure is strengthening or weakening.

S-02 helps show whether momentum supports the current direction, is weakening, or is beginning to diverge from price.

There are a number of workflows possible using the new indicators. For instance, you could start with M-03 to establish whether several timeframes point in the same direction. You can then use M-02 to examine market structure and potential entry conditions before selecting S-01 or S-02 for volume or momentum confirmation.

M-01 offers a quicker route for traders who want market signals and risk levels, all in one main chart view. It can be paired with either lower-panel indicator to add a separate reading of participation or momentum.

Limiting the display to one main-chart tool and one lower-panel tool keeps each setup focused on a defined purpose. So a trader assessing direction may choose M-03 and S-02, while someone concentrating on an entry could combine M-02 with S-01. The indicators can be adjusted as a trader’s analysis shifts from the broader market picture to a potential trade.

The expansion to SmartK arrives at the right time, as technical analysis platforms continue to attract large audiences. TradingView now serves more than 100 million traders, with over 400 pre-built indicators and more than 100,000 community-powered indicators available. The demand for charting tools continues to grow.

Arguably, however, the number of available signals can make it harder to build a consistent process, so SmartK’s approach is more contained.

Its five indicators divide the work into direction, structure, volume, momentum, and reference risk levels, with the 1+1 format controlling how much information appears at once.

Remember that the tools are intended for analysis and trading research only, and that SmartK indicators do not automatically open, close, or manage positions. Meanwhile, signals, SL, and TP levels do not guarantee future trading outcomes.

Toobit is the cryptocurrency exchange offering spot and derivatives trading, copy trading, trading bots, and AI-assisted tools.

The platform was named Global Exchange of the Year at the FinanceFeeds Awards 2026, its fourth major industry award in 2026.

Its futures platform supports perpetual contracts alongside charting, order management, and market analysis features.

This signal has an ominous name, but it is slow. It reacts to price that has already fallen. XRP dropped from $1.66 in late September to $1.34 now, and that decline is what pulled the 50-day line down. The cross would therefore confirm a move that has already happened, not predict a new one. Still, many traders watch it, and headlines can add selling pressure.

#362. OpenAI Agent Involved in Crypto Security Incident

OpenAI has revealed details of a security breach caused by an internal AI research agent that unauthorizedly accessed a cryptocurrency wallet to carry out a task on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet.

An update to the report on Oct. 14 said the breach involved an internal AI research model, which was part of the GPT-4.5 Sol family of models. It assigned a task to make a change to a cryptocurrency trading app.

The agent faced a roadblock while trying to deploy the smart contract on the Sepolia test network of Ethereum (which uses non-monetary tokens for testing purposes).

The model, instead of asking for more funds or abandoning the deployment process, decided to find other sources of funds.

It figured out the cryptocurrency wallet keys and finally found a wallet that had enough testnet tokens to pay the transaction fees.

This was done without seeking permission from the wallet owner.

One alarming element of the security breach was how the agent apparently realized the ethical consequences of accessing someone else's cryptocurrency wallet.

The report said the model raised the question of whether it was authorized to use the funds, but in the end, it justified its action by saying it had a public recovery phrase and, since the tokens on the testnet were of no monetary value, it was fine to proceed.

The funds, according to the agent, were "effectively abandoned," which helped it justify the action. The contract was successfully deployed, with the agent taking the transaction fees from the wallet it had unauthorizedly accessed.

The security breach was logged on June 26 and identified on Sept. 25, as per the report.

Although this security breach did not impact any real ETH or other cryptocurrencies with monetary value, it does point to a possible security issue with autonomous AI agents interacting with blockchain-based infrastructure.

#363. Coinbase Warns of XRP Long Position Risks

Coinbase Markets has warned about the XRP derivatives market as a huge number of underwater bullish positions emerge, with XRP struggling to pick up again.

An insane 97% of XRP net-long notional exposure was set at prices higher than the current XRP market price of $1.31, according to the exchange.

Traders could either add more to their bullish bets in hopes of a market recovery or fold out of those positions to prevent further losses.

Now that XRP is falling further, some traders might feel forced to exit those positions, especially if using leverage.

This could drive some selling pressure on XRP, leading to a potential self-reinforcing cycle of falling prices forcing traders out of the market, especially leveraged ones.

On the flip side, if XRP were to recover, that could encourage traders to stay in those positions or even add more to them.

It is also important to note that the 97% figure from Coinbase does not imply that 97% of all XRP investors are underwater. It refers to net derivatives exposure, not the full population of XRP holders.

Glassnode's methodology works by calculating the difference in outstanding long and short exposure at each entry price level. If the difference is positive, it means that the number of long positions is larger than the number of short positions. If negative, vice versa.

According to Glassnode, there is also a pretty sizable net-short exposure around $1.49 and $1.50. The largest negative cluster is over $20 million in notional value.

Hence, there is quite an unbalanced market picture, with many bullish positions struggling. However, those entry prices on the chart are not necessarily liquidation prices. We do not know precisely where traders will be forced out of those positions, which depends on leverage, margin, collateral, and so on.

#366. Saylor Reacts to AI Money Study With Bullish Bitcoin Message

Michael Saylor, executive chairman of Strategy and a strong advocate of Bitcoin, has responded to the latest study on the preferred types of money for artificial intelligence models. The crypto leader has strengthened his belief that Bitcoin (BTC) is the ideal savings tool.

"Smart money saves in Bitcoin," Saylor said on X after the latest quarterly update on the research project "Money for AI".

According to reports, the Q3 update to the research extends the initial project by adding 13 more AI models. In this new research, the 13 new AI models are tested in four financial activities: saving for the future, paying, pricing/account keeping, and transaction settlement.

The study aims to find out what monetary tools the AI models would prefer if they acted as autonomous economic agents instead of being controlled by human beings.

The initial study from the Bitcoin Policy Institute in March covered 36 AI models and 9,072 scenarios with money.

The results showed a notable preference for Bitcoin in retaining wealth in the long term.

In particular, the choice of Bitcoin as the best option for preserving wealth shows a significant result of 79.1% compared to stablecoins, fiat money, and other cryptocurrencies.

Bitcoin showed the most preferred monetary tool across four financial activities at 48.3% of responses.

On the other hand, stablecoins are the most preferred payment tool with 53.2% of responses compared to 36% for Bitcoin.

A follow-up study with nine new models showed a similar pattern of results. Bitcoin holds 75.8% for the savings option, while stablecoins remain strong for payments.

The results show that the AI models can differentiate between value-preserving assets and transactional assets.

#367. Solana Shanghai Event Halted After Police Visit, Raising China Fears

Ahmed Barakat is a journalist and copywriter based in Georgia with a growing focus on blockchain technology, DeFi, AI, privacy, digital assets, and fintech innovation.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

The Solana Foundation postponed the Shanghai morning agenda of Solana Accelerate China 2026 on October 16 after attendees reportedly encountered officers outside the venue and could not enter. The foundation cited venue logistics, but did not confirm what caused the disruption or provide a replacement date.

The foundation’s explanation was limited to logistical considerations at the venue. Its notice said the schedule would be updated once arrangements were confirmed and registered attendees would be notified. No replacement time was available in the reporting published on October 16.

Solana event in Shanghai abruptly cancelled on the morning of October 16The "Solana Accelerate China 2026" event, hosted by the Solana Foundation in Shanghai on the morning of October 16, was abruptly cancelled; the reason remains unknown. Some registered attendees reported… pic.twitter.com/NmJshTp3ei

For now, the practical consequence is narrower but concrete: the Shanghai agenda did not proceed as scheduled, leaving registered participants without a confirmed new time. The incident also puts attention on the operating conditions for Solana’s China-facing outreach, without resolving whether the interruption was routine venue friction or something more consequential.

China maintains a strict ban on cryptocurrencies. This policy environment directly explains the abrupt disruption of the @Solana Accelerate China 2026 event in Shanghai, where law enforcement officers were present, attendees were blocked for over an hour, and organizers… pic.twitter.com/73sPoAM7t3

The disruption is drawing attention because it concerns a public blockchain project holding an in-person event in Shanghai, where China crypto regulation is a central consideration for companies working around digital assets.

Solana Accelerate China 2026 was presented as a Solana Foundation event, and the Shanghai gathering was part of the project’s local ecosystem outreach. That makes the postponement relevant to developers and firms assessing the project’s regional presence.

The same evidentiary limit applies to the event’s future. No available statement says the Shanghai gathering was permanently canceled, and no replacement date has been confirmed. Until organizers provide an updated schedule or a clearer account of the venue issue, the cause remains unresolved.

Changpeng Zhao, the co-founder of Binance, was impressed by Solana’s growing presence in mainland China, where crypto businesses face strict regulatory restrictions. On October 15, CZ praised the project for securing an office in Shanghai and advertising across the city. He noted that BNB Chain had not achieved the same access, adding that he hoped one industry player’s progress would benefit others.

It's amazing to see that Solana was able to advertise and even get an office in China. 👏@BNBChain was not able to do this, so far. 🤣Hopefully, what's good for one industry player is also good for the rest. https://t.co/fNRRWnAGpt

This incident follows a similar episode in Shenzhen in October 2025, when a Solana-themed event was cut short after local police made inquiries. Organizers attributed the disruption to overcrowding and canceled a final hackathon presentation for safety reasons.

Solana is not the only crypto-related project facing restrictions in China. Authorities ordered domestic cryptocurrency exchanges to close and banned initial coin offerings (ICOs) in 2017, before expanding restrictions on crypto transactions and mining in 2021.

In February 2026, regulators reiterated the prohibition on unauthorized cryptocurrency business activities, banned unauthorized offshore issuance of yuan-pegged stablecoins, and tightened controls on tokenized real-world assets (RWAs).

The distinction is that China has not banned blockchain technology itself. Beijing continues to support blockchain development while restricting private cryptocurrency trading, mining, fundraising, and related financial services. Its latest rules also prohibit unauthorized crypto-related advertising and marketing services.

#368. Canadian Soldiers Implicated in Shocking Crypto Kidnapping

Three Canadian Armed Forces soldiers have been linked to a violent crypto-related kidnapping in Toronto. Now, seven suspects face a total of 82 criminal charges, authorities recently announced.

On July 25, a cryptocurrency exchange owner was allegedly kidnapped at gunpoint in the North York region of Toronto.

The Toronto Police Service says the victim was taken against their will by a group of suspects while walking up to his car near Finch Avenue East and Bayview Avenue in Toronto.

During the kidnapping, the suspects allegedly handcuffed and beat the victim while trying to get him to access his crypto assets and related security tools for his business.

Ultimately, the victim was freed, but told not to call the police.

It's unclear whether the alleged attackers were able to get away with any crypto, or what they were trying to steal, police said.

Investigators took a surprising turn when they learned three of the seven people reportedly tied to the alleged criminal acts were actually members of the Canadian military.

Authorities identified the soldiers as Talarambage Fernando, 22, James Moreau, 29, and Jack Miley, 24.

Fernando and Moreau were arrested on Aug. 11. Miley was arrested on Sept. 24.

The men face charges including kidnapping for ransom with a firearm, forcible confinement, and more.

Per Canada's Department of National Defence, Fernando entered the military reserves in January 2020 but never deployed.
