Overnight on October 15, the cryptocurrency market experienced its largest wave of forced liquidations of margin positions since August. According to CoinGlass, the daily liquidation volume amounted to $939.30 million, with $791.62 million (84.3%) of all losses falling on holders of long positions (longs).

The sharp drop in prices led to a large-scale unloading of the derivatives market, ridding the industry of accumulated speculative ballast.

The main blow was taken by Ethereum ($286.11 million) and Bitcoin ($215.49 million). The largest recorded incident was the liquidation of a long position on the BTC-USDT pair on Binance worth $12.03 million at a price of $80,208.96, while Binance itself accounted for 52.3% of the total volume of closed orders.

At the same time, the sector of highly liquid altcoins with a high share of retail capital came under pressure: the volume of forcibly closed daily positions amounted to $12.82 million in XRP, $12.32 million in NEAR Protocol, and $12.18 million in Dogecoin. For the altcoin market, relaxed by prolonged growth, this correction became the first truly deep shake-up in recent months.

Despite the severity of the overnight ordeal, the technical picture points not to a trend change but to a controlled cleansing of the market. During the drop, the BTC price tested the dynamic support in the form of the 50-day moving average (MA 50), around $81,000, with jeweler's precision, where it met a significant volume of buying.

The fact that Bitcoin held above the psychological mark of $80,000, while the long-term support (MA 200) lies significantly lower, at $72,000, confirms the strength of the current bullish trend.

The subsequent short squeeze confirmed aggressive demand at the lows. As soon as retail traders, under the influence of panic, began opening short positions at the local bottom, the prices of BTC and ETH sharply corrected upward, triggering a cascading closure of "bearish" orders.

In just one hour, Bitcoin sellers lost $15.94 million (95.2% of all hourly liquidations for the asset), while Ethereum short sellers lost $19.41 million. Short positions on NEAR and DOGE also took a hit during the same hour, registering an instant wipeout of sellers.

At the moment, funding rates on key perpetual futures remain in a stable positive zone (0.005%–0.009%), which indicates that mid-term optimism among market participants has persisted after the technical cleansing of excess leverage was completed.

Global search interest in Bitcoin sharply declined in October 2026, plunging to multi-year lows. According to the latest Google Trends data, search volumes for "bitcoin" and "BTCUSD" fell to their lowest levels in several years.

On-chain analyst Willy Woo drew attention to this trend by publishing a long-term chart of user activity.

The decline in interest coincided with a prolonged market correction. After reaching an all-time high of $126,080 in October 2025, the first cryptocurrency entered a cooling phase. In mid-October 2026, the asset is trading in the $82,500–$83,400 range, having lost about 4% since the start of the month, which weakens investors' expectations of the traditional autumn rally.

Historically, periods of minimal search activity among retail investors have preceded the formation of a long-term price bottom. Willy Woo uses this data to support the classic contrarian strategy: "The best time to buy BTC is when nobody is interested in it. The best time to sell is when absolutely everyone is involved." The search query peaks in 2017 and 2021 coincided with the tops of bull cycles and the profit-taking phase of large players.

At the same time, Google Trends statistics revealed an internal split in audience behavior. While Bitcoin queries are falling, the number of general "buy crypto" queries hit new annual highs in October. This indicates that retail capital is not leaving the industry but is being redistributed into alternative tokens in search of higher returns.

The change in the structure of the crypto market in 2026 largely explains why the decline in search activity has carried over into pricing less painfully than in previous cycles. The direct dependence of the exchange rate on retail users' clicks has weakened with the inflow of institutional capital.

The main volumes of liquidity through spot BTC ETFs, pension funds, and hedge funds now flow through specialized trading terminals and over-the-counter (OTC) desks, bypassing standard search engines.

Under these conditions, Google Trends has ceased to be a direct driver of the exchange rate but has retained its status as a key indicator of retail sentiment and the level of speculative overheating in the market.

#373. Ripple Taps $9 Billion Perpetual Futures Boom

According to a recent Bloomberg report, Ripple is broadening its reach in the traditional finance space by opening up access to perpetual futures for stocks, commodities, and other traditional assets for institutional investors.

Ripple's prime brokerage arm, Ripple Prime, is launching the new service that will give institutions access to over 100 markets, including equities, stock indexes, exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and commodities.

The new offerings come at a time of explosive growth in perp contracts on real-world assets, with open interest across several major platforms jumping from near zero to around $9 billion in the last year.

Unlike traditional futures contracts, perpetual contracts don't expire, so users can hold leveraged positions without needing to roll them over into new contracts.

The new products are being rolled out via Trade.xyz, which is a large trading platform for perp contracts on traditional assets on the decentralized Hyperliquid platform.

Earlier this year, in February, Ripple Prime launched crypto perpetual futures as part of its growing efforts to offer a full trading solution for institutional investors.

The new offering includes features like cross-margining, where investors can leverage the same collateral across different positions instead of needing separate margins for each trade.

Per Michael Higgins, the international CEO of Ripple Prime, this new setup could allow institutional users to more effectively manage their capital and access new liquidity pools.

At the same time, Higgins stressed that with this new offering, institutions can gain exposure to these markets on a "more regulated" infrastructure.

The explosion in growth for real-world asset perpetual futures has been drawing increasing interest from hedge funds and professional market makers.

As Higgins pointed out, institutional traders are now looking into various strategies around using these new instruments.

On the one hand, some investors are looking to pursue basis trades by taking positions on perps and their underlying assets to exploit price discrepancies. That would let them avoid general market exposure.

Meanwhile, Higgins indicated that traditional hedge funds are on the cusp of being able to get direct access to tokenized real-world assets.

The crypto project Starknet, which was originally created as a technical add-on for scaling Ethereum, has announced plans to become a fully independent blockchain. The StarkWare team has put a radical question to a community vote: should the project break free from the control of the main altcoin network and move to the status of an autonomous Layer 1?

The market reacted to the prospect of this "divorce" as a powerful financial trigger. In the first weeks of October, the native STRK token had already soared 200%, then pulled back along with the rest of the industry. But today, right on the day the official vote launched, the charts went up again, with the price gaining 25% at one point.

Trading activity has shifted entirely to derivatives: the daily trading volume on the futures market reached $894.84 million, almost eight times the spot sector's figure ($116.38 million). The market is aggressively digesting this flurry of orders alongside today's scheduled unlock of 127 million tokens for early investors.

Behind this decision lies a cold mathematical calculation: Starknet is trying to protect itself against the quantum computers of the future. The head of the project, Eli Ben-Sasson, is convinced that the development of AI has brought the arrival of machines capable of breaking modern encryption closer.

Starknet is technically ready to deploy quantum resistance as early as 2027. The problem is that it is currently tightly tied to the slow Ethereum, which plans to upgrade its security only by the end of 2029. To avoid losing two years, Starknet wants to take full control into its own hands.

The poll on the Snapshot platform, which will run until October 22, has already shown total unanimity: the "For" option is gaining 99.88% of the votes. At the same time, the project's tokenomics will not change: STRK will remain the network's only settlement asset, and the bridges to Ethereum will keep working.

However, investors should understand that the current referendum is preliminary (non-binding) and only gives the green light to research. The technical transition itself will require months of preparation and new votes.

The main price of this independence is security. Currently, Starknet transactions are protected by the authority of Ethereum and the billions of dollars of its staked validators. Having set sail on its own, the project will have to build its own protection system, whose reliability will rest solely on the capitalization of the STRK token.

At the moment, it stands at $580.24 million, which is incomparably smaller than Ethereum's, but the developers are deliberately accepting this trade-off for the sake of a technological edge.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse has defined the next stage of XRP Ledger (XRPL) development. On air on the Wall Street show, the head of the company stated that native credit infrastructure and on-chain yield tools for institutional capital are being added to cross-border settlements and the buy-and-hold strategy.

The plan outlined by Garlinghouse is being implemented against the backdrop of the Evernorth Holdings fund's listing on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN, to which Ripple allocated 127 million XRP tokens.

According to the CEO's statement, the goal of the partnership is to deploy on-chain and off-chain products capable of making liquidity work.

The yield-generation vector outlined by the head of Ripple already relies on the existing hybrid CeDeFi architecture. The Doppler Finance platform has accumulated $150 million from 14,000 depositors in vaults for XRP and the RLUSD stablecoin. The XRP vault accounts for $125 million (~90 million tokens).

Using delta-neutral strategies, arbitrage, and spot-perp basis trading, Doppler provides the very yield that Garlinghouse spoke about for the Evernorth treasury, the Japanese conglomerate SBI, and large exchange wallets. Additional flows come through the earnXRP gateways on the Flare network and the ledger's own native AMM.

First, reach an agreement with the validators. The credit market announced by Garlinghouse technically depends on two code updates that are currently being voted on by the network. The first amendment, XLS-65, is meant to launch single-asset liquidity pools (XRP-only or RLUSD-only), which will protect large funds from impermanent loss risks.

The second, XLS-66, activates the very mechanism for issuing fixed-term loans. As of mid-October 2026, 50–55% of validators support this key amendment. To launch, the code must stay above the 80% threshold for two weeks.

Second, embed Wall Street rules into the blockchain. The ledger's unique capabilities that the CEO spoke about are tied to strict compliance in the XLS-66 protocol. To spare institutions the risks of anonymous DeFi, underwriting and borrower assessment have been moved off-chain and will be conducted by licensed institutions.

At the same time, capital safety will be backed by a "first-loss" mechanism, and KYC/AML verification will be handled by the native layer of domain verification and digital mandates.

Third, deploy the accompanying software, and this base is already live on mainnet. The Permission Delegation and Atomic Batch features allow funds to distribute account access rights without handing over private keys, and the MPT standard is already used for tokenizing real-world assets (RWA) in tandem with Ripple's USD stablecoin.

Evernorth, Doppler, Clearpool, and Cicada have announced their intention to roll out native lending immediately after its activation in Q4 2026.

#382. Vitalik Buterin Reveals New Key Priority for Ethereum (ETH)

Vitalik Buterin says the race for speed in the zero-knowledge Ethereum era is over, and security should now come first. In a post on X, he congratulated the ZKsync Airbender team for a new milestone and stated that the fight for speed is definitively won. He wants teams building zkEVMs, which are tools that prove Ethereum transactions with math, to focus fully on security from here.

He named three goals for formal verification. The first is proving that the mathematics behind the proofs matches the Ethereum spec exactly. The second is a hard maximum on prover cost for the amount of gas in a block. The third is the security of the proof system itself. Ethereum's roadmap leans more on zero-knowledge proofs to check blocks, so a proof that is fast but incorrect is dangerous.

Big congratulations to the @zksync airbender team for this milestone. At this point, I consider the battle for speed to be definitively won, and the top priority for zkEVMs should shift fully to security. To me that means formally verifying (i) equivalence of the arithmetization to the ethereum spec (ii) a hard maximum bound on (prover cost) / (amount of gas in block) (iii) security of the proof system itself https://t.co/cgtFXBpicf

A prover that costs too much for heavy blocks may also push smaller operators out, which hurts decentralization. Vitalik is calling on developers to close those gaps before the technology carries real weight.

The news comes at a weak time for the price. ETH trades near $2,365 on the daily chart, down about 15% from the late September high near $2,800. It fell through the blue and cyan averages around $2,490 and $2,550 and is now sitting at the orange average near $2,360. The black average near $2,305 is the next support, just below the recent low of $2,313.

Volume is steady but not strong, and the RSI is near 38, close to oversold. That indicates sellers have control, but a bounce could form if the orange and black averages hold. A move back above $2,490 would be the first sign of recovery.

Vitalik's message is not a short-term price trigger. Security work is slow, and traders are unlikely to react to it. Still, it sets a clear direction for Ethereum's technical road. If teams follow it, the network could end up with proofs that are fast, cheap, and trusted, which is what the roadmap needs. For now, the chart will decide the next move, and a break below $2,305 could put the larger recovery since August at risk.

Patrick Witt, the former executive director of the White House Crypto Council, has finally come forward and addressed the news of his exit from the current administration, saying he plans to stay focused on supporting US technological innovation in the private sector.

Witt offered a long-form statement on X, where he shared his thoughts about his stint in the administration, praised some high-level figures within the administration and showed his optimism about the future of the US crypto sector.

"It's been the privilege of a lifetime to serve in this administration. I've been the luckiest guy in the world for the last 2 years," Witt said in his post, describing his overall experience.

"I'm so grateful to have played a role in unleashing American innovation while in government, and I'm looking forward to continuing that mission in the private sector!" he said.

Witt noted the crypto-related policy achievements of the administration, especially the passage of the GENIUS Act and progress on the CLARITY Act.

In his statement, the former crypto chief expressed his gratitude to his former colleague David Sacks, who was the former AI and crypto czar at the White House, for his leadership and mentorship.

At the same time, he thanked SEC Chairman Paul Atkins, CFTC Chairman Brian Quintenz, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and some lawmakers for the support they have provided in shaping digital assets legislation.

According to Witt, the efforts of all these people have been vital to achieving Trump's vision of establishing the US as the world's top crypto hub.

"With regulators and elected officials like you, I feel at ease knowing that the future for digital asset innovation in America is very bright," he said.

The former official's exit comes at a particularly awkward time for the crypto policy of the administration.

In particular, the CLARITY Act, which aims to create an all-encompassing federal regulatory framework for digital assets, recently failed in the Senate.

NEAR trades close to $4.94 after a sharp rejection from the $6.00 level. Price spiked to that high on October 12, then reversed in a large red candle that erased most of the gain. A move like this, with a long upper wick, suggests that sellers were waiting at the top.

NEAR has more than tripled from its August base near $1.60, and every long average is rising. They now sit near $3.95, $3.60, $3.20 and $2.60. But this is also the problem. Price is far above all of them, so a deeper pullback would not necessarily break the trend. It would only bring price back to more normal levels.

The first support is the short-term average near $4.65. Below it, the October 8 low near $4.30 is the next line, followed by the $4.00 area. A daily close below $4.30 would suggest that the sideways range held since late September is breaking, and $4.00 would come into view.

On the upside, $5.20 is the first hurdle, where recent candles failed. Above it, $5.60 capped several rallies in late September and early October, and $6.00 is the high set on October 12.

XRP trades near $1.346 and is resting at the orange moving average around $1.34, the only line that has kept it from a deeper fall. The coin dropped from approximately $1.66 in late September, a loss of about 19%, and the past couple of daily candles show buyers defending this level with small lower wicks near $1.31.

Above the price, the picture is crowded. The black average near $1.38 and the blue one near $1.39 sit just overhead, with the cyan line near $1.42 above them. XRP lost all of these in early October, so they now act as a wall of resistance. Today's high of $1.385 ran straight into that area and was sold, which fits the weak mood. The market needs a daily close above $1.39 to begin changing that.

Volume tells the same story. Trading has declined gradually since the larger moves in August and September, and the recent red candles are not heavy, so sellers are not rushing either. That is why the price is moving sideways.

Zcash is trading near $1,199 after a sharp pullback from the late-September high near $1,700. That is a drop of approximately 30% in under three weeks, and the coin now sits right on an important line. The blue moving average near $1,190 has held the price twice in the past week, with buyers pushing it back up from lows around $1,115 and $1,120.

The bounces were weak, though. Each attempt to move higher has stalled under the cyan and green averages near $1,230 and $1,285. Today's candle opened at $1,218 and is already back under them, which suggests sellers still step in on every small rise. Volume has also dried up compared with the rally days in September, so there is little buying strength behind these attempts. The daily RSI is around 45, a neutral reading that suggests momentum has cooled but the coin is not oversold.

What matters now is whether $1,190 continues to hold. If it does, ZEC can build a base and try to reclaim $1,285. A daily close above that level would be the first real sign that the drop is over. A move back toward $1,350 could then be realistic, since that area held the price in early October.

If the blue line breaks, the chart offers little nearby protection. The next support is the orange average around $990, which is about 17% below the current price. Under that, the long black average near $765 marks where the rally began to accelerate. A fall that deep is not the base case, but the empty space on the chart suggests how fast it could happen.

The bigger picture remains positive. ZEC more than doubled from about $500 in August, and the longer averages keep rising far below the price. A cooldown after a run like this is normal. For now, the coin sits at a decision point with falling volume, and a clear move in either direction is likely soon.

Chainlink trades close to $12.46, down approximately 21% from its late-September high close to $15.75. The drop was accompanied by a sharp spike on heavy volume, a pattern that often marks a short-term top. Since then, every bounce has been weaker than the last, and price has made lower highs near $14.30, $13.50 and $13.10. LINK now sits on its short-term moving averages, which run right at $12.45. These lines carried the uptrend through September, and buyers have defended them twice this month.

Wicks down to $12.05 on October 8 and $12.20 this week show that dip buyers are still active. But the bounces are small, and today's red candle is pressing on the line again.

Volume is the weak spot. Trading activity has dropped well below the levels seen during the September rally, which means few investors are willing to push price in either direction. Low volume near support can end with a sharp break, so the $12.05 area matters.

A daily close below it would open the way to the orange average near $11.40, and then the 200-day average near $10.85, which is close to the mid-September low of $10.60.

On the upside, LINK needs to reclaim $13.10, where a faster average now acts as resistance. A close above it could turn the bounce into a real recovery, with $13.50 and $14.00 as the next targets. Reaching $15.75 again would require a strong return of volume, and that looks unlikely in the near term.

The bigger picture is still positive. LINK is up approximately 50% from its August base near $8.20, and all the long averages point up. This looks more like a cooling phase than a trend reversal. Still, price is at a decision point, and the next strong daily close should show which side wins. Bulls need to hold $12.05 to keep the uptrend safe.

#386. China Seeks to Confiscate Billions in BTC, XRP, DOGE, BCH, BTG and BSV

Chinese authorities are seeking to confiscate approximately $5 billion worth of Bitcoin (BTC), alongside millions of XRP and Dogecoin (DOGE) tokens, in connection with one of the largest cryptocurrency fraud cases in history.

According to an October 14 report by Chinese media outlet The Paper, the Tianjin No. 2 Intermediate People's Court has accepted a confiscation application involving crypto assets seized from convicted money launderer Qian Zhimin.

The court announced on October 13 that it had formally accepted the application on September 28. Chinese prosecutors are seeking to recover 61,896.41552945 BTC, worth roughly $5 billion at recent market prices, alongside several other cryptocurrencies.

The application also covers cash denominated in U.S. dollars, euros and British pounds, as well as jewelry, bank deposits and investment portfolios.

Notably, the DOGE holdings have reportedly already been converted into cash by British judicial authorities and deposited into an interest-bearing account.

The confiscation proceedings stem from a massive investment fraud scheme allegedly orchestrated by Qian through Tianjin Lantian Gerui Electronic Technology.

Between April 2014 and August 2017, the company illegally raised approximately 40.38 billion yuan (roughly $6 billion) by selling fraudulent investment products that promised substantial returns.

According to Chinese prosecutors, the scheme affected more than 102,000 investors, who suffered combined losses of approximately 19.98 billion yuan.

Much of the money was used to repay existing investors, operate fraudulent investment projects and purchase assets, including Bitcoin, real estate, vehicles and jewelry.

Qian fled China in 2017, eventually arriving in the United Kingdom, where British authorities subsequently seized her cryptocurrency holdings.

In November 2025, she was sentenced to 11 years and eight months in prison by a British court for money laundering offenses.

The latest development comes as British courts are also considering the legal ownership of the massive Bitcoin fortune.

On Oct. 12, the UK's High Court ruled that Chinese law should govern claims made by victims seeking to recover the seized cryptocurrency.

The decision could have major implications for whether investors are entitled to the original value of their losses or potentially benefit from Bitcoin's substantial appreciation since the fraud took place.

However, the British ruling does not establish final ownership of the assets. Further proceedings will determine whether the victims can demonstrate enforceable rights to the cryptocurrency.

Meanwhile, the Chinese court has opened a six-month period during which Qian's relatives and other interested parties, including affected investors, can participate in the confiscation proceedings.

#387. Ripple Makes Big Move Into Global Investment Infrastructure

Ripple, a payments company using blockchain technology, is set for a huge partnership with DriveWealth, a global brokerage infrastructure provider, which is expected to usher in blockchain-based payments, stablecoin settlements, and digital asset custody to traditional financial markets.

As per the announcement, both companies are set to integrate a number of Ripple's institutional products with the global investment infrastructure of DriveWealth.

DriveWealth is a brokerage-as-a-service provider that powers the investing and trading services for over 100 partners globally, ranging from fintechs, digital wallets, and financial institutions providing access to U.S. stock markets.

Through this new partnership, Ripple's exposure in the traditional financial space may take a massive leap forward by offering a global footprint of investment platforms access to Ripple's blockchain-based infrastructure.

One of the major aspects of this partnership is the integration of a U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin (RLUSD) for institutional settlements.

DriveWealth will first roll out institutional settlements using RLUSD on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) in Europe before making its way to the U.S. as well.

Ripple's stablecoin minting and burning features will be used for this integration.

The objective here is to enable institutional customers to fund and manage their collateral accounts with stablecoins, which can easily be exchanged for traditional currency in close to real time.

This will help them minimize their dependence on traditional bank transfers, which might take a much longer time to complete, especially if the money is being transferred overseas.

There's a disconnect between U.S. equities settlement, which is cyclical, and cross-border money transfer, which could take a lot more time to complete.

With stablecoins, DriveWealth aims to enable faster capital availability so that clients can fund their trading operations without relying on bank wires.

Apart from payments and stablecoin settlement, this partnership could also offer Ripple's expanding prime brokerage business new avenues.

DriveWealth and Ripple Prime are looking into equity financing opportunities that Ripple Prime's Delta One can offer.

#390. Stellar (XLM) Lands Chainlink to Wake Up $3.5 Billion in Tokenized Real-World Assets

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. The Stellar blockchain has officially launched the Chainlink Data Feeds and Data Streams oracle infrastructure on its mainnet. The key element of the deal is purely commercial: the Stellar Development Foundation has fully taken over the operating costs of running the oracles under the Chainlink Scale program.

This decision opens external markets to a giant ecosystem of tokenized real-world assets (RWA) worth $3.54 billion, which until today had remained effectively isolated.

.@Chainlink Data Feeds and Data Streams are now live on Stellar. The integration adds new capabilities for builders, helping to put more assets to work across DeFi applications for lending, trading, stablecoins, tokenized equities, and more. https://t.co/7uuH8e6pG6

According to the latest data from the analytics tracker RWA.xyz, Stellar ranks fourth in the world among all blockchain platforms by RWA volume, trailing only Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Solana.

However, the structure of this capital is specific. It consists exclusively of conservative reserves held by major players, distributed across strictly regulated sectors.

The ecosystem's landscape is defined by the European fintech sector, led by the Spiko platform, which digitized Amundi's interbank swaps in euros, pounds, and francs, as well as Eurozone treasury bills. The American wing is represented by the public sector: secure Ondo Finance products based on US government bonds and the flagship money market fund from the investment giant Franklin Templeton.

Infrastructure liquidity is provided by Circle's regulated dollar stablecoin USDC and Figure's American stablecoin YLDS, registered with the SEC.

The thing is, the Soroban smart contracts within Stellar were completely cut off from the outside world. The network held colossal reserves of highly liquid and legitimate assets but could not build a full-fledged financial turnover around them.

They physically could not verify the exact value of these instruments in real time. Billions of dollars sat on the blockchain passively, serving as digital warehouse receipts.

It was impossible to launch even basic instruments against them. For example, it was impossible to use tokenized Ondo bonds as collateral to automatically receive stablecoins, since the system could not instantly calculate the liquidation value of the collateral at the slightest market fluctuation.

The Chainlink integration fully removes this technical barrier. Low-latency data streams deliver market quotes to Stellar smart contracts with virtually no delay.

This enables full-fledged automated lending with per-second recalculation of the collateral ratio, allows safe liquidations of large players' positions without the risk of systemic failures, and also creates a foundation for prediction markets and perpetual futures on tokenized stocks.

Since the volume of RWA transfers on Stellar grew by a quarter over the past month, and stablecoin capitalization rose by 10%, the foundation's decision to subsidize the integration looks like a pragmatic, preemptive commercial move.

By lifting the financial burden from developers, Stellar is trying to wrest the status of the main platform for structured DeFi from the market leaders, turning passive billion-dollar reserves into dynamic working capital.

Shiba Inu has completed a death cross signal on its 4-hour chart, the first occurrence of such a signal on this timeframe in October. The MA 50 has fallen below the MA 200 on the 4-hour chart, a death cross.

This comes against the backdrop of a tough run for SHIB, whose price fell for a third day in a row to trade below $0.000005. Similar bearish crossovers have appeared on other short-term timeframes since October's start, including the hourly, 2-hour, and 3-hour charts, as SHIB struggled to maintain its upward momentum.

At the time of writing, SHIB was significantly down on a 24-hour basis as the markets reacted sharply to hotter-than-expected CPI data.

Consumer prices increased again, keeping the inflation rate well above the Federal Reserve's goal. The consumer price index rose a seasonally adjusted 0.6% for the month, putting the 12-month rate at 3.7%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Wednesday.

Fed officials responded in September by approving their first interest rate hike in more than three years, a quarter-percentage-point move that took the benchmark funds rate to a target range of 3.75%–4%. Markets expect the Fed to skip an October increase but to hike again in December.

At the time of writing, SHIB was down 3.88% in the last 24 hours to $0.000005015 amid a weeklong selloff and is down 6.66% over the past seven days.

The recent selloff has brought SHIB beneath its moving averages, supporting the bearish short-term setup. If SHIB continues to trade below important support levels, sellers could continue to have the upper hand, potentially exposing it to lower levels; in this case, the $0.000004 level.

However, the crossover alone would not confirm a deeper correction. Traders would also need to watch for price action, trading volume, and whether buyers defend nearby support, which could see SHIB back above $0.000005 and then $0.000006.

Alternatively, SHIB could continue to range trade as the short-term bearish signals enter a tug of war with the earlier bullish daily-chart crossover.

#392. Bitcoin Hashrate Stabilizes After Sudden Plunge

The hashrate of the Bitcoin (BTC) network seems to have stabilized after a major fall, which led miners to downscale their operations due to declining profitability, rising electricity prices, and competition from artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

As per the four-year Bitcoin hashrate chart presented by Zach Pandl, Bitcoin's network computing power reached more than 1.1 zettahashes per second (ZH/s) in late 2025. Then, the network saw a significant course correction in 2026.

The hashrate has now started recovering to the psychologically important level of 1 ZH/s. As per the YCharts data collated by Blockchain.com, on Oct. 13, the Bitcoin hashrate is around 1.075 ZH/s. This is in comparison to the previous day's 1.003 ZH/s.

However, this hashrate level is still lower than a year ago.

Declining profitability for Bitcoin mining has been among the major reasons for the drop, especially after the significant correction in Bitcoin's price following the October 2025 high.

As per a mining report by CoinShares, Bitcoin's hashrate fell from roughly 1,160 exahashes per second (EH/s) in October 2025 to 850 EH/s in early February 2026 (a nearly 27% plunge).

The decreasing price of cryptocurrency, coupled with high mining difficulty and relatively low transaction fee income, led to a major dip in miners' earnings.

In June, the hash price for Bitcoin, which represents miner earnings per unit of computing power, fell to a record monthly average low of $27.70 per petahash per second per day.

This meant that several operators with older mining hardware were struggling to meet their operational costs.

Rising electricity prices also contributed to the decline. As per CoinShares, this includes increasing power rates in Texas, temporary power curtailments, and winter-related events that forced some mining operations to reduce their output.

The cryptocurrency market is emerging from the consolidation phase right now following the release of critically important macroeconomic data from the US. The September Consumer Price Index (CPI) showed accelerating inflation across all components: the annual figure rose to +3.7% (+3.6% expected), while the underlying Core CPI climbed to +2.6% y/y, provoking a harsh reaction in financial markets.

The release of "hot" data triggered an instant jump in US Treasury yields, a +2.55% rise in the VIX volatility index, and a -1.10% drop in gold. Traders across all markets are urgently reassessing risks in light of the return of inflationary pressure on the eve of the Fed meeting.

The local support for spot prices, recorded in the morning reports on US ETFs for October 13, has been completely offset by the reaction to the inflation shock. On the eve of the release, Bitcoin funds attracted $175.62 million (mainly through Fidelity FBTC — $103 million and BlackRock IBIT — $66 million), while Ether ETFs added $24.80 million, ending a ten-day streak of outflows as per SoSoValue.

Despite this reversal, the overall five-day net trend at the start of October remained negative (minus $600 million), which predetermined the buyers' vulnerability to the release of the statistics.

Investors' focus is now shifting to assessing the Fed's hawkish inflation scenario. In parallel, the market is digesting major infrastructure shifts in the UAE, where Standard Chartered is opening retail trading of Bitcoin and Ether, as well as the morning news block on the Evernorth listing on Nasdaq and the integration of AI agents into the XRP Ledger.

The financial conglomerate Standard Chartered is opening direct trading of Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) for wealthy private clients in the UAE through existing bank accounts. This is the first such service from an international bank in this jurisdiction.

The release is part of the SC Ventures strategy, which previously invested in the operators Zodia Custody, Zodia Markets, and the Libeara platform. In July 2025, the bank launched institutional spot trading of BTC/ETH in the UK; in September 2026, it expanded it to the UAE corporate sector, and has now scaled the solution to the retail premium segment.

The launch of the retail line was preceded by the deployment of custody infrastructure based on the XRP Ledger (XRPL). On October 12, the Standard Chartered branch in DIFC (Dubai) launched institutional custody for Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin.

Together with Ripple and LMAX Group, the bank is implementing a collateral-mirroring setup. The scheme allows RLUSD to be used as trading collateral in real time while keeping the assets within Standard Chartered's custody perimeter.

The bank's management emphasizes that the integration is focused exclusively on the ledger's stablecoins and does not involve trading or holding the native XRP token on the balance sheet.

At this hour, the treasury company Evernorth Holdings is preparing for the closing bell ceremony on Nasdaq at 16:00 New York time. The event is timed to the listing of shares under the ticker XRPN, whose trading began on October 12 following the SPAC deal with Armada.

#395. Binance to Delist Two Cryptocurrencies in October

As part of its commitment to ensuring the safety of its users, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, has announced plans to remove some tokens from its wide list of crypto assets.

In a recent announcement shared earlier today, the exchange announced that it will delist Epic Chain (EPIC) and QuickSwap (QUICK) following its latest review of the two cryptocurrencies.

According to the announcement, Binance revealed that it will stop spot trading for all trading pairs involving both EPIC and QUICK on October 28, 2026.

Once trading ends on the stated date, the exchange has warned that it will automatically cancel all outstanding orders for the affected pairs.

While this is not the first time Binance has announced the removal of an asset from its exchange, it explained that it regularly reviews listed cryptocurrencies to ensure they continue to meet its standards and ensure safety for users.

As such, the move comes as a regular practice for Binance after it carefully observed the supply dynamics, regulatory compliance, liquidity, and other major factors regarding the cryptocurrencies.

Although Binance has stated some of the reasons behind its frequent decisions to remove certain assets from its trading platform, the exchange did not specify which particular factors led to the decision to delist EPIC and QUICK.

Nonetheless, the exchange has mentioned that it will also halt several other Binance services supporting EPIC and QUICK by the end of the month, urging traders to start removing their assets before the specified date.

Shiba Inu is trading near $0.00000517, and the chart indicates a market that has gone quiet. Trading volume in recent sessions is tiny compared with the spikes seen in late July, August and September. When volume fades like this, price moves lose strength, and neither buyers nor sellers show real control.

SHIB peaked near $0.00000627 in late September, but it could not hold above the long black moving average near $0.00000563. Since then, it has slipped below the blue and orange averages, which sit near $0.00000541 and $0.00000529. Both now act as resistance. The daily RSI is around 40, which indicates weak momentum but not an oversold market, so a bounce is not guaranteed.

Price dipped to approximately $0.00000502 in recent days and buyers stepped in, so the $0.00000500 area is the line to hold. A break below it could open the way toward the September low near $0.00000475. A recovery above $0.00000530 would be the first sign that sellers are tiring.

On-chain data presents mixed signals. Exchange reserves are approximately 87.1 trillion SHIB, down 0.11% on the day, and netflow is negative at approximately 98.9 billion SHIB. That means more coins left exchanges than came in, which is usually a sign that holders are not rushing to sell. But the picture is not entirely positive. The seven-day average of coins leaving exchanges fell 42%, while the average inflow fell 14%. Fewer coins are moving in either direction, which fits the low volume on the chart.

Network activity is flat too. Transactions sit near 4,800 and transfers near 3,700, both up less than 1% on the day. The value of coins held on exchanges is approximately $447.7 million, down 0.69%. The burned supply metric shows no data, so burns provide no clear support for the price right now.

For now, SHIB is stuck below resistance with thin trading and no push from either side. A move on rising volume is needed to end the uncertainty. Until that appears, the price direction remains unclear, and a retest of $0.00000500 is possible.
